title: feat(messages): draw SPIP1 pixel-image messages as images
body:
## Summary

Adds support for [SPIP1 (Small Packet Image Protocol 1.0)](https://github.com/lilyellowtags/spip-editor), a way to send a tiny pixel image in one text message. A message like `8:zyyzzyyzyaayyaayyaaaaaayzyaaaayzzzyaayzzzzzyyzzz` now shows as a red heart instead of a string of letters.

![SPIP images in a channel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maxhayim/meshmonitor/ca5a5efaefd4f3e6d18b3bec978c9d6ab06068fb/docs/public/images/features/spip-images.png)


- `src/utils/spip.ts`: decoder and the 35-colour palette from the spec.
- `src/components/Spip/SpipImage.tsx`: draws the image as an SVG, one unit per pixel, with crisp edges and a fixed width. The raw code is the hover title and the aria-label.
- Hooked into `renderMessageWithLinks` (Meshtastic channels and DMs, the unified messages page) and the MeshCore `renderMessageText` (SPIP was designed with MeshCore in mind).
- Docs: `docs/features/spip-images.md` with a screenshot, plus a sidebar entry.

### Detection

To keep normal chat from turning into images, a message is drawn only when:
- the whole message (trimmed) is the code;
- it has 2–32 columns and at least 2 rows;
- the pixels fill whole rows, up to 1,024;
- every character is `a–z` or `1–9`, case ignored (`0` is reserved).

So `12:30`, `John 3:16`, `4:abcd` (one row) and `3:abcde` (partial row) all stay as text.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:** none. This only changes how messages that were already received are shown. It sends nothing and makes no requests.
2. **Spam:** no new sends, events, notifications or automations.
3. **Timers:** none.

## Testing

- New tests: `src/utils/spip.test.ts` (decoding, the spec examples, false-positive cases) and `src/components/Spip/SpipImage.test.tsx` (rect layout, plus the `renderMessageWithLinks` integration).
- Full Vitest suite: 2158 files passed, 0 failed (PG/MySQL suites skipped, as there were no local containers; this PR has no DB changes).
- `npm run lint:ci` passes; `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- Screenshot: the real `renderMessageWithLinks` output in the real message-bubble markup with the app's stylesheets (mocha theme), on a throwaway Vite page. I didn't capture it from a running instance with a radio attached.

title: fix(meshcore): return empty channel info within advertised capacity
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5933.

- Return an empty, zero-filled 50-byte `ChannelInfo` for unconfigured slots below the capacity advertised in `DeviceInfo`, matching real companion firmware and allowing pipelined channel reads to complete.
- Share the capacity calculation between `DeviceInfo` and `GetChannel`, including real-device capacity, stock/highest-slot fallback, and the wire-byte clamp.
- Preserve configured-channel responses, out-of-capacity `NotFound` errors, source scoping, and the database-failure path. No additional LoRa traffic, timers, or notifications.

## Tests

TCP-level regression coverage exercises empty and configured slots, pipelined reads, capacity boundaries and fallback cases, source-scoped queries, and DB failures. Seven regression cases failed before the fix.

Validation recorded for this exact commit during preparation:
- Application TypeScript check passed with a 4 GiB Node heap; the default 2 GiB invocation exhausted its heap.
- Changed-file lint and `npm run lint:ci` passed. Full lint retains 2,351 repository baseline problems.
- Focused tests: 261 passed.
- Full Vitest: 32,485 passed, 1,765 skipped, 21 todo, zero failures.
- Production Vite build, server TypeScript compilation, and diff checks passed.

Immediately before opening this PR, reran `npx vitest run src/server/meshcoreVirtualNodeServer.test.ts`: **199/199 passed**. The reviewed commit is unchanged.

## Limitations

- Optional `typecheck:tests` is not green: repository-wide declaration/DOM-matcher diagnostics include two on unchanged lines in this test file; no diagnostics point to added lines. The attempted baseline comparison timed out.
- PostgreSQL/MySQL-dependent tests remain skipped.
- Physical-device validation in MeshCore One, the official app, and meshcore-flutter has not been performed. Local TCP wire-level checks pass; hardware/client confirmation remains outstanding.

title: feat(nodes): set, clear and lock a node's channel by hand (#5923)
body:
Follow-up to #5926 (#5923).

## Why
`nodes.channel` decides which channel-scoped viewers can see a node. #5926 stopped recording it from evidence that isn't the node's own key-decoded traffic. Rows written before that fix can still name a private channel the node has no key for. This adds a way to correct them by hand, and to keep them corrected.

## Decisions (from the maintainer)
- **Permission:** `nodes:write` on the source (same gate as notes, position override and hide-from-map).
- **Channel Lock:** a new `nodes.channelLocked` column. Every existing row starts unlocked. While a channel is locked, traffic does not change it.
- **Per-node only:** no bulk clear.

## Changes
- **Migration 217** adds `nodes.channelLocked` (SQLite INTEGER 0, PG BOOLEAN false, MySQL TINYINT(1) 0). It is idempotent through the shared helpers.
- **`NodesRepository.upsertNode`** keeps the stored channel when `channelLocked` is set. Every packet path (Meshtastic, MQTT, VN, NodeInfo) writes through this one method. The new `setNodeChannel()` is the only writer while locked.
- **Route:** `POST /api/nodes/:nodeId/channel` with `{ sourceId, channel: number | null, locked: boolean }`, using `ok`/`fail` envelopes.
  - `requirePermission('nodes','write',{ sourceIdFrom: 'body' })`.
  - Returns 404 `NODE_NOT_FOUND` when the node has no row on that source.
- **UI:** the node details Channel card has an Edit button for users with `nodes:write` (new `NodeChannelEditor` + CSS module).
  - The picker offers None plus the source's channels, and the stored channel if the source no longer lists it.
  - A Lock checkbox, with a hint that an unlocked channel is re-learned from the next key-decoded packet.
  - A Locked badge shows when the channel is locked.
  - Saving refreshes the per-source poll.
- **Mappers / cache:** `channelLocked` flows through `dbNodeMapper`, `nodeDbMaintenanceService`, `nodeCacheService` and the `DeviceInfo` types.
- **Node identity merge** carries a locked channel to a survivor that has none, like notes and a locked favourite.
- The hand-written PG/MySQL `nodes` DDL in the five node repo test files gains the column.

## Mesh impact
None. MeshMonitor-local data only. No packets, timers or notifications.

## Tests
- Route (`createRouteTestApp`): clear then re-learn while unlocked; a locked set and a locked clear both survive traffic; unlock resumes learning; `nodes:write` on another source is refused (403); the other source's row is untouched; bad input and unknown node are rejected.
- Migration 217 on SQLite / PG / MySQL, including idempotency.
- Node identity merge carries a locked channel across.
- `NodeChannelEditor` (7 tests).
- **Full suite with the PG and MySQL containers up:** 34,147 passed. The one failure was the new merge test, which the run picked up before the merge change was saved. Run alone, both merge suites pass (36 tests, including PG/MySQL).
- `tsc` (client and server) and `lint:ci` are clean.
- **Dev container:** migration 217 ran. On BOCA G2 t

title: test(i18n): treat Weblate's empty-string keys as untranslated
body:
Unblocks #5929.

## Problem
Weblate now writes every untranslated key into each locale as `""` (about 30k lines across 12 files in #5929). Two tests failed on it:
- `AutomationFormLayout.cosmeticI18n.test.ts` required `auto_responder.channels_label` / `multiline_label` to be **absent** from de.json.
- `AutomationFormLayout.placeholderHint.test.ts` required `auto_responder.trigger_placeholder` to be non-empty when present.

## Fix
`src/config/i18n.ts` sets `returnEmptyString: false`, so i18next reads `""` as missing and falls back to English, the same as an absent key. Both tests now accept `""`. Each also asserts `returnEmptyString: false`, so the shortcut fails loudly if that setting ever changes.

## Tests
Both files pass (42 tests) against main's locales **and** against #5929's locales.

**Mesh impact:** none (tests only).

title: fix(meshcore): split the Nodes list header into two rows (#5936)
body:
Closes #5936

## Change
The MeshCore Nodes list pane is a fixed 320px with `overflow: hidden`, and its header held the collapse button, title, count, age filter, Import, Discover and the sort controls on one row. With a 3-digit node count, Discover was clipped.

The header now has two rows:
- **Top:** collapse, "Nodes", count, then Import and Discover on the right.
- **Bottom:** the age filter and the sort select and direction button.

The Discover menu now opens leftwards (`right: 0`), because Discover sits at the pane's right edge and a left-anchored menu would also be clipped.

Styling lives in a new `MeshCoreNodesView.module.css`. It overrides the global `.sort-controls` wrap and top margin (#5420) and the `.sort-dropdown` min-width only inside this header, so other views are unchanged.

## Verification
- Dev container (279 nodes): every header control and the open Discover menu stay inside the pane (right edge ≤ 361px within a 56–376px pane).
- New test: title, Import and Discover sit on row 1; filter and sort sit on row 2. `MeshCoreNodesView.test.tsx` passes. MeshCore component suites pass (1263 tests).
- `tsc --noEmit` and `lint:ci` are clean.

**Mesh impact:** none (layout only).

title: feat(automation): one Auto-Responder trigger syntax for Meshtastic and MeshCore (#5924)
body:
Closes #5924

## Decisions

- **Per-trigger syntax mode on both sides.** Every Auto-Responder trigger, Meshtastic and MeshCore, has an optional `syntax`: `'pattern'` (the Meshtastic placeholder DSL) or `'regex'` (bare, unanchored, case-insensitive). Both modes work on both source types.
- **Back-compat is a read-time default, not a migration.** A trigger with no `syntax` reads as its old behaviour: Meshtastic = `'pattern'`, MeshCore = `'regex'` (`resolveResponderSyntax`). No stored data is rewritten. A migration would have to parse two JSON settings per source on three backends to add a field that has a safe default anyway.
- **New triggers default to `'pattern'`** on both UIs.
- **One matcher.** `src/utils/responderTrigger.ts` holds the parsing, splitting, checks and param extraction with no regex engine. The server passes RE2 (`matchResponderTrigger` in `src/server/utils/autoResponderMatcher.ts`, called by both managers). The browser passes the native engine shaped like RE2 (`src/utils/responderTriggerNative.ts`). The UI preview therefore runs the same code as the server.
- **Charset: any printable Unicode.** Letters, marks (incl. U+FE0E/FE0F), numbers, punctuation, symbols, spaces, tab/CR/LF, ZWJ, ZWNJ (Persian / Indic text) and tag characters (subdivision flags). Control characters, other format characters (e.g. bidi overrides), line/paragraph separators, private-use and unassigned code points are refused. The 100-char cap and the ReDoS shape check stay. RE2 always runs in Unicode mode (it reports flags `iu`), so emoji in classes match whole code points.
- **Where the checks apply.** Regex mode: length cap, charset, ReDoS shape at save time and at match time (as MeshCore always did). Pattern mode: per-alternative 100-char cap (the Meshtastic UI already had it), charset and "must compile" at save time in both UIs and on the MeshCore save route; the Meshtastic settings route leaves pattern-mode triggers as it always did. At match time pattern mode checks only "must compile", so a stored Meshtastic trigger that predates the checks keeps matching.
- **Named groups (optional item): done.** In regex mode `(?<name>…)` supplies params on both sides. RE2 and the browser engine both support it cleanly.
- **MeshCore pattern mode gets full parity:** comma alternatives, anchoring, homoglyph normalisation, `{name}` / `{name:regex}` params. Params fill the text reply the same way Meshtastic does (substituted before token expansion) and reach a script as `PARAM_<name>`, as on Meshtastic.

## Changes

Server
- `src/utils/responderTrigger.ts` (new): engine-free core. `ResponderSyntax`, `resolveResponderSyntax`, `PRINTABLE_CHARSET_RE`, `DANGEROUS_SHAPE_RE`, `parsePatternDsl` (the DSL expansion moved here unchanged), `compileResponderTrigger`, `runResponderTrigger`, `substituteResponderParams`.
- `src/server/utils/autoResponderMatcher.ts`: `matchResponderTrigger`, `compileResponderTriggerRe2`, `matchCompiledResponderTrigger`, `validateResponderTrigger`. `matchAu

title: fix(virtual-node): prefer MQTT proxy client as proxy delegate (#5927)
body:
Fixes #5927

`broadcastToProxyDelegate()` picked the newest writable client, so a non-proxy client that connected after the MQTT proxy sidecar received the `FromRadio.mqttClientProxyMessage` frames and uplink silently stopped.

It now prefers writable clients with `sentMqttProxy === true` (newest among them). It falls back to the newest writable client overall when none has identified as a proxy yet.

title: fix(nodes): record a node's channel only from its own key-decoded traffic (#5923)
body:
Closes #5923

## Root cause

`nodes.channel` is the only per-node channel record. The channel node list (`NodesTab`, `useProcessedNodes`, `useSourceView`) and the node details page (`NodeDetailsBlock`) both read it. On a TCP source, two places write it:

1. `processMeshPacket` in `src/server/meshtasticManager.ts`, from **every** packet with `decryptedBy === 'node'` (since #2208).
2. `processNodeInfoProtobuf`, which seeds it from the device NodeDB only when the row has none.

Write path 1 treated "the radio handed us a decoded packet" as "this sender used that channel's key". Firmware 2.8.1 (`v2.8.1.8e6a88d`) breaks that rule in several ways:

| Packet | What `channel` holds | Firmware source |
|---|---|---|
| PKI DM / PKI ACK | always 0: `chIndex` starts at 0 and `p->channel = chIndex` runs after a PKI decrypt | `src/mesh/Router.cpp` L954, L1019, L1099 |
| 2.8 NodeDB replay (position/telemetry) | `header->channel`, the NodeDB value, not a reception | `src/mesh/PhoneAPI.cpp` L1306, L1333, L1445, L1513 |
| TrafficManagement cached NodeInfo reply | `from = p->to` (the target), `channel = p->channel` (the **request's** channel), hops 0/0. A relay with the private key answers on the private channel for a node that has no key. | `src/modules/TrafficManagementModule.cpp` L1568-L1575 |
| Virtual Node MQTT-proxy envelope | the uplinking gateway's slot or a hash. Our radio never saw it. | `src/server/virtualNodeServer.ts` |

Any of these can stamp a node that lacks the key onto a private slot. If the private channel is slot 0, every PKI packet does it.

## Fix

- New `src/server/utils/nodeChannelEvidence.ts`: `channelIndexFromPacket()` returns a channel index only for a node-decoded packet with an in-range index (0..`MAX_CHANNEL_INDEX`). It returns nothing for PKI packets, firmware replays (reuses `isFirmwareReplayPacket`), spoofed zero-hop packets, and MQTT-proxy packets. A spoofed zero-hop packet has `hop_start == hop_limit == 0` and a `relay_node` byte that is not the sender's. `Router::send` stamps the transmitter's own byte (`Router.cpp` L525).
- `processMeshPacket` uses the helper. The virtual node MQTT-proxy path passes a new `ProcessingContext.fromMqttProxy` flag.
- Per-source scoping is unchanged: the same `upsertNode` call carries the same `sourceId`.

## Mesh impact

None. The change sends no packets, adds no timers and fires no notifications. It only decides whether an existing DB write includes `channel`.

## Data cleanup

The fix stops new wrong writes. It does **not** rewrite rows that are already wrong. A wrong row corrects itself when the node next sends channel traffic our radio decrypts. A node that never does keeps its stale value. This PR has no migration. A cleanup is a policy call, so it is left for review:

1. Leave as is (self-heals for active nodes).
2. Add an admin action that clears `channel` for chosen nodes on a source.
3. Run a migration that sets `channel = NULL` for all nodes. This also erases correct values and makes DMs f

title: feat(waypoints): round-trip firmware waypoint geofence fields (#5922)
body:
Closes #5922

## What
Firmware's `Waypoint` carries a geofence in fields 9-13:
- `geofence_radius`
- `bounding_box`
- `notify_on_enter`, `notify_on_exit`, `notify_favorites_only`

MeshMonitor dropped these on ingest. A waypoint made in the Apple or Android app lost its geofence here, and any rebroadcast or edit from MeshMonitor stripped it from the mesh. This PR stores the fields, sends them, and adds editor and map UI.

Maintainer decisions:
- Round-trip plus UI only; no alerts raised by MeshMonitor itself.
- Radius limited to 160 m-16 km, Apple's range.
- Box drawn on a mini-map, with editable N/S/E/W fields.

## Changes
- **Migration 216** adds these columns on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL:
  - `geofence_radius_m`
  - `bbox_west/south/east/north`
  - `notify_on_enter/exit/favorites_only`

  Existing rows get no geofence and every flag off.
- **Ingest:** `upsertFromMesh` stores the fields. A waypoint packet is the whole waypoint, so a sender with no geofence clears ours.
- **Broadcast:** create, edit and the rebroadcast scheduler all build the packet with `toWireWaypoint()`, which includes the geofence.
  - A waypoint without a geofence encodes byte-for-byte as before (tested).
  - Automation-owned waypoints are unchanged.
- **API:** `geofence_radius_m` (an integer from 160 to 16000, or null), `bounding_box` (`{west,south,east,north}` with west < east and south < north, or null), and the three booleans. A bad value returns 400 `INVALID_GEOFENCE`. PATCH changes only the keys it is sent.
- **Editor:** a Geofence section with:
  - a shape picker (none / circle / rectangle, plus "both" when an incoming waypoint has both)
  - the radius, shown in km and mi
  - the box, drawn on the existing `BBoxMapEditor` and centred on the waypoint, with N/S/E/W fields
  - the enter / exit / favourites-only toggles
  - a warning next to the toggles
- **Map:** the region is drawn dashed under the pin and can't be clicked, so it never takes a click meant for a node. It uses a `--color-info` token. The pin popup gets a summary line.
- The pure helpers are in `waypointGeofence.ts`, so the route, the service and the protobuf encoder share them.

title: fix(config): refetch channels after Reload Config on Device (#5919)
body:
Closes #5919

## Root cause

The server stores the new channel name. The page does not show it until the next poll.

1. **Reload Config on Device** (`handleReloadConfig` in `src/components/ConfigurationTab.tsx`) calls `POST /api/nodes/refresh` (`nodesRoutes.ts`). That calls `refreshNodeDatabase()` (`nodeDbMaintenanceService.ts`), which sends `want_config_id = 0xFFFFFFFF`. The node replays all 8 channel slots, and `processChannelProtobuf` saves each one through `channels.upsertChannel(..., this.sourceId)`. A slot stored as "Channel 4" / DISABLED that now arrives as "Custom" / SECONDARY gets the new name, role and PSK. The `hasValidConfig` gate does not skip it: protobuf.js decodes an elided name to `''` and an elided role to `0`, so even an empty slot passes the gate. I checked this by decoding real `FromRadio` bytes.
2. The channel list on the Configuration tab comes from the **poll cache** (`useChannels()` → `usePoll()`). While the WebSocket is up, that cache refetches only every **30 s** (`WEBSOCKET_POLL_INTERVAL`). The server never pushes a channel change: `dataEventEmitter.emitChannelUpdate` has no callers.
3. `handleReloadConfig` waits 2 s and then refetches `/api/config/current`. That covers device and module config only. It never refetched channels, so the stale name stayed until the next 30 s poll. That matches the "about 20 s later it fixed itself" report. No live channel read happened. That was just the next poll.

### Firmware 2.8.1
I compared `PhoneAPI.cpp` at `v2.7.15.567b8ea` and `v2.8.1.8e6a88d`. `STATE_SEND_CHANNELS` still sends all `MAX_NUM_CHANNELS` slots on every `want_config_id`. 2.8.1 sends blank channels only on lockdown builds (`MESHTASTIC_PHONEAPI_ACCESS_CONTROL`), and `configuration.h` turns that off by default. 2.8.1 also adds a `region_presets` frame before the channels, which MeshMonitor ignores. I found no firmware change that explains the 2.7.15 → 2.8.1 timing. My best guess, which I have not verified: on 2.7.15 the reporter's channel edit also rebooted the node. The TCP reconnect then refreshed the whole UI. 2.8.1 applies the change without a reboot, so the stale poll cache shows.

## Fix

- After the 2 s wait, `handleReloadConfig` now invalidates the source's poll query (`sourcePollQueryKey(sourceId)`), so the channel list refetches right away.
- `POLL_QUERY_KEY` / `sourcePollQueryKey` move into `src/hooks/pollQueryKey.ts`, a module with no imports. `usePoll.ts` re-exports them, so existing imports still work. Without the move, importing the key from `usePoll` would load `init.ts`, which has side effects, and break the ConfigurationTab test mocks.

## Mesh impact

- **Airtime:** none. No new packets. The reload sends the same single `want_config_id` to the local node over TCP as before. Nothing goes over RF.
- **Spam / fan-out:** none. One extra `GET /api/poll` per manual button press. No events, notifications or automations.
- **Timers:** none added. No periodic request.

## Tests

- `src/components/ConfigurationT

title: fix(meshcore): send a firmware-v3 DeviceInfo from the Virtual Node (#5916)
body:
Closes #5916

## Problem
The Virtual Node answered DeviceQuery with version byte 1, zeros where the capacity bytes go, and a model string of any length. MeshCore One reads `maxContacts`, `maxChannels` and the fixed-width strings only when the version byte is **≥ 3** (`Parsers+Device.swift`). It read `maxChannels = 0`, synced no channels, and its Add Channel sheet said every slot was in use.

Fixing the layout alone (the issue's proposal) would not help: with the byte pinned at 1, MeshCore One still skips those fields.

## Fix
- **Version byte 3.** This is the lowest value at which MeshCore One reads capacities. It is also below every feature gate in both clients: meshcore-flutter (meshcore-open) gates at 8/9/11/12, and MeshCore One at 9/10/11/12/13. So the #3705 rule still holds: never send the real node's byte, and never claim features the VN lacks.
- **80-byte v3 frame**, the same layout as the companion firmware: `[13][ver][maxContacts/2][maxChannels][blePin u32][build 12][model 40][version 20]`. It omits the v9 `client_repeat` and v10 `path_hash_mode` bytes, because a v3 device doesn't send them.
- **Empty version string.** MeshCore One also enables features when that string reads "v1.11" or later (`isAtLeast`).
- **Real capacities.** `applyDeviceInfo` now caches `maxContacts`/`maxChannels` on the local node. Until the poller has cached them, the VN reports 8 slots, raised to cover the highest synced channel index, and 100 contacts.
- GetChannel is unchanged: MeshCore One treats `Err(NotFound)` on an empty slot as unconfigured.

## Mesh impact
No packets, timers or notifications. The change only affects the reply to a local TCP client.

## Tests
- Codec: v3 byte offsets, the 80-byte length, one-byte clamping, string truncation, and meshcore.js still decoding the frame.
- VN: real capacities, the empty version string, the fallback that covers synced slots, and the stock 8-slot default. The #3705 regression test is kept.
- Full suite: 32,286 passed, 0 failed (PG/MySQL suites skipped; no schema change). `tsc` and `lint:ci` are clean.

## Still to verify by hand
Connect MeshCore One to a VN and confirm the channels sync and Add Channel shows free slots. Also check that meshcore-flutter and the official app still complete the handshake.

title: fix(meshcore): trace direct-neighbour repeaters through their own hash (#5914)
body:
## Summary
Scheduled (and manual) MeshCore trace-path failed for direct neighbours. A contact with `pathLen == 0` has no `out_path`, and the guard in `traceContactPathDetailed` returned `no known path`, so SNR history never filled for direct links.

## Fix
- **Direct repeater or room server:** trace the single hop through the target's own key hash. The target appends its SNR and repeats the trace, and we hear the repeat, so one hop gives both directions. This is how the existing zero-hop Ping (#4393) already works.
  - The hop width is the caller's `hashBytes`, otherwise the source's default path hash size. A 3-byte default falls back to 1, since `CMD_SEND_TRACE_PATH` encodes only 1- and 2-byte hops (#4786).
  - Auto-return makes no difference here: the single hop already comes back.
- **Direct companion:** it still fails, now with a clear log line and **without sending**. Companion firmware drops traces (`allowPacketForward()` is false), so a trace would only wait out the timeout.
- **Unknown route** (`pathLen` null or negative): unchanged.
- **UI:** the contact panel now offers Trace Path for direct repeaters and room servers. It stays hidden for direct companions.

## Mesh impact
- **Airtime:** a scheduled trace to a direct repeater now sends one packet plus the target's one repeat per tick, where it used to send nothing. The schedule's existing interval and limits are unchanged, and the user already configured those traces to run.
- **Spam / notifications:** none new.
- **Timers:** none added or changed.

## Tests
- `meshcoreManager.tracePathDirect.test.ts` (8 tests): direct repeater and room server; 1- and 2-byte widths; the 3-byte fallback; caller-chosen width; auto-return; a direct companion sends nothing; an unknown route still fails.
- Contact panel: Trace Path is shown for a direct repeater and hidden for a direct companion.
- Full suite (`--maxWorkers=2`): 32,281 passed, 0 failed, 1,761 skipped (PG/MySQL; no schema change), no unhandled errors.
- `tsc` (app and server) and `lint:ci` are clean.

Closes #5914

title: feat(map): tropospheric ducting overlay UI on the Map tab and Dashboard map (#5734)
body:
## Summary

The UI for the tropospheric ducting overlay (#5734), built on the backend spike from #5875. Both the Map tab and the Dashboard map get a **Ducting** toggle, a time scrubber (now to +72 h), and a legend. An admin turns the feature on in Settings. It is off by default.

## Decisions applied

1. **Access.** New global setting `ductingOverlayEnabled`, off by default, in a new Settings section, "Tropospheric ducting overlay" (admin-only section, `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS` + `GLOBAL_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS`, strict boolean). Only admins can write it: a new `ADMIN_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS` set makes `POST /api/settings` drop the key for a non-admin `settings:write` holder, the same way it drops secret keys. Their full Settings save still works, and the stored value stays as it was. The key is not secret, so every map viewer can read it.
   - While off, `GET /api/ducting/forecast` answers **403 `DUCTING_DISABLED`** to everyone, admins included, before any other work. Nothing contacts NOAA, and both maps hide the toggle.
   - While on, `requireAdmin()` is replaced by the map's read gate. `optionalAuth` + `resolvePermittedSourceIds` (`nodes:read` on at least one source, including the anonymous user). Without it the caller gets 403 `FORBIDDEN`.
2. **Fetching.** The UI fetches only the step on view, through TanStack (`['ducting','forecast',hours]`, 30 min stale, `retry: false`, `keepPreviousData`). The scrubber commits a step only after a 300 ms rest, so a drag across all 25 steps makes one request. There is no prefetch and no timer. The server's per-(cycle, hour, box) cache is unchanged.
3. **Box.** The UI never sends `bbox`. **The default area did leak.** It came from every source's nodes, so a viewer who can read only source A could learn the rough spread of source B's nodes. The box is now built from the nodes the **caller** can see on the map: their readable sources, filtered by `buildPositionFilter` (hidden, private-position, and no-`viewOnMap` channel nodes drop out). Viewers who see the same nodes get the same box and share one cache entry. See "Decisions to confirm" for the cache-key cost.
4. **Legend.** The three ITU-R P.453 classes. Normal: no fill. Super-refractive: one light tint (`--color-info`, opacity 0.22). Ducting: `--color-caution`, opacity 0.30 → 0.60 as ΔM (`ductStrengthM`) rises from 0 to 20 M-units. **Sub-refractive is left unfilled**, the same as normal: it means shorter range, and the overlay marks only where range is longer. Colours are existing role tokens, set as CSS `fill` in `DuctingLayer.module.css`. That works because a CSS `fill` beats Leaflet's SVG attribute. No new theme tokens and no hardcoded colours.
5. **Maps.** One layer, `src/components/map/layers/DuctingLayer.tsx` (non-interactive, unstroked `Rectangle`s, so markers stay clickable and readable). title: feat(meshcore): resolve unknown route hops from other sources (#5909)
body:
## Summary

When a relay hash in a MeshCore message route matches none of the receiving source's contacts, the route view can now name it from MeshCore nodes on **other sources the viewer can read**, including `meshcore_mqtt` feeds. Display only.

- **Resolution order:** own contacts first, unchanged. The fallback only fills hops with zero own matches.
- **Server pool:** `GET /api/sources/:id/meshcore/hop-candidates?prefixes=a3,7f01` returns `{ enabled, candidates: { hash → [{ name, publicKey, sourceId, sourceName, latitude?, longitude? }] } }` for the requested hashes only (2/4/6 hex, max 64).
  - Gate: `requirePermission('nodes','read',{ sourceIdFrom: 'params.id' })` on the requesting source.
  - The pool holds only other `meshcore` / `meshcore_mqtt` sources the viewer can read (`resolvePermittedSourceIds`, admins: all enabled). It never includes the requesting source itself.
  - It returns only relays (advType 2/3), which matches `resolveRoute`.
  - Positions go through `buildMeshCorePositionFilter`: without `nodes:viewOnMap` on the candidate's source, the candidate comes back with no coordinates. A private override also needs `nodes_private:read`; without it, no position is returned at all. An enabled, visible override is the position used.
  - A node known to several sources appears once. The device source's copy names it, and any readable copy can fill in the position.
- **MQTT trust:** no verification marker existed (MQTT ingest decodes signatures but does not check them, #5040). This PR adds `meshcore_nodes.advertSignatureVerified` (migration 215, all three backends, nullable). MQTT ingest writes it on every advert. MQTT nodes count only when it is `true`. See Decisions.
- **Shared resolver:** `resolveRouteWithFallback()` in `src/utils/meshcorePath.ts` builds on `resolveRoute` and is pure, so the Packet Monitor path column and the trace SNR rows can reuse it later.
- **Labels (CSS module, colour tokens):**
  - A single fallback match reads `Name (via Source)` in the info colour. It is not tentative.
  - A collision with positions reads `Name? (via Source, N candidates)` in italics in the warning colour. A "Show all N candidates (nearest first)" list expands under it, and the same list appears on hover.
  - A collision with nothing to rank shows `N candidates` and the list.
  - A guess carries no position, so the flow map never draws one.
- **Ranking:** I used both signals. A candidate's score is its summed distance to (a) the previous hop's position, only when that hop is not itself a guess; (b) the next hop's position, when that hop resolves to one node; and (c) the receiving radio's position, standing in as the "next hop" after the last relay. With no neighbour anchor, the receiving radio alone is used. Candidates without a position sort last.

title: feat(telemetry): cross-source Telemetry Dashboard on Unified Telemetry (#5896)
body:
## Summary

Rewrites **Unified Telemetry** as a cross-source Telemetry Dashboard. The page now opens on graphs of every favorited series across the sources you can read. Each chart covers one (node, telemetry type) and draws one line per source. The old card grid stays as a **Latest** tab.

### Graphs (default view)
- The page shows the union of each readable source's `telemetryFavorites` list. The schema does not change.
- Each chart has one overlapping line per source, coloured by source, and the legend shows the source name. Lines are never merged or averaged together.
- Observer-relative types (SNR, RSSI, channel util/air TX, LocalStats packet counters, MeshMonitor per-source series, clock offset) are still overlaid, but each line is labelled **"heard by <source>"**. A new `isObserverRelative(type)` in `telemetryCategory.ts` drives the label, and tests enforce it.
- Charts are grouped into the per-source dashboard's category sections. The view adds the range presets (15m to 7d, remembered), a source filter, a refresh button, CSV export per chart (one file, with a `Source` column) and an empty state.
- The view fetches on load, on a range change, and on refresh. It does not poll.

### Latest tab
- Same cards as before. Each reading now has a star that adds it to or removes it from **its own source's** favorites. The star only appears where you hold `settings:write` on that source.
- **The N+1 is gone:** `GET /api/unified/telemetry` now runs one query per source (`getLatestTelemetryPerNodeAndTypeSince`) instead of a query per node per type. The poll interval is now 60 s instead of 15 s.

### Backend
- New `GET /api/unified/telemetry/series?hours=` returns `{ success, data: { series: [{ subjectKey, nodeName, type, favoriteType, category, observerRelative, lines: [{ sourceId, sourceName, unit, favorited, canEditFavorite, points }] }] } }`. `subjectKey` is the `!hex` node id for Meshtastic/MQTT and the public key for MeshCore.
- The per-source rules match `GET /api/telemetry/:nodeId`:
  - The source needs `nodes:read`.
  - A Meshtastic node needs channel `viewOnMap` there; a MeshCore node needs `nodes:viewOnMap`.
  - The position rows of a private node need `nodes_private:read`.
  - This reuses `loadNodeViewAccess` / `canViewNode` / `omitPositionTelemetry` from #5901 and loads grants once per request.
- A favorite only counts on a source where you can see its node.
- The averaged query (`getTelemetryByNodeAveragedSqlite` / `…Sql`) gains an optional `types` filter, so the endpoint never fetches unfavorited types. It still returns ~240 buckets per line.
- The logic lives in `src/server/services/unifiedTelemetryService.ts`; `unifiedRoutes.ts` only wires the routes.

### Shared frontend utilities (lifted, not duplicated)
- `telemetrySeriesDisplay.ts`: unit scaling, C/F conversion and CSV download. `TelemetryGraphWidget` now uses it too.
- `telemetryRangePresets.ts`: the range presets, now shared with `TelemetryGraphs`.

title: feat(adsb): add OpenSky Network as an ADS-B feed (#5877)
body:
## Summary

Adds **OpenSky Network** as a third ADS-B feed for likely-aircraft flight matching, next to adsb.lol and adsb.fi.

OpenSky does not fit the readsb point-query shape, so `AdsbFeedInfo` gains optional hooks. The readsb feeds keep the defaults:

- `buildRequest(lat, lon, nm)`: OpenSky turns the point and radius into a `states/all?lamin=&lomin=&lamax=&lomax=` box. Δlat = r/111 km and Δlon = Δlat/cos(lat). Near a pole the box takes every longitude. At ±180° the box is clamped instead of wrapped (documented in `src/utils/openSky.ts`).
- `parse(body)`: maps the positional `states[]` arrays to `AdsbAircraft`: m→ft, m/s→kt, `on_ground`→`'ground'`, `seen_pos = time − time_position`, callsign trimmed, hex lower-cased. OpenSky has no type or registration, so popups show callsign and hex only.
- `auth: 'oauth2'`: the client sends `Authorization: Bearer`. On a 401 it drops the token and retries **once**. **The shared `adsb_api_token` is never sent to OpenSky.**
- `retryAfterHeader`: reads `X-Rate-Limit-Retry-After-Seconds` on a 429.
- `credit`: popup credit reads "Data: The OpenSky Network".

New `openSkyTokenManager.ts` runs the client-credentials flow. It caches the token in memory only, refreshes 60 s before expiry, shares one request between concurrent callers, and sends the token request through `safeFetch`.

## Maintainer decisions applied

- **Credentials required, no anonymous mode.** `POST /api/settings` refuses `adsbFeed=opensky` (400 `ADSB_OPENSKY_CREDENTIALS_REQUIRED`) unless both credentials are set, whether they come in the same save or are already stored. It also refuses a save that clears a credential while OpenSky stays selected. In the UI the OpenSky option is disabled and labelled "(needs client ID and secret)" until both fields hold a value. If OpenSky is selected with a credential missing, a warning shows. The service also skips the lookup without both.
- **Retry-After honoured on 429.** OpenSky pauses until the given time, not the fixed 10-minute backoff. The pause-until time is saved in the settings key `adsb_opensky_paused_until`, so a restart does not hammer a spent quota. That key is server-written only and is not in `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS`, so a settings save cannot clear it. Other failures, and a 429 without the header, keep the existing 10-minute backoff. **No migration.**
- No per-day credit budget, no cross-feed fallback. An OpenSky pause does not block adsb.lol or adsb.fi.
- New settings `adsb_opensky_client_id` / `adsb_opensky_client_secret`. Both are in `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS` and `GLOBAL_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS`, and both are hidden from non-admins: the secret by its `_secret` suffix, the id through `SECRET_SETTINGS_KEYS`.
- The terms line reads "non-commercial and research use only" and gives the credit.

## Decisions to confirm

- **24-hour cap on a Retry-After pause** (`MAX_RETRY_AFTER_MS`), so a bad header cannot stop OpenSky lookups for good. OpenSky's quota is daily, so a real value should fit.

title: feat(adsb): re-check aircraft flight matches as the node moves (#5876)
body:
## Summary

A likely-aircraft flight match used to lock in after the second lookup. A flight-number rollover (`GJS4418` → `GJS4455` on the same airframe) or a wrong first pick stayed on screen for the whole flagging.

After the two first lookups, a live position now re-checks the match when the node has moved **more than 10 km** from the last lookup's position, **or** **15 minutes or more** have passed since the last lookup. Each re-check is one point query through the existing queue, backoff and reuse cache, then `matchAircraft`:

- **same hex**: refresh callsign, speed, track, altitude and distance; status `matched`
- **different, unambiguous hex**: status `possible` with the new aircraft
- **no hit**: miss count +1. **Two misses in a row clear the match** (status `none`, so the popup line goes away). A hit resets the count.

At most **6 re-checks per flagging**. The re-check count, miss count and last-lookup time/lat/lon live in `aircraft_flight_matches` (migration 214). `recordRecheck` writes with the same compare-and-set as `lookups` (episode + `rechecks` must match what the caller read), so a restart or a settings save cannot reset the cap or spend the same re-check twice. A restart triggers nothing; only a live fix starts a re-check.

## Decisions applied (maintainer)

- Trigger: > 10 km from the last lookup's position OR ≥ 15 min since the last lookup.
- Same hex → refresh, matched. Different unambiguous hex → possible. No hit → miss; 2 consecutive misses clear; a hit resets.
- Cap 6 re-checks per flagging, persisted with CAS. Last-lookup lat/lon/time persisted.
- No link to `aircraftPositionRequestService`, no new events or notifications on a callsign change.
- Help text and docs now say "two lookups per flagging, then up to six re-checks".

## Decisions to confirm

1. **Who gets re-checked.** Re-checks are open to rows with `lookups ≥ 2` OR status `matched`/`possible` (as specified). A row still inside the lookup-2 window (60 s–30 min after lookup 1) waits for lookup 2 and is not re-checked first. A `possible` row whose lookup-2 window passed with no fix goes to the re-check lane. A `none` row with only one lookup does not.
2. **A `possible` row that re-checks to the same hex becomes `matched`.** That matches lookup 2: the same aircraft seen twice confirms it.
3. **An ambiguous result (two aircraft about equally close) counts as a miss**, because `matchAircraft` returns no match for it.
4. **Rows from before this change** have no last-lookup position or time. For the time check they fall back to `matchedAt`, then `firstLookupAt`. The distance check is skipped until the first lookup or re-check writes a position.
5. The internal columns (`lastLookup*`, `rechecks`, `misses`) are left out of the `/flight-match` response. The last-lookup point is a node position, and the route's private-position gate does not cover new fields.

## Mesh impact

- **Airtime: none.** Outbound HTTPS only, no mesh packets, no link to the position-request service

title: fix(estimator): count unique anchor positions; explain estimates on Node Details (#5900)
body:
## Summary

**Estimator fix.** Repeat observations of one anchor counted as independent evidence. Six traceroute replies through one relay gave `nEff ≈ 5.75`, a zero spread, and a 50 m radius for what is one anchor's worth of information.

- `nEff` is now the Kish effective sample size over **unique anchor positions**: weights are summed per position first. Centroid and RMS spread are unchanged (both are linear in the weights).
- A solve backed by one position is always `single_anchor` (radio-range default), however many observations it has.
- The #3616 guard is unchanged and its tests still pass.
- Positions match within `ANCHOR_POSITION_TOLERANCE_DEG = 1e-6` (about 0.11 m), documented in the service.
- Stored anchors (cap 20) now hold the strongest observation of each distinct position before any repeats, so one busy relay can't fill every slot.
- **Stale rows:** a run now also deletes estimates it did not rewrite. Without this, a node with no observation left in the lookback window kept its pre-fix 50 m row forever. On the dev container the issue's pattern (`!580f28cc`: 16 obs, 1 anchor, 50 m "convergence") was in exactly that state, and only this change cleared it.

**API.** `GET /api/nodes/:nodeNum/position-estimate` adds `uniqueAnchors`, `uniqueAnchorsIsLowerBound`, and per-anchor `anchorLongName` / `anchorShortName`. All existing fields stay. No migration: `uniqueAnchors` is counted from the stored anchor rows. This is exact unless all 20 stored slots hold different positions and observations were dropped; then the API sets `uniqueAnchorsIsLowerBound` and the UI shows "20+".

**Node Details box.** When the displayed position is estimated, a bordered box explains it:
- method in plain words (single anchor with radio-range default / partly converged / converged from N anchors)
- uncertainty, observations, unique anchors, and when it was computed
- the anchor list (name, id, kind, SNR, weight, distance from the estimate), collapsed when there are more than 3

It is a CSS module with tokens, uses `UiIcon` and i18n with English defaults, and goes through `ApiService.getPositionEstimate` (unwraps `body.data`). Hidden for GPS and override positions.

## Permission check

The route used `nodes:read` with no source, but anchors are pooled from every Meshtastic source and each stored row carries that node's coordinates. So it could reveal positions from sources the caller can't read, private overrides, nodes on channels without `viewOnMap`, and "Hide from Map" nodes. Changes (`src/server/utils/positionEstimateAccess.ts`):

- **Anchors:** a non-admin sees an anchor only when a source they hold `nodes:read` on has that node **at the same coordinates**, and that row passes `buildPositionFilter` on its own source. That filter covers channel `viewOnMap`, `nodes_private:read` for private overrides, and `hideFromMap`. The coordinates must match because the estimator takes an anchor's position from whichever source it read last: a node visible on source B c

The server already checks `traceroute:read` for reads and `traceroute:write` for sends. The Users page did not: it showed one "Can Initiate Traceroutes" box that set both. So an admin could not give anonymous users a read-only Traceroute Explorer without also letting them send traceroutes.

- **Users page:** the `traceroute` row is now the standard **Read / Write** pair. The tooltip says what each covers (Write includes NeighborInfo requests). `permission.ts` description and `en.json` key updated (`users.can_initiate_traceroutes` → `users.traceroute_permission`).
- **MeshCore Trace Path** (`POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/contacts/:pk/trace-path`) now takes `traceroute:write` on that source (`sourceIdFrom: 'params.id'`), not `nodes:write`. The contact panel gates the button the same way (`canTraceroute` prop).
- **Migration 213** (SQLite / PostgreSQL / MySQL, idempotent): every (user, MeshCore source) with `nodes` canWrite gets `traceroute` canWrite. If a traceroute row exists it sets canWrite; if not, it inserts one with only canWrite on. It never clears a flag.
- Docs: new "Traceroute read and write" section in `docs/features/per-source-permissions.md`.

## Decisions applied

1. Standard Read / Write pair for `traceroute`; label, tooltip, description and en.json updated.
2. NeighborInfo requests stay under `traceroute:write`; named in the Write tooltip.
3. MeshCore trace-path moved to `traceroute:write` with a backfill. Write-only rows are left alone; no read access is added anywhere.
4. Anonymous / new-user seeding: checked. Anonymous seeds only `dashboard`, `nodes`, `info`, and new-user provisioning writes only global (non-per-source) resources, so neither grants `traceroute`. Effective access is unchanged; no change needed.

Existing grants need no migration for the split: the old checkbox always wrote `{read: v, write: v}`, so every existing row already has both or neither.

## Decisions to confirm

- **Backfill limited to MeshCore sources.** The brief says "every (user, source) with nodes:write". I limited the backfill to sources with `type = 'meshcore'` (the only type with a trace-path route, same join as migration 135). Running it on Meshtastic sources too would give `nodes:write` holders the right to send Meshtastic traceroutes they cannot send today, which widens mesh TX for no regression benefit. To cover every source, drop the `sources` join in migration 213.
- **MeshCore zero-hop Ping** (`/contacts/:pk/ping`) also sends a TRACE packet but stays on `nodes:write`; the brief named only trace-path.

## Mesh impact

No change to what can be sent or how often. Only who may click changes. Read-only traceroute users can no longer send anything (as before, for users with neither grant). Current MeshCore `nodes:write` holders keep Trace Path through the backfill. Meshtastic grants are untouched.

## Tests

- `src/server/routes/tracerouteReadWrite.permissions.test.ts` (route harness, new): read grant → 200 on a read route, 403 on PO

title: fix(mqtt-bridge): single-mode client ID, eviction stop, uplink drop count (#5893)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the three problems in #5893 on the MQTT bridge side:

1. **`single` mode could not log in to strict brokers.** It always used a random `mm-bridge-<sourceId>-<random>` Client ID, and brokers that accept only `!<8-hex>` refused it with CONNACK 4.
2. **`per_gateway` mode fell into an endless eviction loop.** It opens one connection for the bridge plus one per local gateway, all with the same login. Under a per-username connection cap, or with a second client holding the same ID, these connections evicted each other for ever.
3. **Uplink packets vanished.** `handleUplink` returned silently when the subscriber was disconnected, with no log line and no counter.

## Changes

- **Optional single-mode Client ID** (`upstream.clientId`). Validated on POST and PUT `/api/sources` against `^!?[0-9a-fA-F]{8}$`, stored as lowercase `!xxxxxxxx` (`INVALID_CLIENT_ID` on failure; blank removes it). The bridge uses it as given, with no random suffix. The default stays `mm-bridge-…`, and `per_gateway` mode ignores the field. The bridge settings page shows the field only in Single mode. It has a **Use the parent broker's gateway ID** button and placeholder, plus help text: strict brokers need `!xxxxxxxx`, and the ID must not match one another client uses on that broker. The redaction spec classifies it as `withheld`: editors see it, viewers do not.
- **Eviction stop.** `MqttBrokerClient` takes an opt-in `maxEvictions` / `evictionWindowMs`. An eviction is a session the broker closes within 10 s of CONNACK with no client-side error. That is the same signal the duplicate-ID hint already used. The bridge sets **5 evictions in 10 minutes** on the subscriber and on every per-gateway publisher. A stopped client sends no more CONNECTs. The status gets `evictionStopped`, `evictionStoppedGateways`, `evictionStoppedGatewayCount`, and a fixed `permissionMessage`/`lastError` that the unauthenticated status may show. The sidebar card reads **Stopped: evicted** and shows the **Connect** button. A source save (new manager), a manual Connect (`reconnectAuthStopped`, which now covers eviction stops too), or a restart resumes it. The count is in memory by design.
- **`uplinkDisconnectedDrops`** on the status. It counts packets dropped while the subscriber is down, plus packets dropped on eviction-stopped gateways. The log notes the drop **once per disconnected episode** at info level; the next successful connect re-arms it. The bridge settings page shows the count next to the other drop counters.
- **Duplicate-ID hint reworded.** It now names four causes: another bridge source on the same broker and upstream; a per-username connection cap (per_gateway opens N+1 connections with one login, so try single mode with a `!hex` Client ID); the gateway node itself; another MeshMonitor instance.
- **Shared-upstream warning (optional item 5).** When two running bridges share a parent broker and upstream URL in `per_gateway` mode, the bridge logs a warning at start and the status

title: fix(security): scope traceroute history and unified telemetry to permitted sources
body:
## Summary

Two cross-source read leaks. Both let a non-admin read data from a source, or a node, their grants do not cover.

### Leak 1: traceroute history and route-segment records (#5898)

`GET /api/traceroutes/history/:from/:to`, `GET /api/route-segments/longest-active` and `GET /api/route-segments/record-holder` gate on `requirePermission('traceroute', 'read', { sourceIdFrom: 'query' })`. With no `sourceId` in the request, that gate passes on a `traceroute:read` grant for **any** source, and the handlers then read `ALL_SOURCES`.

**Impact:** a user with `traceroute:read` on source A only could omit `sourceId` and read source B's traceroute history for any node pair, and B's longest-active / record-holder segments (with node names looked up across every source).

**Fix:** a shared `permittedReadScope(user, resource, sourceId)` in `src/server/utils/sourcePermissions.ts`. A named source (already checked by the gate) reads as before; with none named, an admin reads every source and anyone else reads the list of sources they hold `traceroute:read` on (empty list = no rows). The same rule `/traceroutes/recent` already uses. The three repository methods now take a `SourceSetScope`, so the list goes into one `IN (...)` query rather than N queries. Segment node names now come from the segment's own source. The frontend callers pass `sourceId` optionally; the cross-source form still works, narrowed.

### Leak 2: unified telemetry (#5896)

`GET /api/unified/telemetry` checked only `nodes:read` per source. The per-node route `GET /api/telemetry/:nodeId` also requires channel access for the node and strips latitude/longitude/altitude rows for a private-position node unless the caller holds `nodes_private:read`.

**Confirmed** with a route test before the fix: a user with `nodes:read` + `channel_0:viewOnMap` on A got all 12 rows, including position rows for a private-position node and every row for a node on channel 3 they cannot view.

**Impact:** any user with `nodes:read` on a source could read the latest telemetry of every node there, including private-position coordinates and nodes on channels hidden from them.

**Fix:** the unified route loads `loadNodeViewAccess(user)` once and applies the per-node route's rules: `canViewNode(source, channel)` per Meshtastic node, `nodes:viewOnMap` on the source for MeshCore peers (as `checkNodeChannelAccess` does), and `omitPositionTelemetry()` (now shared with the per-node route) for private-position nodes without `nodes_private:read`. Admins are unaffected.

## Tests

- `src/server/routes/tracerouteHistoryScope.test.ts` (harness): user granted only A gets no B rows from `/history`, `/longest-active`, `/record-holder` with no `sourceId` (these 3 failed before the fix); admin sees all; a named forbidden source stays 403.
- `src/server/routes/unifiedRoutes.telemetryScope.test.ts` (harness): private-position stripping, channel access, `nodes_private:read` restores position rows, cross-source channel grants do not op

title: feat(meshcore): store CLI command history (#5892)
body:
Closes #5892

## Summary
MeshMonitor now stores every MeshCore CLI command a **person** sends through it, with a timestamp, and shows that history in the UI.

Recorded at the four entry points where a person is known:
1. Remote console: `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/admin/cli`. This also covers the Companion remote console (#5867).
2. Local console: `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/cli`. Covers Repeater/Room Server serial, Companion fw 1.18 native CLI, and the older synthetic Companion CLI.
3. Time-sync button: `POST /nodes/:publicKey/time-sync`, stored as `clock sync`, the console verb the manager rewrites to `time <epoch>`.
4. Virtual Node CLI relay (`handleSendCliTxtMsg`): `origin: 'vn'`, no user id, `username: 'vn:<clientId>'`, plus the app's IP.

Background CLI use is **not** recorded: stats and neighbour polls, config `get` refreshes, `meshcoreTimeSyncScheduler`, and automations. They call the manager directly, and recording happens only in the route and VN handlers.

Outcomes: `ok`, `blocked` (danger guard without `confirm`, receive-only gate on a transmitting local verb, VN with admin commands off; nothing was sent), `failed`, `timeout`.

## Schema: migration 212, `meshcore_cli_history` (per-source)
`id, sourceId, timestamp (ms), targetKind ('local'|'remote'), targetPublicKey, targetName, origin ('user'|'vn'), userId, username (denormalised), command (redacted), outcome, reply (redacted, capped at 8 KB), error, elapsedMs, ipAddress`. Indexes are `(sourceId, timestamp)` and `(timestamp)`. All three backends use idempotent DDL. The table is in `BACKUP_TABLES` and `migrationTables.ts`, and source delete purges its rows.

Retention is 90 days by default. The new setting `meshcoreCliHistoryRetentionDays` (7–365, the same range as the audit-log field) sits next to Audit Log Retention in Database Maintenance. The nightly maintenance job prunes in batches and reports the count in its stats.

## Redaction (security)
`src/server/utils/meshcoreCliRedact.ts`:
- masks the argument of `password`, `passwd`, `login`
- masks the value of `set <key> …` when the key is `password`, `guest.password`, `admin.password`, `prv.key`, any `*.key`, or any `*.password`/`*.pwd`/`*.pass`/`*.psk`/`*.secret` (`wifi.password`, `bridge.secret`, …)
- masks the reply to `get` of any such key (`get prv.key`, `get guest.password`), and any echo of a written secret in a reply or error

The same redactor now runs on `details.command` in `auditMeshcoreEvent`, which closes the existing plaintext leak into `audit_log` for every MeshCore CLI audit row. The `[MeshCore] TX:` serial debug log line is masked too. The radio still gets the real text.

## API
- `GET /api/sources/:id/meshcore/cli-history?limit=&before=&target=&user=&from=&to=`
- `GET /api/meshcore/cli-history?…&source=`: covers every source the caller may read, and returns the readable MeshCore sources for the filter.

Permissions are per source and checked per row kind. Remote rows need `remote_admin:read`; local rows nee

title: fix(config): honor DATA_DIR for every data path (#5889)
body:
Fixes #5889

## Summary

On a baremetal install, setting `DATA_DIR` did not move MeshMonitor's data off `/data`. Under the documented systemd unit (`ProtectSystem=strict`, `ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/meshmonitor`), the server failed to write there (`ENOENT ... mkdir '/data/firmware-backups'`).

Two causes:

1. **Most paths ignored `DATA_DIR`.** Backups, system backups, the restore marker, the access log, the default database path, the Apprise URL file and the default GeoJSON/map-style singletons (used by the public embed routes) all hard-coded `/data`.
2. **The paths that read `DATA_DIR` read it at module load.** `firmwareUpdateService` held it in a module-level const. ESM hoists imports above `server.ts`'s `dotenv` load, so a `DATA_DIR` set in a `.env` that dotenv loads came too late. (A systemd `EnvironmentFile` sets the variable before Node starts, so that path depended only on cause 1.)

## Fix

New `src/server/config/dataDir.ts` with `getDataDir()` (`$DATA_DIR`, else `/data`), `dataPath(...)` and one getter per path. All of them read `process.env` **at call time**. A path-specific variable still wins over the derived default. With `DATA_DIR` unset, every path is byte-for-byte the same as before, so Docker is unchanged. The desktop sidecar already sets `DATA_DIR` and keeps working.

| Path | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| SQLite DB (`environment.ts`) | `$DATABASE_PATH` or `/data/meshmonitor.db` | `$DATABASE_PATH` or `$DATA_DIR/meshmonitor.db` |
| Access log (`environment.ts`, incl. invalid-path fallback) | `/data/logs/access.log` | `$DATA_DIR/logs/access.log` |
| Device backups (`backupFileService.ts`) | `$BACKUP_DIR` or `/data/backups` | `$BACKUP_DIR` or `$DATA_DIR/backups` |
| System backups (`systemBackupService.ts`, `systemRestoreService.ts`) | `$SYSTEM_BACKUP_DIR` or `/data/system-backups` | `$SYSTEM_BACKUP_DIR` or `$DATA_DIR/system-backups` |
| Restore marker (`systemRestoreService.ts`) | `/data/.restore-completed` | `$DATA_DIR/.restore-completed` |
| Firmware backups/staging (`firmwareUpdateService.ts`) | `DATA_DIR` read at module load | read at call time |
| Apprise URL file (`notificationRoutes.ts`) | `$APPRISE_CONFIG_DIR` or `/data/apprise-config` | `$APPRISE_CONFIG_DIR` or `$DATA_DIR/apprise-config` |
| GeoJSON / map styles default singletons (`geojsonService.ts`, `mapStyleService.ts`) | `/data/geojson`, `/data/styles` | `$DATA_DIR/...`, resolved at use |
| Scripts dir (`scriptRoutes.ts`, `meshtasticManager.ts`, `scriptRunner.ts`), `server.ts` geojson/styles | inline `process.env.DATA_DIR \|\| '/data'` | shared `dataPath()` |

The startup config log now prints `DATA_DIR`.

### `/data/scripts/` was left unchanged on purpose

`/data/scripts/<name>` is the **logical** identifier that auto-responder triggers, timer triggers and the script list store in settings. The `startsWith('/data/scripts/')` checks in `meshtasticManager.ts`, `scriptRoutes.ts` and `settingsRoutes.ts` check that stored format, then map the basename onto the real `$DATA

title: feat(autoack): choose the 0-hop and MQTT tapback glyphs (#5890)
body:
Closes #5890.

Lets an operator choose the tapback glyphs Auto Acknowledge sends, so a mesh that uses `0️⃣` for "heard directly over RF" and `*️⃣` for "came over MQTT" can match its own convention.

## What changes
Two new **per-source** settings in Auto Acknowledge, next to the response matrix. Both are blank by default, and blank keeps today's behaviour exactly.

| Setting | Replaces | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| **0-hop tapback** (`hopEmojiZeroHop`) | `*️⃣` for a 0-hop message | Auto-Ack tapbacks; automation hop-count tapbacks and `{{ trigger.hopEmoji }}` |
| **MQTT tapback** (`hopEmojiMqtt`) | Auto-Ack: the hop glyph for an IP-row message (received over MQTT/UDP). Automations: `#️⃣` for a message from an MQTT source | Same as above |

For the requester's mesh: 0-hop = `0️⃣`, MQTT = `*️⃣`.

The issue proposed one global setting. These are per source instead, because every other Auto-Ack setting is per source and the panel saves per source. Automations read the setting for the source the message came from.

## Screenshot
Auto Acknowledge on a Meshtastic source, set up for the requester's mesh (not saved):

![0-hop and MQTT tapback fields](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/assets/screenshot-5890/screenshots/pr5890-glyphs.png)

## Details
- `src/utils/hopEmoji.ts`: `hopCountEmoji` / `hopOrMqttEmoji` take optional overrides; adds `parseHopEmojiOverrides` and `isValidHopEmojiSetting`. The glyph table itself is unchanged.
- `meshtasticManager.ts`: the Auto-Ack tapback reads the two settings. An IP packet uses the MQTT glyph only when one is set.
- Automation Engine: a new optional `getHopEmojiOverrides` provider method, read only when a message automation is loaded (the existing DB-free hot path stays intact).
- `POST /api/settings` rejects anything except blank or one short glyph (≤16 chars, no spaces), with `400 INVALID_INPUT`. A bad stored value is ignored at send time.
- Docs: `automation.md` and `automation-engine.md`.

## Mesh impact
None. It changes which emoji an existing tapback carries. No new packets, no new timers, and nothing about when or how often Auto-Ack fires.

## Tests
- `hopEmoji.test.ts`: overrides, blank/invalid fallback, validator.
- `meshtasticManager.autoAckTapbackGlyphs.test.ts`: 0-hop glyph, multi-hop untouched, IP with/without MQTT glyph, invalid stored value.
- `settingsRoutes.hopEmoji.test.ts` (route harness): per-source storage, blank accepted, invalid rejected without writing.
- `triggerContext.test.ts`: automation context uses the glyphs.
- Existing `autoAckTapbackEmoji` regression suite still passes unchanged.

`tsc` (app + server) and `lint:ci` are clean. Full Vitest suite: 31,918 passed; the only 2 failures were the settings round-trip test, which needed valid sample values for the new keys (fixed and rerun green). 1,731 PG/MySQL tests skipped locally; no schema change.

title: build(deps): bump node-notifier from 10.0.1 to 11.0.0
body:
Bumps [node-notifier](https://github.com/mikaelbr/node-notifier) from 10.0.1 to 11.0.0.
Changelog

Sourced from node-notifier's changelog.

v11.0.0

Even though this is a major version, there are no real breaking changes for most people. This removes uneeded external dependencies and updates the internal dependencies to the latest versions.

But it now only checks and verifies node versions 20.x, 22.x, 24.x. So if you are on older versions, this might break.

There will be an upcoming major version that has bigger breaking changes, so this is an intermediate major version to clean up the codebase and dependencies.

Features:

  • Adds clearAll() to NotificationCenter to stop waiting on active notifications, so the application can exit without waiting for their timeouts. See #210

title: build(deps): bump emoji-picker-react from 4.22.3 to 5.0.0
body:
Bumps [emoji-picker-react](https://github.com/ealush/emoji-picker-react) from 4.22.3 to 5.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from emoji-picker-react's releases.

5.0.0

5.0.0 (2026-10-10)

⚠ BREAKING CHANGES

  • The published JavaScript targets ES2020. webpack 4 setups that do not run dependencies through Babel must transpile emoji-picker-react or upgrade; see docs/v5/MIGRATION.md.
  • Native rendering checks glyph availability even when emojiVersion is supplied. That prop remains an additional version cap; choose an image style for inventory independent of installed fonts.
  • v5 changes the default emoji style to native and replaces managed markup and interaction defaults. See docs/v5/MIGRATION.md for compatibility options and migration steps.

Features

  • add composable picker primitives (#560) (0852459)
  • add picker recipes and the design gallery (#564) (8b37306)
  • add styling tokens, cascade layers and BYOD composition (#561) (277d46e)
  • data: return emoji text and display name from the data API (e48a4d2)
  • data: ship shared emoji search and lookup APIs (#559) (e4d6f9a)
  • define the v5 release contract and migration (#566) (6617179)
  • expand controlled picker interactions (#562) (ce8e145)
  • harden the picker runtime for v5 (#557) (

title: build(deps): bump express from 5.2.1 to 5.3.0
body:
Bumps [express](https://github.com/expressjs/express) from 5.2.1 to 5.3.0.
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. v6.14.0

  • Fix the view sliding hundreds of meters off the center when terrain is switched on during a gesture (#8688) (by @​johncarmack1984)

Updates `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` from 4.38.3 to 4.39.0
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's releases.

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

title: feat(ducting): spike GFS tropospheric ducting forecast endpoint (#5734)
body:
Spike for #5734 (tropospheric ducting overlay). Backend only, no UI. It answers the open question of whether we can compute ducting ourselves from NOAA GFS without new dependencies or a tile server: **yes**.

## What it adds

`GET /api/ducting/forecast?hoursAhead=0..72[&bbox=minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat]` (admin-only)

Returns a 0.25° grid (row-major, north row first) with, per cell:
- `minGradientNPerKm`: the steepest refractivity gradient below ~3 km above ground (ITU-R P.453)
- `class`: `sub-refractive` / `normal` / `super-refractive` (≤ −79 N/km) / `ducting` (≤ −157 N/km)
- `ductStrengthM`: the largest M-unit drop across a trapping layer (0 when nothing traps)
- `layerBaseM` / `layerTopM`: where that gradient sits, in metres above ground

It also returns `cycle`, `forecastHour`, `validTime` and a per-class `summary`. Without `bbox`, the area is the 5th–95th percentile spread of Meshtastic nodes heard in the last 7 days, padded by 0.5°, snapped to the grid and capped at 20°×20°.

## How it works

- **Data:** the NOMADS grib filter cuts one GFS forecast file down to TMP/RH/HGT/PRES at the surface, 2 m and nine isobaric levels (1000–700 hPa) inside the box. A Florida-sized box is ~50 KB and ~1.2 s per forecast hour, instead of the ~500 MB global file.
- **Decoding:** a ~200-line GRIB2 reader. The filter always repacks its cuts as simple packing (template 5.0) on a regular lat/lon grid, so that's all we need. Other templates are refused by name (502 `GFS_UNREADABLE`), not misread. No eccodes, no npm dependency.
- **Physics:** `N = 77.6/T · (P + 4810·e/T)`, `M = N + 157·h(km)`. Levels below ground are dropped, as are layers under 10 m thick.
- **Load on NOAA:** an in-memory cache per (cycle, hour, box); concurrent identical requests share one fetch. An unpublished cycle (NOMADS answers 403 HTML) falls back to the previous one and is skipped for 15 minutes. **There is no timer:** a fetch only happens when an admin calls the endpoint.

## Findings

Live results for the current cycle (dev container, then three regions):

| Area | ducting | super-refractive | normal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Florida (default area from dev nodes, 384 cells) | 0 | 356 | 28 |
| Southern California (273) | 123 | 33 | 117 |
| Kansas (273) | 1 | 104 | 168 |

SoCal's marine-layer inversion shows up as ducting, the humid Gulf coast as super-refraction, and the dry interior as mostly normal, which matches known climatology. So the method behaves.

What the spike surfaced for the real feature:
1. **Pressure levels are coarse.** They sit 200–500 m apart near the ground, so sharp inversions are smoothed out and the index **under-reads** ducts. In ~30–60% of cells, the steepest layer is surface→1000 hPa. Better vertical resolution needs GFS's other level types (the `pgrb2b` file or hybrid levels). This is a v2 option, not a blocker.
2. **NOMADS cuts are south-first** (scanning mode 0x40). The decoder flips them, and a test pins this.
3. **Payload size is fine for the browser.** A 16×24

title: feat(mqtt): saved broker presets, reusable across MQTT forms (#5794 Phase 1)
body:
Phase 1 of #5794: saved MQTT broker presets. Phases 2 (traffic-direction badges) and 3 (overlap warnings) follow as separate PRs, as agreed in the issue.

## What it does
- **Admins save a broker as a preset** (name, host, port, TLS, username, password, optional root topic) from any Meshtastic MQTT form: the bridge **Settings** page, the device MQTT settings, and remote admin. **Save as preset** fills the dialog from the form; **Manage saved presets** edits, renames, duplicates and deletes them.
- **Saved presets appear as a second chip row, "My saved presets"**, under the built-in ones. Picking one fills the address, TLS and login. A root topic, when set, fills the device root topic or sets the bridge subscription to `<root>/#`.
- **Copied in, not linked.** A pick only edits the form. Editing or deleting a preset changes no source or radio already using its values.

## Security
- The table is **global** (`mqtt_broker_presets`, migration 211). This is a deliberate exception to the per-source rule, signed off in this session: one broker serves many sources.
- **Only admins** can write presets or see their username and password. Anyone holding `sources:write` or `configuration:write` on any source can list them **without the login** (`hasUsername` / `hasPassword` only). Everyone else gets 403, or 401 with no login.
- **Server-side fill.** When a non-admin picks a preset with a hidden login, the fields stay blank and the save carries `brokerPresetId`. The server (`services/mqttBrokerPresetFill.ts`) copies the login in only if the submitted address still reaches the preset's host, port and TLS setting. If it doesn't, the save is refused with `400 BROKER_PRESET_ENDPOINT_MISMATCH`, so nobody can aim a preset's login at a broker they control. The id is then removed before anything is stored or sent to a radio. A typed value always wins over the preset's.
- The fill is wired into `PUT`/`POST /api/sources` (mqtt_bridge, after the credential merge so a stored password still wins), `POST /api/config/mqtt`, and `setMQTTConfig` (admin-only, so there it never actually needs to fill).
- **Known exposure:** once a password is written to a radio, anyone who can read that device's MQTT config can read it. That holds for every device MQTT password today; the docs say so.
- Passwords are stored as typed, the same as `sources.config`. The table is in `BACKUP_TABLES` and `BACKUP_SECRET_TABLES` (protection: NONE), and in the migrate-db `TABLE_ORDER`.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime:** none. No packets; a device save still sends the one `set_module_config` it always did.
2. **Spam:** none. No events, notifications or automations.
3. **Timers:** none.

## Tests
- Repository and migration on **SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL** (containers up; 0 skipped in that file).
- Route harness: admin CRUD, case-insensitive unique names, validation, redaction for non-admins, 403/401 gates, and the bridge-save fill: fill, typed value wins, endpoint mismatch, TLS mismatch, deleted

title: fix(db): run maintenance on PostgreSQL/MySQL, prune audit_log, tune PG (#5870)
body:
Closes #5870

## Root cause
Cleanup only runs when `maintenanceEnabled` is on, and the only control for it (Settings → Database Maintenance) was hidden on PostgreSQL/MySQL, both in the section and in settings search. `databaseMaintenanceService` has supported all three backends for a long time (`vacuumAsync` handles PG and MySQL), so a Postgres install could never turn cleanup on. That is how production ended up with 1.75M `route_segments` rows, 942 MB of telemetry indexes and a 2.9 GB `audit_log`.

## Changes
- **Maintenance visible on every backend.** The SQLite gate is gone from `DatabaseMaintenanceSection` and `configSections`. It stays **off** until an admin enables it (agreed: no auto-enable, since the first run may delete a lot).
- **`audit_log` retention.** New `auditLogRetentionDays` setting (default **90**, 7–365, agreed), shown with the other retention fields and run by the nightly job. `cleanupOldAuditLogs` was already there but nothing called it, and it issued one `DELETE` per row; it now deletes in batches of 5,000 by id.
- **Migration 210.**
  - `idx_messages_source_channel_ts` on `messages(sourceId, channel, timestamp)`, all three backends. The MQTT-source channel list runs `COUNT`/`MAX(timestamp) … GROUP BY channel` over a source's messages, which was a full scan (likely the 5–10 s Channels load on MQTT sources).
  - PostgreSQL only: `autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = 0.05`, `autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor = 0.02` on `telemetry`, `route_segments`, `nodes`, `messages`, `audit_log`, `packet_log` (skips any that don't exist). These are storage parameters only: no rewrite, no blocking lock.
- **Docs** (`docs/development/database.md`): Postgres memory settings for the compose service (`shared_buffers`, `effective_cache_size`, `work_mem`, `shm_size`), how to check the cache hit ratio, enabling maintenance, and a one-off `REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY` / `VACUUM (ANALYZE)` after the first big cleanup.

## Not done, and why
- **No index dropped.** Each "0 scans" index in the report has a query that uses it: `route_segments(timestamp)` and `audit_log(timestamp)` serve the retention cutoff (which never ran), `route_segments(distanceKm)` serves the longest-segment ranking, `(fromNodeNum, toNodeNum)` the per-node segment lookup, `telemetry(nodeId)` and `nodes(updatedAt)` their reads. Zero scans on one instance means those pages and jobs didn't run there; the size is bloat that pruning plus one REINDEX removes.
- **REINDEX is not in a migration.** `REINDEX … CONCURRENTLY` can't run inside the migration transaction, and a plain REINDEX would lock the tables for minutes on a big instance. It is a documented one-off instead.

## After merge, on production
1. Settings → Database Maintenance: enable, check the retention values, **Run Maintenance Now** (the first run is the long one).
2. Run the REINDEX / VACUUM block from the docs.
3. Raise `shared_buffers` as documented and restart Postgres.

## Testing
- Migration 210: SQLite (idempotent, and `EXPL

title: feat(meshcore): Companion text CLI on fw 1.18.0 — local, catalog, remote (#5866, #5867, #5868)
body:
Closes #5866
Closes #5868
Closes #5867

## Protocol: the issue was wrong
#5866 proposed `CMD_SEND_TXT_MSG` + `TXT_TYPE_CLI_DATA` addressed to the companion's own key. The `companion-v1.18.0` source does something else:

- **Local CLI** is `CMD_RUN_CLI_COMMAND` (66) → `RESP_CODE_CLI_REPLY` (29), synchronous, no RF (`examples/companion_radio/MyMesh.cpp:1118`).
- It arrived with companion protocol **v14** (`FIRMWARE_VER_CODE`); 1.16 and 1.17 report 13. That is DeviceInfo's `fw ver` byte, so it is the gate.
- The over-the-air CLI is `TXT_TYPE_CLI_COMMAND` (3), run only when the target's contact for us has flag `0x10`. That is #5867, not this PR.
- The firmware verbs (`MyMesh::handleCommand`, `CommonRadioPrefs`, board hooks) are config get/set, `ver`, `board`, `reboot`, `poweroff`/`shutdown`. There is **no** `stats`, `clock`, `advert` or `neighbors`.

## What changed
- `run_cli` bridge command in the native backend (raw frame on the `rx` tap, under the radio-op lock, since the reply has no tag). Classified serial-only.
- `sendLocalCliCommand` on a Companion with protocol 14+ sends every line to the firmware, except `stats`/`clock`/`advert`/`advert.zerohop`/`help`/`version`, which stay on the shim. It reads the protocol byte once if the poller hasn't. Strips the firmware's `> ` value marker, caps lines at 170 bytes (frame size), and reads a timeout on `reboot`/`poweroff` as sent (they never answer).
- `poweroff` and `shutdown` join `DANGER_COMMAND_PATTERN` on both server and client.
- #5868: on protocol 14+ the Local Console shows Version, Stats, Clock, Radio, TX power, Time zone, Zero-hop advert, Help and a danger Reboot. WiFi verbs exist only on WiFi builds, so they are in the placeholder rather than buttons.
- Dev notes updated.

## Mesh impact
No new transmissions. None of the firmware CLI verbs transmit; `advert` still goes through the existing shim and floor. Receive-only mode still blocks only `advert`/`advert.zerohop`.

## #5867: Companion-to-Companion remote CLI
- **Permission toggle** in the contact panel (Companion contacts, `configuration:write`): sets ContactInfo.flags `0x10` via `set_contact_remote_cli`, read-modify-write keeping the other bits, then a read-back. `POST /nodes/:publicKey/remote-cli`. Disabled with a tooltip below protocol 14 or when the radio doesn't hold the contact. The flag isn't stored; it comes from the device contact table.
