title: feat(unified): All Channels view on Unified Messages, with channel tags (#5361)
body:
Closes #5361. Finishes #5654 by @Cryptoteep: their commit is kept as the first commit here, and a second commit fixes the two items from that review.

## What it does

**Unified Messages** has a new **All Channels** entry at the top of the channel list. It shows every channel you can read, from every source, in one feed. Each row carries a channel tag next to the existing source pills, so you can see which channel a message came in on and which sources heard it.

## Fixes on top of #5654

- **No DMs.** The page now sends `channel=__all__`. With no `channel`, the route takes the legacy path, which returns direct messages too. The legacy path is unchanged for existing callers.
- **Scrolling back works.** The legacy path reads only the newest `limit × 2` rows per source and then drops rows past the cursor, so history ran out after a page or two. The new path pages in SQL:
  - Meshtastic: one query over the reader's channel list with a `createdAt` cursor (`getMessagesBeforeInChannels`). The channel list is the filter, so a DM (`channel = -1`) or a channel the reader cannot open never loads.
  - MeshCore: channel traffic only (no DMs or room posts), paged by `createdAt` (`getRecentChannelMessages`). Rows are read one merge window past the cursor so a message that straddles it keeps its later receptions.
- Shared `ALL_CHANNELS_PARAM` constant moved to `src/utils/unifiedChannelFilter.ts` (a `.tsx` page may export only components under the lint ratchet).
- The mocked route test is replaced by a harness test (real auth, real SQL).

## Permissions

Same rules as the named-channel path: `messages:read` on a source opens all of its channels; without it, each channel needs its own `channel_N:read`. Virtual channels follow their own read list. DMs never appear in this view, whatever the grant.

## Mesh impact

None. Read-only; sends no packets, arms no timer, fires no notification.

## Tests

- `unifiedRoutes.allChannels.test.ts` (8, route harness): DMs left out, legacy form unchanged, paging through 60 rows at 10 per page, per-channel reader, `messages:read` reader, MeshCore channel-only, MeshCore paging, MeshCore per-channel reader.
- Full Vitest run: 2030 files, 31,249 tests pass, no unhandled errors. Both `tsc` projects clean. `lint:ci` clean.
- Live in the dev container against real data (Meshtastic TCP, MQTT bridge, MQTT broker, MeshCore): paged back 15 pages, 1,500 distinct messages, 0 DMs. The page shows the tags and requests `channel=__all__`.

title: feat(automation): trace MeshCore paths on a schedule, each path on its own interval (#5723)
body:
Closes #5723

## What
A new automation action, **Trace MeshCore paths on a schedule**: one step holds any number of paths (contacts), **each with its own interval** and hop hash width. The per-hop SNR lands in the Trace SNR history from #5722.

## Maintainer decisions (as built)
- **Scheduler:** per-path due times, checked each minute. The automation runs from a Schedule trigger of `* * * * *`; on each run the step traces only the paths that are due. No change to the engine's one-cron-per-automation model.
- **Limits:** a path runs **at most every 10 minutes**; one source sends **at most 12 scheduled traces in a rolling hour**. Up to 20 paths per step.
- **Persisted state.** A path's last run and the hourly count are stored per source (`tracePathScheduleState`, server-written only). A restart or saving the automation fires nothing early, and the stamp is written **before** the send, so a failed or unanswered trace still counts. Nothing retries. A path that is new runs on the next tick.
- The 10-minute floor is checked at save (server validator and builder) and again at run time, so a hand-edited config cannot go under it. The check-and-stamp is serialised per source, so concurrent runs cannot exceed the cap.

## Details
- **Action** `action.tracePathSchedule`: `paths: [{ publicKey, hashBytes: 'auto'|1|2, intervalMinutes, label? }]`, `sourceIds` (MeshCore only), `autoReturn`.
- **Hop hash width override.** `traceContactPath(Detailed)` takes `hashBytes`. A path is a list of key prefixes, so narrowing truncates; widening needs each hop's full key and works only when every hop matches exactly one contact. Otherwise nothing is sent and the step says why. Nothing is guessed.
- **Storage:** none added here. The reply arrives through #5722's passive capture with `initiated: true`.
- **Idle ticks are not logged.** A run in which every action had nothing due writes no run-log row (new `idleActions` on the eval context); a run that traced, hit the cap or failed is logged as usual, and Run Now is always logged. Without this a one-minute schedule would add 1,440 rows a day per automation.
- **Dry run (Test):** reports the path and neither sends nor uses up its interval.
- **TX gates:** the manager's own `requireTransmit()` applies; a TX-disabled source records a skip.
- **Builder:** a path-list editor (name, contact key, width, interval) with inline checks for a malformed key and a duplicate contact, and the airtime warning beside it.

## Where the issue was off
- It proposes `intervalSeconds`; the unit is minutes (the floor is 10 minutes).
- "User-settable byte length" cannot always be honoured: a stored 1-byte path can only be sent as 2-byte hops when each hop resolves to one contact (above).
- The issue's "option 2" (several cron jobs per automation) was not needed.

## Mesh impact
- **Airtime:** one trace per due path: a direct-route packet relayed by each hop, doubled with the return leg. Worst case 12 traces per source per hour, only for automations a u

title: feat(meshcore): capture every TRACE the radio hears and keep per-hop SNR history (#5722)
body:
Closes #5722

## What
MeshMonitor now stores the per-hop SNR from **every completed MeshCore TRACE a companion radio hears**, and shows it as a per-link history in Node Details. It is passive: nothing is sent.

## How it works
- **Capture.** The native backend used to listen for `TraceData` only while one of its own `trace_path` calls was waiting. It now keeps the corrected parser (#4786) and a listener for the whole session, and emits each push as a `trace_data` event flagged `initiated` when this backend sent that tag. The per-request `trace_path` call still resolves exactly as before (including auto-return).
- **Ingest** (`meshcoreTraceIngestService.ingest(sourceId, trace, localPublicKey)`): one function for both our own replies and overheard traces. **#5723's scheduled traces need no extra storage call**: their replies arrive through the same push with `initiated: true`.
- **Rows are directional.** Per firmware `Mesh::onRecvPacket`, each forwarding hop appends the SNR at which *it* heard the packet. So `pathSnrs[i]` is the SNR at hop `h[i]` receiving from `h[i-1]` (from the originator for `i = 0`), and the trailing byte is our own radio receiving from the last hop. One trace of N hops stores N + 1 rows: **receiver heard sender**.
- **Hash resolution never guesses.** A path hash is the first 1 or 2 bytes of a public key. It is resolved only when exactly one contact (or our own node) matches; otherwise the key is null and the candidate count is stored (0 = unknown, > 1 = ambiguous).
- **Dedup:** the same (tag, auth code) within 60 s is one trace per source: an in-memory window, plus a table check so a restart cannot double-store. **Each source keeps its own reception** of the same trace (per-source data rule).

## Storage: migration 201 `meshcore_hop_snr` (three backends, idempotent)
`sourceId, traceTag, authCode, hopIndex, hopCount, hashBytes, sender{PublicKey,Hash,Candidates}, receiver{PublicKey,Hash,Candidates}, snrQuarterDb, initiated, timestamp`.
- Indexed for per-link history and by time.
- MeshCore contacts are keyed by public key, so the ends are keys, not node numbers.
- Retention: 90 days, pruned at most every 6 h per source from the ingest path.
- In `BACKUP_TABLES` and the CLI table list; deleted with its source.

## Reading
`GET /api/sources/:id/meshcore/hop-snr?publicKey=&hours=` returns directional links with count, last/avg/min/max SNR and up to 120 points each. It is gated by the per-source **`traceroute:read`** grant (maintainer decision), and anonymous follows its grants. Registered in the MeshCore route classification guard.

## UI
**Trace SNR history** card in MeshCore Node Details: one row per link direction ("Hilltop heard this contact"), with the latest SNR, average and range, sample count, age and a small trend line. Unknown and shared hashes are labelled as such. Hidden without the grant or with no history.

## Where the issue was off
- It cites `meshtastic/MeshCore`; the firmware is `meshcore-dev/MeshCore`.
- "The fir

title: feat(map-analysis): add on-air waypoints from Map Analysis, with a per-source picker (#5685)
body:
Closes #5685

## What this does

Map Analysis could show waypoints but not make them. You can now add, edit and delete on-air waypoints there, and choose which source sends.

- **Tools → Add Waypoint.** Click the map, pick the sending source, fill in the existing waypoint editor, click Create.
- **Source picker** at the top of the editor. It lists only enabled Meshtastic radio sources the user holds `waypoints:write` on.
  - One such source: chosen for you, shown as text.
  - Several: you must choose, and Create stays off until you do. If the map's source filter leaves exactly one, that one is preselected.
  - The channel list and "Lock to this node" come from the picked source (#4341). Changing the source puts both back to their defaults and keeps everything else you typed.
- **Edit / Delete** in a waypoint's popup, for a radio source the user can write to. They act on the waypoint's own source and the editor names it. Both are disabled, with the reason, for a waypoint locked to another node. Delete keeps the existing "This will be broadcast to the mesh" confirmation and adds the sending source.
- **Tools → Add Local Marker** (#5686, never transmitted) through the same placement flow, with a picker of every source the user can write to. Edit / Delete in the marker popup too.

## Which sources can send

`src/server/routes/waypoints.ts` stores a row for any source but broadcasts only when the source's manager has `broadcastWaypoint`. Only `MeshtasticManager` has it, and its `sourceType` is `meshtastic_tcp`. The client mirrors that in `canSourceSendWaypoints` (`src/utils/waypointSources.ts`): type `meshtastic_tcp` and enabled. MQTT broker / bridge, MeshCore, MeshCore Observer and Reticulum sources are never offered, since a waypoint saved there would be stored and never sent. No server change.

## Design

- `usePinSources` — who may add a pin and where (permission × source type). Shared by the toolbar and the canvas.
- `usePinAuthoring` (Map Analysis) — placement state, the two editors, popup actions per source. The only waypoint writes are in `saveWaypoint` and `removeWaypoint`.
- `PinSourcePicker` (`src/components/map/`) — shared by both editors through an optional `sendingSource` / `storingSource` prop. The Nodes map passes neither and is unchanged.
- Placement reuses `LocalMarkerPlacementBridge` from #5717 as is (crosshair, click-through overlays per #4342).
- `useWaypoints` / `useMapMarkers` now export their plain calls (`createWaypoint(sourceId, …)` etc.) so a surface that picks the source per action can use them; the hooks call the same functions.
- `useSourceChannels(sourceId)` reads `/api/sources/:id/channels`, the existing route that applies per-channel read permission and never returns a PSK to a reader.
- `ToolbarMenuItem` gained `closesMenu`. Arming a pin tool closes the Tools menu: left open, Escape would close the menu and cancel the tool at once, and the click that dismissed the menu would also be the pick.

## Decisions

- **No def

title: feat(notifications): one notification when several sources hear the same packet (#5729)
body:
Refs #5729

First step of #5729: **cross-source dedup only.** The unified-config half of the issue stays open. Per-source notification settings are untouched: no settings migration, no new permission, no new setting.

## The fault

With two or more sources on one mesh, each source that hears a packet raises its own notification. A user with two gateways gets two alerts for one message; add an MQTT source and it is three.

## What this does

When two or more sources hear the same packet, a recipient gets **one** notification. Web Push then names every source that heard it.

- New `src/server/services/notificationDedup.ts`: one in-memory store, shared by all delivery channels, so they agree on what a duplicate is.
- Key: `(fromNodeNum, packetId, portnum)`, as the issue asks. Window: **60 s from the first copy, a constant** (`NOTIFICATION_DEDUP_WINDOW_MS`), not a setting in this step. It does not slide, so a stream of copies cannot hold an entry open.
- The caller that raises the event puts `dedup: { key }` on the payload. `messagePushNotifier` builds the key for every message (radio and MQTT use the same notifier, so an MQTT echo collapses with no extra code). A row with no packet id (the `Date.now()` fallback id) gets no key and is never deduped.
- Each delivery wrapper still runs **that source's** permission and filter for the recipient first, exactly as before. Only a copy that was about to be sent calls `claim()`. A filtered copy never uses up the event.

### Per recipient, and the two-source rule

State is per `(recipient, key)`, never per key. The list of sources a recipient sees holds only sources whose copy passed that recipient's own permission and filter. A user who can read one source never sees another source's name, id or deep link. Recipients:

| Channel | Recipient | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Web Push | user + browser endpoint | a phone subscribed on A and a laptop on B must each still get one |
| Apprise | user | a user's URLs are one target |
| Desktop app | the machine | it shows one notification, for the first user who passes; it never lists sources |

### What each channel does

| Channel | First copy | Later copies inside the window |
|---|---|---|
| Web Push | sent at once, with `tag` = the event, `renotify: false` | another source: one push with the same `tag`, `renotify: false`, `silent: true`, title re-rendered with `{{ sourceName }}` = `Hilltop, Valley` (the first source's template). Same source again: nothing |
| Apprise | sent at once | nothing; Apprise cannot change a delivered message |
| Desktop | shown at once | nothing; node-notifier cannot replace a shown notification |

The first notification is never delayed. `src/sw.ts` now passes `renotify` and `silent` through to `showNotification`; a browser still on the old service worker replaces by `tag` anyway.

If the first copy's delivery fails (push 5xx, Apprise error), the claim is released so another source's copy can still reach the user. That is not a retry: nothing is

title: fix(meshcore): honest delivery state for own DMs and room posts (#5682)
body:
Closes #5682

#5693 gave our own MeshCore **channel** messages a "Sent to radio" mark. This PR closes the same gap for **direct messages** and **room posts**, the last open item on the issue.

## What changes

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| DM, ack awaited | single tick, lost on the next refetch | **Sent to radio**, kept |
| DM, acked | double tick, lost on reload | double tick, kept across reload and restart |
| DM, no ack after all retries | "Delivery failed", lost on reload | **Not confirmed**, kept |
| DM from history | no mark | **Sent to radio**, or the stored ack outcome |
| Room post, any state | no mark at all | **Sent to radio** → double tick, or **Not confirmed** |
| Room post after a restart | dropped out of the Rooms view | stays a room post |

![DM marks](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/blob/454785cbf/docs/public/images/features/5682-dm-delivery-marks.png?raw=true)
![Room post marks](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/blob/454785cbf/docs/public/images/features/5682-room-post-delivery-marks.png?raw=true)
![Room post Delivery Details](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/blob/454785cbf/docs/public/images/features/5682-room-post-delivery-details.png?raw=true)

The screenshots show this branch's built frontend against the dev container's API through a read-only proxy. The dev container held no DM or room post of ours (its 1000-message pool was all received channel traffic), so the proxy added nine fixture rows to the `GET` responses and answered the room login itself. No request but `GET`s and the web login reached the container. Nothing went out on a radio.

## What each MeshCore message kind can and cannot know

Checked against MeshCore firmware `a366955cb2` (`examples/companion_radio/MyMesh.cpp`, `examples/simple_room_server/MyMesh.cpp`).

| Kind | Radio accepted it | It went out on the air | The far end got it | A person read it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Channel** (#5693) | Yes: `Ok` to the send | Only if a repeater's re-flood is heard | No. Channels have no ack | No |
| **Direct message** | Yes: `RESP_CODE_SENT` with an ack CRC and a timeout estimate | Only through the ack | Yes, when `PUSH_CODE_SEND_CONFIRMED` (0x82) carries that CRC: the recipient's radio got it | No |
| **Room post** | Yes: same `RESP_CODE_SENT` (a room post is a DM to the room server) | Only through the ack | Yes, when 0x82 arrives: the **room server** stored the post | No, and not which members fetched it |

What none of them can know:

- **That the radio transmitted.** The companion has no transmit report (see #5693). "Sent to radio" claims only that the radio took the message.
- **Why an ack did not come.** No ack reads **Not confirmed**, never "failed" or "lost": the message may have arrived with the ack lost on the way back. For a room post there is one more cause the radio cannot tell apart: the room server sends no ack to a client that is not logged in, or that has guest (read-only) access, and drops the post.
- **A radio refusal as a s

title: feat(aircraft): ask a newly flagged aircraft for its position, opt-in, 2 an hour per source (#5704)
body:
Closes #5704

## What
When a node is first flagged as a **likely aircraft**, MeshMonitor can ask it for its position so the trail shows the flight instead of one or two points.

## Maintainer decisions (as built)
- **Per-source, opt-in, default off:** Settings → Node Display → **Ask new aircraft for their position**, next to the other aircraft settings, with the cost beside it. Needs likely-aircraft detection on.
- **3 requests at t = 0, 2 and 4 minutes**, through the source that classified the node, on the node's channel, using the existing `sendPositionRequest` path and all of its TX gates.
- **Cap: 2 aircraft per source per rolling hour** (≤ 6 requests). The start times are stored per source (`aircraftPositionRequestStarts`, server-written only), so a restart or a settings save cannot reset the cap. The check-and-stamp is serialised, so simultaneous transitions cannot exceed it.
- **Only on the false→true transition.** The service listens to the existing `node:aircraft` event, which is emitted for live positions only, never for the startup backfill. So a node already flagged at boot does not fire, and a node must stop being flagged and be flagged again to be asked again.
- **A sequence in flight is in memory only.** A restart drops it; nothing resumes or fires on boot.
- **Stops early** when the node is no longer flagged (landed, aged out, or marked not-aircraft by hand), is ignored or deleted, the source disconnects, or a send is refused (TX disabled / receive-only).
- **Never:** the local node; MQTT, MeshCore or Reticulum sources (only `meshtastic_tcp` sources can send this).
- Sends are tagged `origin: 'automation'`, so a bridge with "Don't uplink MeshMonitor automation traffic" keeps them off the upstream broker. The call site is registered in the pinned send-callers test.

## Firmware finding (the issue's open question 1)
`PositionModule::allocReply()` on firmware `develop` keeps **one** `lastSentReply` timestamp and skips any reply within 3 minutes of it. The throttle is **global on the responder, not per requester**.
- With 0/2/4, the t = 2 min request gets a reply only when the first got none; t = 4 min is past the limit. A 0/3/6 schedule would get three replies. The maintainer's 0/2/4 is kept.
- The issue's "multi-source parallel pings" idea cannot add samples, for the same reason. Not built.

## Logging
Each request writes an info log line ("Asked likely aircraft !xxxxxxxx for its position on <source> (n/3)"); a skipped sequence at the cap writes a debug line. There is no run log for non-automation features, and the trail itself shows the result.

## Mesh impact
- **Airtime:** one request packet per send, relayed up to the hop limit, plus the node's reply. Worst case 6 requests per source per hour, only when a source opts in.
- **Timers:** no recurring timer; three one-shot timers per sequence.
- **Save or restart:** neither re-arms anything. The hourly cap is persisted; a restart drops in-flight work and sends nothing.
- **Feedback
author: Yeraze

title: feat(mqtt): per-bridge skip raise, text in the raise picker, subscription-scope docs (#5708, #5709, #5718)
body:
Closes #5708
Closes #5709
Closes #5718

Three issues on the same MQTT hop-policy code and docs page.

## #5708: per-bridge "Skip raise" and docs
- **New per-bridge option** (bridge **Settings → MQTT Bridge Configuration**): **Skip raise on packets from this bridge**, stored as `skipRaise: true`, off by default. Packets that bridge brings into its parent broker are never raised by the broker's "Raise hop count for backhaul"; **the clamp still applies**.
- **How it reaches both radio egress paths.** A bridge is a separate source that republishes into the parent broker, so at the point where the raise is applied the broker no longer knows which bridge a packet came from. The bridge now calls `parentBroker.markSkipRaise(from, packetId)` just before it republishes. Both egress paths, Aedes `authorizeForward` (radios subscribed over MQTT) and `handleLinkedBrokerLocalPacket` (TCP-linked devices), already go through the one `transformForwardedPayload`, which now drops only the raise for a marked packet. Marks live 60 s, capped at 5,000 entries (the oldest go first).
- **Docs:** the asymmetry with `mqtt.meshtastic.org` (what you send up is not raised for anyone else; what comes down is raised for you) and the new option, under *Raise hop count for backhaul* and in the bridge Caveats.

## #5709: text messages in the raise picker
- **Maintainer decision: broadcasts and DMs.** `TEXT_MESSAGE_APP` is added to `RAISEABLE_PORTNUMS` on the server, the client and the save validator, labelled "Text messages (including DMs)" (they share one portnum). Traceroutes stay excluded. `MAX_RAISE_TARGET` stays 3. Opt-in: existing configs are unchanged.
- **Warning beside the checkbox** when Text is ticked: raising text is loud, and to watch channel utilisation.

## #5718: "Scope your subscriptions" docs
New section beside the bridge's Upstream topics row: the topic ladder, pick the narrowest topic, why it matters with radios behind the broker, and the public-broker zero-hop note. No UI change.

## Where the issues were off
- #5708 says the raise is "global per-source without per-bridge opt-out" and suggests plumbing a bridge-level override "into the call site that handles that bridge's deliveries". There is no such call site: the broker cannot tell which bridge a packet came from, so the bridge has to mark its packets (above).
- #5709's rationale comment in the code ("text … routing-layer concerns") is replaced. The reason text is now allowed is undoing an upstream zero-hop, not firmware hop scaling.
- The issues' line references held.

## Mesh impact
- **Skip raise** only removes transmissions.
- **Text raise** adds airtime when an operator opts in: each raised text or DM floods up to the target (≤ 3) hops locally, and text payloads are larger than position or telemetry. The UI and docs both warn about this. Encrypted packets (unreadable portnum) are still never raised.
- No new timers or scheduled sends.
- **No loop.** A raised text that a radio rebroadcasts and a gateway

title: feat(aircraft): mark a node as not aircraft / aircraft by hand (#5715)
body:
Closes #5715

## What

Node Details → **Actions** gets three entries, each with the aircraft icon:

- **Mark as not aircraft** — shown while the node is flagged.
- **Mark as aircraft** — shown while the classifier says it is not one.
- **Clear aircraft override** — shown while the node has a manual mark or a fixed anchor.

They need `nodes:write` on that node's source (checked server-side with `sourceIdFrom: 'body'`, `requireSourceId`), are hidden on MeshCore / Reticulum sources, and every accepted change is audit-logged (`aircraft_manual_mark`: user, source, node, mode, previous mark).

`POST /api/aircraft/mark { sourceId, nodeNum, mode: 'not_aircraft' | 'aircraft' | 'clear' }`

## Rules

| Mode | Effect | Ends when |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `not_aircraft` | Anchors at the node's current **effective** position (the one the classifier and the sweep's fixed rule use), clears the flag. | The node moves more than 1 km (`AIRCRAFT_FIXED_RELEASE_M`), someone clears it, or detection is turned off for the source. No usable position → `400 AIRCRAFT_NO_POSITION`. |
| `aircraft` | Forces `likelyAircraft = true` whatever the altitude says; drops any fixed anchor. | Someone clears it (or marks it not-aircraft), or detection is turned off. **It holds until cleared.** |
| `clear` | Drops the manual mark and any fixed anchor, manual or automatic. The classifier decides again. | — |

**Why "aircraft" holds until cleared, with no "seen on the ground" release:** the reason to mark by hand is that the altitude/terrain data is wrong for this node. Any automatic release would have to trust that same data, and would undo the mark on the next position packet.

**Age-out and the manual aircraft mark:** the sweep's stationary "reclassify as fixed" pass skips a node marked `aircraft` (else a parked drone would lose the mark within the hour). The age-out pass itself still applies, as for any aircraft: not heard for N hours → ignored or deleted, per the source's setting.

**Other rules**

- A mark never fires `trigger.becameLikelyAircraft`. The route writes the verdict, recomputes once from stored values (no network), and queues a job with a new reason `'manual'` that never emits. Queue priority is `position > manual > backfill`.
- Turning detection off for a source clears manual marks with every other classification (as it already did the fixed anchor). The route answers `409 AIRCRAFT_DETECTION_DISABLED` while it is off.
- The audit row holds no coordinates: the anchor may be a private position override.

## Storage

Migration **200** adds three nullable columns to `nodes` (SQLite / PostgreSQL / MySQL, idempotent via the shared helpers):

- `aircraftManualMark` — `'not_aircraft' | 'aircraft'`
- `aircraftManualMarkAt` — ms epoch
- `aircraftManualMarkBy` — `users.id`

Why a migration, when the issue said none was needed: the `aircraftFixed*` anchor cannot say who set it, so "marked by you" vs "reclassified as fixed" had nowhere to live; and every other aircraft column

title: feat(pki): Avoid PKI mode — channel-encrypted data requests, DMs untouched (#5711)
body:
Closes #5711

Adds a third Reliable PKI mode, **Avoid PKI**, beside Off and As needed (global default in **Global Settings → Security**, per-source override on a Meshtastic source's **Settings → Reliable PKI**, same controls). In Avoid PKI mode, telemetry, remote LocalStats and neighbor-info requests go out **channel-encrypted** on the node's channel, so the node does not need our public key to read them. DMs, waypoints and remote admin are unchanged.

Help text beside the control when Avoid PKI is in effect: *"Requests and their replies are readable by anyone on that channel. DMs are not affected."*

## Firmware finding: the radio overrides `pki_encrypted = false`

Read from `meshtastic/firmware` `develop`, checked against v2.5.20, v2.6.11, v2.7.15 and v2.7.26.

- `Router.cpp` `perhapsEncode` → `wouldEncryptWithPKC`: the radio PKI-encrypts **every** unicast it originates to a node whose key it holds, except `TRACEROUTE_APP`, `NODEINFO_APP`, `ROUTING_APP`, `POSITION_APP`. The client's `pki_encrypted` flag can only *force* PKI; `false` (the default) is not a request for channel encryption. The only exceptions are ham mode (`owner.is_licensed`, turns off all encryption) and, since 2.7, channels **named** `serial` / `gpio`.
- 2.5.x and 2.6.x had one more exception: `!(p->pki_encrypted != true && p->channel > 0)`, so a request on a *secondary* channel skipped PKI. 2.7 removed it. The primary channel never had it.
- So none of "set `pki_encrypted=false`", "pick a channel", or "clear the PKI flag on a `want_response` request" works on current firmware. A broadcast with `dest` would make **every** node in range answer (`MeshModule` treats a broadcast `want_response` as addressed to everyone), which is a mesh flood, so I did not use it.
- **What does work:** `Router::send` only calls `perhapsEncode` on a `decoded` packet; a packet that arrives already `encrypted` goes out as is (the relay path). `PhoneAPI::handleToRadioPacket` / `MeshService::handleToRadio` accept an encrypted `MeshPacket` from the client (same in 2.5.20 and 2.7.26), keep a non-zero client packet id, and set `from` to our node number. So MeshMonitor encrypts the `Data` with the channel key exactly as `perhapsEncode` would and hands the radio the ciphertext.
- Receiving side: the remote decrypts it like any channel packet. `develop` rejects a channel-encrypted unicast only for `TEXT_MESSAGE_APP` ("Rejecting legacy DM"), which is another reason DMs stay PKI. The reply comes back PKI if the node holds our key, channel-encrypted if not; our radio reads both.

New module `src/server/utils/channelEncryption.ts` mirrors the firmware: `Channels::getKey` (1-byte shorthand expansion incl. `n-1` bump, zero padding, secondary-without-PSK borrows the primary key), `Channels::getName` (empty name → modem preset name, or `Custom`), `Channels::generateHash`, AES-CTR with the `CryptoEngine::initNonce` nonce, and the `bitfield` (`ok_to_mqtt`, `want_response`) `perhapsEncode` sets on packets we originate.

title: fix(notifications): Emoji Reactions off also mutes protocol tapbacks and keycap reactions (#5720)
body:
Closes #5720

## Problem
With **Notifications → Emoji Reactions** off (`notifyOnEmoji=false`), tapbacks still pushed notifications. The filter only looked at the message text, through its own regex.

## Fix
1. **Protocol flag.** The push notifier now passes `isTapback: message.emoji === 1` through the filter context (Web Push, Apprise and desktop). The filter treats a flagged tapback as a reaction whatever its text. This is the authoritative check.
   - **Where the issue was off:** it proposed `emoji > 0 **or** replyId > 0`. A normal text reply also has `replyId`, so that rule would have muted every reply. Only the `emoji` flag is used.
2. **Text fallback uses the app's shared `isEmoji`** (the same test the UI uses to decide a row is a tapback) instead of a private regex. Whitespace between emoji is ignored, as before.
3. **`isEmoji` now accepts:**
   - keycaps (`1️⃣`, `#️⃣`, with or without VS-16), which is what the reporter's iOS app sent;
   - tag-sequence flags (England, Scotland).

   The old private regex also stopped at U+1FAD6 (missing 🫡 and others); the shared one already handled those. Bare digits stay text.

## Side effects of the shared change (intended)
- A keycap tapback now renders as a reaction in the UI instead of a reply (`messageReplies.isTapbackMessage`).
- The tapback-emoji settings input and sender-avatar emoji detection accept keycaps.
- Translation skips keycap-only text.
- One old test (#1678) asserted `isEmoji('1️⃣') === false` because keycaps were "not commonly used as tapbacks". This report shows phone apps do send them, so the test now expects `true`.
- Symbols that are not pictographic (e.g. `✓` U+2713), which the old private range matched, no longer count as emoji-only.

## Tests
- `notificationFiltering.test.ts`:
  - a protocol tapback is filtered even with non-emoji text;
  - keycap, spaced and newer emoji are filtered without the flag;
  - a real text reply and a number are never filtered;
  - a tapback is kept when the setting is on.
- `text.test.ts`: keycaps, an England flag and 🫡 are emoji; `1`, `42`, `#` and `1️⃣ ok` are not.
- tsc (both configs) clean; `src/utils`, `src/server/utils` and `src/server/services` suites pass (7,703); `lint:ci` clean.

## Mesh impact
None. This only decides which received messages notify.

title: feat(map): local map markers, per source, never transmitted (#5686)
body:
Closes #5686

## What
**Local map markers:** planning notes on the map (candidate repeater sites, survey points, aid stations) that are stored in MeshMonitor and **never transmitted**. Hundreds of them cost no airtime.

## Maintainer decision: per source, shared with readers
- A marker belongs to one source (`sourceId` NOT NULL; no "global" rows).
- **Permission:** reuses the per-source **`waypoints`** resource: `waypoints:read` on the source to see its markers, `waypoints:write` to add, edit or delete. Markers sit beside waypoints on the same maps, so a separate resource would only add a grid column users must remember to tick. Every check is scoped to the path's source (`sourceIdFrom: 'params.id'`); a grant on another source does not help. Anonymous follows the anonymous account's grants.
- **Unified views** (Dashboard all-sources, Map Analysis) show markers from every source the viewer can read (a 403 reads as an empty list); editing happens on the source's own map.

## Never transmitted
`mapMarkerRoutes.ts` imports no source manager, registry, waypoint service or queue. A test spies on the registry through create/read/update/delete (zero calls) and checks the module's imports. Markers are REST-only, with no WebSocket events (so no socket gate is needed).

## Schema: migration 199 `map_markers` (all three backends, idempotent)
`id, sourceId, label, description, latitude, longitude, altitude?, icon, color, createdByUserId?, createdAt (ms), updatedAt (ms)`, indexed on `sourceId`.
- `icon` / `color` are **keys** from fixed sets (`src/types/mapMarker.ts`): six icons, six colours that map to `--color-*` tokens, so markers follow the theme and the colour lint stays clean.
- Classified in `BACKUP_TABLES` (user data) and the CLI migration table list.
- Deleting a source deletes its markers; a node purge does not (same as Reliable PKI state).

## Limits and validation
- **Cap: 1,000 markers per source** → `409 MARKER_LIMIT_REACHED` (a site survey wants a few hundred; the cap keeps one source's layer and its GET bounded).
- Label ≤ 64 chars, notes ≤ 2,000, lat/lon ranges, altitude −1,000…100,000 m, icon/colour from the sets; `fail()` codes `INVALID_LABEL`, `INVALID_POSITION`, `INVALID_ICON`, `INVALID_COLOR`, ….

## UI
- **Layer:** an outline glyph in a dashed ring (a waypoint is a filled disc with an emoji), with the tooltip/popup "Local marker — not sent to the mesh". It is on its own pane at z 590, just under Leaflet's marker pane, so a waypoint or node at the same spot always draws on top. The issue asked for "above nodes, below waypoints", but nodes and waypoints share one pane, so that ordering would mean moving one of them.
- **Toggles:** **Show Local Markers** in **both** Map Features panels (NodesTab and DashboardMap; per-browser, default on, disabled in 3D like Waypoints) and a **Local Markers** layer in Map Analysis.
- **Authoring** on the source's Nodes map: **+ Local marker**, click the spot (Escape cancels), then the editor (label, notes, l

title: fix(automations): offer the suggested template and warn when a step sends nothing (#5697)
body:
Closes #5697

## Problem
On the **Send a message** action, the Message field's trigger-specific placeholder (`MOVEMENT_MESSAGE_HINTS` on Left home / Became mobile / Likely aircraft) reads like a saved message. Users saved without typing, the stored text was `""`, and every run hit the #5636 empty-send rule: it fired and sent nothing, with only a routine-looking line in the run log.

## Fix
- **Use suggested template.** A field whose placeholder is a complete template (new catalog flag `suggestTemplate`) shows a button while it is empty. It copies the exact suggestion, tokens intact, into the field as its real value, marks the form dirty, keeps focus in the field with the caret at the end, and disappears once the field has text, so typed text is never replaced. Touch-sized; has an accessible name; i18n.
- **Placeholders look like hints:** italic, in `--color-text-subtle`, both in the token field and in plain inputs, in both themes.
- **Builder warning.** A step that will send nothing shows "This step will send nothing: …" inside the block, with a one-tap **Use suggested template**. A notification with an empty body (it still sends, with only its title) shows "Check this step: …".
- **Save.** Empty is not invalid (the user may be drafting), so Save asks once: "Some steps will not send what you expect: … Save anyway?" Cancel returns to the form.
- **Server agrees.** `validateAutomationGraph` returns the same finding as a warning (shared `emptySendFinding` in `src/types/automation.ts`), and POST `/api/automations`, PUT `/:id` and POST `/import` include `warnings` in the response, so API and import callers see what the builder shows. Nothing is rejected.
- **Runs and Trace.** A step held back by the empty-send rule now shows as **nothing sent**, with a warning icon and colour, instead of "action ran". Run status is unchanged (#5636: the run stays `completed`).

## Per-field decision
| Field | Placeholder | Button | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Send a message → Message | generic + 3 movement templates | yes | the reported trap; a complete message |
| Send a notification → Body | generic + 3 movement templates | yes | same movement hints |
| Send a notification → Title | "MeshMonitor alert" | yes | a usable title |
| Tapback → Emoji | 👍 | no | an absent emoji already sends 👍; a blank one is warned about |
| DM to node #, Target node, Value, Region, Waypoint name/lat/lon, Expires, etc. | "e.g. …" / "blank = …" | no | examples or explanations, not templates |

## Where the issue was off
- It names only `action.sendMessage`; `action.notify` Body uses the same `MOVEMENT_MESSAGE_HINTS` and had the same trap.
- An empty notification body does not send nothing: the title defaults to "MeshMonitor automation", so it sends a title-only notification. The builder says that rather than "sends nothing".
- The tapback placeholder is not a trap: an absent emoji sends 👍.

## Not changed
- The #5636 empty-send rule and run statuses.
- Saved automations are not migrated or a

title: fix(config): module-config saves update the module cache
body:
No issue: found during #5713.

## The fault

`GET /api/config/current` serves the manager's cached `actualDeviceConfig` / `actualModuleConfig`. A local save writes that cache, and when the firmware does not reboot, nothing else corrects it until the next reconnect.

- **`setNeighborInfoConfig` wrote the wrong bucket.** It called `updateCachedDeviceConfig('neighborinfo', …)`, but NeighborInfo is a `ModuleConfig` section, read from `moduleConfig.neighborInfo`. The Configuration tab kept showing the old values. This is the bug #5713 fixed for MQTT.
- **Several sections merged where the firmware replaces.** `AdminModule::handleSetConfig` / `handleSetModuleConfig` assign every section whole (`config.lora = validatedLora`, `moduleConfig.telemetry = c.payload_variant.telemetry`, …). So a field the save leaves out is cleared on the node. A merged cache kept it.
- **Four device saves never touched the cache.** Those are device, power, display and bluetooth. LoRa always applies live (`requiresReboot = false`), and device/power/display skip the reboot when no reboot-only field changed (e.g. `tzdef`, `nodeInfoBroadcastSecs`, `screenOnSecs`). For those saves no config download follows, so the reload showed pre-save values.

## Audit

Bucket comes from `CONFIG_TYPES` (`src/server/constants/configTypes.ts`) and the protobuf (`Config` vs `ModuleConfig`). Reboot behaviour comes from firmware `develop` `AdminModule.cpp`.

| Save path | Protobuf | Cache before | Cache now | Reboots after save? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `setDeviceConfig` | `Config.device` | none | device `device`, replace | only if role/rebroadcast/GPIO changed |
| `setLoRaConfig` | `Config.lora` | device `lora`, merge | device `lora`, **replace** | never (applies live) |
| `setNetworkConfig` | `Config.network` | device `network`, merge | device `network`, **replace** | yes |
| `setPositionConfig` | `Config.position` | device `position`, merge | device `position`, **replace** | yes |
| `setPowerConfig` | `Config.power` | none | device `power`, replace | only if a sleep/INA field changed |
| `setDisplayConfig` | `Config.display` | none | device `display`, replace | only if screen-on/flip/oled/mode changed |
| `setBluetoothConfig` (restore only) | `Config.bluetooth` | none | device `bluetooth`, replace | yes |
| `setMQTTConfig` | `ModuleConfig.mqtt` | module `mqtt`, replace (#5713) | unchanged | yes on `develop` |
| `setNeighborInfoConfig` | `ModuleConfig.neighbor_info` | **device** `neighborinfo`, merge | **module `neighborInfo`, replace** | yes |
| `setTelemetryConfig` | `ModuleConfig.telemetry` | module `telemetry`, merge | module `telemetry`, **replace** | yes |
| `setGenericModuleConfig` (serial, extnotif, storeforward, rangetest, cannedmsg, audio, remotehardware, ambientlighting, detectionsensor, paxcounter, statusmessage, trafficmanagement, tak, meshbeacon) | `ModuleConfig.*` | module `<field>`, replace (#5045) | unchanged | statusmessage, meshbeacon: never; others: yes |

title: fix(config): local MQTT save keeps location consent and map report settings
body:
No issue: found while doing #5707, which fixed the same class of bug on the remote-admin MQTT form. This PR fixes the **local** Device Configuration > MQTT form (`POST /api/config/mqtt`).

## The fault

Firmware replaces the node's whole MQTT struct with what Save sends, so any field the form drops or misreads gets written to the node.

1. **Location consent wiped.** The form never loaded or sent `map_report_settings.should_report_location` (fw 2.6.8+), so every local save turned it off. (`ConfigurationTab.tsx` built `mapReportSettings` from interval and precision only.)
2. **Map report settings zeroed with map reporting off.** Save sent `mapReportSettings: mqttMapReportingEnabled ? {...} : undefined`, so a save with map reporting off reset the interval and precision on the node to 0.
3. **Stored precision 0 loaded as 14.** `getCurrentConfig()` spread the decoded MQTTConfig, which left `mapReportSettings` a protobufjs Message. `res.json()` runs its `toJSON`, which drops 0 and false, so the browser got no `positionPrecision`, and `?? 14` loaded it as 14.
4. **Found on the way: a local save cached into the wrong bucket.** `DeviceAdminService.setMQTTConfig` called `updateCachedDeviceConfig('mqtt', …)`, but the form reads `actualModuleConfig.mqtt`, so a reload after Save showed the old values until the node resent its config.

## Fix

- `getCurrentConfig()` now returns `formatAdminMqttConfig(moduleConfig.mqtt)` (from #5707): all 11 fields, stated, as plain values. The admin `load-config` route already used it, and formatting twice gives the same result.
- The local Save builds its payload with `buildAdminMqttSavePayload` (from #5707), so it always sends every field, map report settings included. The builder now takes `Omit<MQTTConfigState, 'loadedForNodeNum'>`, so both forms share one mapping; no third mapping was added.
- New **Report Location** checkbox under Map Reporting on the local form, with the existing `mqtt_config.map_report_location*` strings. It counts toward the save bar's change check and Dismiss.
- Precision loads with `?? 0`; the initial state is 0 too. The zero hint (`0 = firmware default (14 bits, about 1.5 km). Save sends 0.`) was already on the local form; I checked that it shows.
- `setMQTTConfig` now calls `updateCachedModuleConfig('mqtt', config, 'replace')`, matching the firmware's whole-struct replace (#5045).

## Field table (local path, `module_config.proto` MQTTConfig)

| Field | Tag | Load before | Save before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| enabled | 1 | ok | ok | ok |
| address | 2 | ok | ok | ok |
| username | 3 | ok | ok | ok |
| password | 4 | ok | ok | ok |
| encryption_enabled | 5 | ok (`=== true`, the `!== false` bug was already fixed here) | ok | ok, pinned by a test |
| json_enabled | 6 | ok | ok | ok |
| tls_enabled | 7 | ok (#5700) | ok | ok |
| root | 8 | ok | ok | ok |
| proxy_to_client_enabled | 9 | ok | ok | ok |
| map_reporting_enabled | 10 | ok | ok | ok |
| map_report_settings.publish_interval_secs | 11

title: fix(map-analysis): phone-width inspector and time slider clear of map controls
body:
Two Map Analysis layout faults found while checking #5710. No issue exists for them.

## The faults

1. **Detail pane on a phone.** `.map-analysis-inspector` is a fixed 340px flex column with no phone rule. At 390px wide the map got about 50px until the user folded the pane.
2. **Time slider over the Map controls column.** The slider is centred on the whole canvas at z-index 2000, so with the Map controls panel open it sat over the panel's lower end.

## What changed

**Detail pane (phone layout, `MOBILE_LAYOUT_MEDIA_QUERY` / `useIsMobileLayoutViewport()`):**
- With nothing selected, the pane renders nothing: no empty placeholder, no expand rail. The map gets the full width.
- A selection (node, segment, neighbour link, trail) opens it as a **docked sheet**:
  - portrait: under the map, full width, `max-height: 45%`, scrolls inside;
  - short landscape: beside the map, `min(300px, 40%)` wide.
- Docked rather than overlaid, so the time slider, the Map controls sheet and the tool column, which all position against the canvas, stay clear of it. The canvas shrinks, and BaseMap's existing ResizeObserver redraws the map.
- Its close button (X) dismisses the sheet for that selection only. The next map click opens it again. The persisted `inspectorOpen` flag belongs to the desktop column and is untouched, so a pane folded on desktop does not hide selections on the phone.
- Desktop is unchanged: same 340px column, collapse arrow and empty state.
- Styles live in a new `AnalysisInspectorPanel.module.css` (the body's flex direction plus the `.sheet` variant); content styles stay in `map-analysis.css`.

**Time slider:**

title: fix(map-analysis): keep tool panels open across layout changes and clear of map controls
body:
Two Map Analysis follow-ups found while checking #5706. No issue was filed for these.

## 1. Tool panels "closed" when the viewport crossed the phone/desktop boundary

**Cause.** Nothing closed. No layout branch remounts the tool panels, no tool selection resets, and every panel keeps its state: in a live browser, a MutationObserver recorded no DOM removals during the resize. But on desktop the Map controls panel (`.map-sidebar`, z-index 1001) is usually open, and `MapSidebar` reads `useIsMobileLayoutViewport()` only for its *first* collapsed state. Resize into the phone layout and the open column becomes a full sheet over the map pane (60% of it in landscape), on top of the Site Planner and GNSS DOP panels (z-index 1000). The panel looked closed, and Tools still showed it checked, so clicking Tools closed it for real.

A second thing looks the same while testing: switching DevTools device mode **with touch emulation** reloads the page, and all tool state is transient React state. A plain resize or a phone rotation does not reload. This PR leaves reload behaviour alone (see "Not changed" below).

**Fix.** `MapSidebar` folds an open panel when the layout crosses into mobile, and restores the saved preference when it crosses back. The change is in memory only, so a resize never overwrites the user's saved choice. Opening the sheet again on the phone still works. This applies to every `MapSidebar` user (Dashboard and Nodes maps too). They had the same sheet-over-map problem, and "mobile starts collapsed" is already their default on load.

## 2. Tool panels under the open Map controls panel

#5706 moved only the Site Planner, with `:global(.map-sidebar) ~ .sitePlanner` and the controls panel's 10px/300px copied into its module. Checking each tool on desktop with the controls open:

| Tool | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Site Planner | beside controls (#5706) | beside controls, via the shared column |

title: fix(admin): remote MQTT save keeps client proxy and map reporting
body:
No issue: found during #5700.

## The fault

Admin Commands → Module Configuration → MQTT sends the node a whole `MQTTConfig`, and firmware replaces its struct with what it gets. The load reply and the form carried only the broker fields (TLS joined in #5700). So every remote Save turned off:

- client proxy (`proxy_to_client_enabled`)
- map reporting (`map_reporting_enabled`)
- the map report settings (`publish_interval_secs`, `position_precision`, `should_report_location` — the location consent flag)

Two more faults in the same path:

- **Encryption loaded as on when the node had it off.** The load used `encryptionEnabled !== false`; proto3 leaves `false` off the wire and a decoded protobuf.js field reads null, so a save turned encryption back on.
- **Save before Load wrote defaults over the node.** Nothing stopped it, and after switching nodes the form still held the previous node's config.

## Field table (`protobufs/meshtastic/module_config.proto` `MQTTConfig`)

| Tag | Field | Loaded before | Saved before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | enabled | yes | yes | yes |
| 2 | address | yes | yes | yes |
| 3 | username | yes | yes | yes |
| 4 | password | yes | yes | yes |
| 5 | encryption_enabled | wrong (elided false read as true) | yes | yes, `=== true` |
| 6 | json_enabled (deprecated) | yes | yes | yes |
| 7 | tls_enabled | yes (#5700) | yes (#5700) | yes |
| 8 | root | yes | yes | yes |
| 9 | proxy_to_client_enabled | **no** | **no** | yes, checkbox |
| 10 | map_reporting_enabled | **no** | **no** | yes, checkbox |
| 11.1 | map_report_settings.publish_interval_secs | **no** | **no** | yes, number |
| 11.2 | map_report_settings.position_precision | **no** | **no** | yes, number (10–19, or 0 = default) |
| 11.3 | map_report_settings.should_report_location | **no** | **no** | yes, checkbox |

## Design

- **The form shows the fields** rather than carrying them through out of sight, matching the device MQTT page: Proxy to Client, Map Reporting, and under Map Reporting the interval, precision (same `NumberInput` bounds and zero hint) and a Report Location checkbox. The device page has no Report Location control; see below.
- `src/server/utils/adminMqttConfig.ts` builds the `load-config` MQTT reply for both the local and remote branches (they had two copies).
- `src/components/admin-commands/mqttSavePayload.ts` builds the Save message with every field. Map report settings go out even while map reporting is off, so the node keeps them.
- **Unloaded guard:** `mqtt.loadedForNodeNum` is stamped by the load applier and cleared on node switch, the same rule as security (#4736). Save stays disabled, with a warning line and tooltip, until this node's MQTT config is loaded; the handler refuses too. Before this, Save was enabled with no load.

## Local device MQTT save (Configuration tab), report only, not changed here

It sends every field but one: **`map_report_settings.should_report_location` is never loaded or sent**, so each local save clears loca

title: fix(site-planner): clear the old ring on a new origin; keep map controls off the panel
body:
Two Site Planner faults found while reviewing #5698 (#5687). No issue exists for them.

## 1. A new origin left the old ring drawn

Clicking a new spot moved the transmitter marker but left the previous prediction ring, the result summary and the shape notices on screen. The ring then belonged to a site that was no longer selected.

**Fix (`SitePlannerPanel.tsx`):**
- When the origin's coordinates change, the panel clears the ring (`onCoverage(null)`), the summary, the notices, any error and the running state. Picking the same spot again keeps the result.
- A reply that lands after the origin moved is dropped (request sequence + origin key check), so a slow request can no longer draw the old site's ring under the new marker. Clear also cancels an in-flight reply.
- **Choice on other inputs:** editing frequency, heights, power, gain, sensitivity or radius does **not** clear the ring, since comparing a 10 m mast with a 20 m one needs the old ring on screen. The panel (and the folded bar) shows "Inputs changed since this ring was drawn. Predict again to update it." until Predict runs again. The ring can therefore be stale against the inputs, but never against the origin.

## 2. The open Map controls panel covered the planner

Both panels are children of `.map-analysis-canvas` and pin to its top-right corner. The controls panel (`.map-sidebar`) sits at z-index 1001 (above Leaflet's controls, #5052); the planner sits at 1000, so the controls panel covered it.

**Fix (`SitePlannerPanel.module.css`, CSS only):** BaseMap renders `.map-sidebar` before the planner, and that element exists only while the controls are open (collapsed, it is the small `.map-sidebar-toggle` button). So `:global(.map-sidebar) ~ .sitePlanner` moves the planner exactly when the controls are open, with no shared JS state:
- **Desktop:** planner sits left of the 300px controls column; width shrinks to fit narrow maps.
- **Short landscape** (phone rotated): the controls are a right-edge sheet of `min(300px, 60%)`; the planner takes the space beside it. Placed after the portrait block so a 667x375 phone, which matches both, gets the landscape rule.
- **Portrait phone:** the controls are a full sheet over the map pane, so there is no room beside it; the planner keeps its corner under the sheet until the user closes it.
- **Controls collapsed:** unchanged. The planner keeps the `top: 4rem; right: 0.75rem` from #5698, so its close button still clears the map-controls button.

title: test: stop the onUserConsoleLog teardown flake
body:
## The fault

The v4.17.0-rc7 Release Pipeline (run 37978638320) failed three attempts in a row with every test green:

```
Unhandled Rejection: EnvironmentTeardownError: [vitest-worker]: Closing rpc while "onUserConsoleLog" was pending
```

Each attempt blamed a different file: `crossSourceCorrelation.test.ts`, then `nodeInfoEnrichmentService.perSource.test.ts`, then `virtualNodeServer.test.ts`. The cause is the same in all three: **un-awaited work that writes a log line after its test file has ended.**

Vitest 5 reuses a fork for many files. When a file ends, the worker rejects every RPC still in flight. A `console.*` call is sent to the main process as an `onUserConsoleLog` RPC, so a log line issued after the file's last test can still be pending when the worker shuts that file down. That rejection is unhandled, and the run fails. The "originated in" file is whichever file the worker was attached to when the rejection fired, which is why it moved around.

## Evidence

1. **Attempt 3 log.** Right after `nodeInfoEnrichmentService.perSource.test.ts` finished, the log shows `Failed to send new node notification: EnvironmentTeardownError: Cannot load notificationFiltering.ts ... after the environment was torn down`, with this call chain: test → `database.ts` → `notificationService.ts` → `pushNotificationService.ts`. `DatabaseService.maybeNotifyNewNode` runs that dynamic import without awaiting it.
2. **Instrumented full run (new-node path).** I temporarily logged the test file each time `maybeNotifyNewNode` fired. Nine suites seed complete nodes against the real singleton without mocking the notification: `nodeInfoEnrichmentService.perSource`, `mqttGeoSweepService.perSource`, `mqttIngestion.{perSource,coverage.perSource,distanceInline}`, `nodeInfoEnrichment.permissions`, `sourceRoutes.{deleteCleanup,geoSweep}`, `surveyRoutes`. In `nodeInfoEnrichmentService.perSource`, **all 3** notifications were still in flight when its last test ended, in 3 out of 3 local runs.
3. **Reproduced locally.** A full suite run with only that path drained still failed the same way (`Errors 2`, blamed on `meshcoreMessageFilter.test.ts`). So there was a second source.
4. **Instrumented logger.** I temporarily made `logger` record any line issued after its own test file had finished, with a stack trace. Two more sources showed up:
   - `DatabaseService.ensureAdminUser()` runs `createAdminIfNeeded()` and `ensureAnonymousUser()` without awaiting them (a bcrypt hash plus a dynamic import of `systemRestoreService`). **Any** file that imports `database.ts` and finishes in under about 100 ms leaves them running. That matches the blamed files: `crossSourceCorrelation` (62 ms), `virtualNodeServer` (60 ms) and `meshcoreMessageFilter` (73 ms) only import it transitively.
   - `cotFeedService.stop()` resolved before each client socket's `'close'` handler had logged `CoT feed client disconnected`.

## The fix

- **`src/utils/backgroundTasks.ts`** (new): `trackBackgroundTask(promise)`

title: feat(pki): Reliable PKI — prime NodeInfo before PKI sends to nodes that stopped answering (#5691)
body:
Closes #5691

This also covers #5690 (the automation-only "send NodeInfo first" toggle): every automation `action.requestData` telemetry / LocalStats / neighbors request goes through the same send paths, so it is primed by this setting. #5690 is left open for the maintainer to close.

## What it does

A new **Reliable PKI** setting, **Off** (default) or **As needed**:

- Global default: **Global Settings → Security**.
- Per-source override: a Meshtastic source's **Settings → Reliable PKI** (*Use the global default* / Off / As needed). MeshMonitor behaviour, so Settings, not Device Configuration (#5694's rule).
- Beside both controls: *"When a node stops answering encrypted requests, MeshMonitor sends it your node info first (at most once an hour per node). Each one uses airtime on the mesh."*

In **As needed**, before a PKI send to node N on source S: if the last PKI exchange with N on S **failed** and no priming NodeInfo went to N from S in the last hour, MeshMonitor sends N our NodeInfo, stamps the time in the database, waits 5 s, then sends the real message.

**Node Details** gains a read-only *Encrypted requests* line: *Last answered …* / *Failing since …* + reason / *Waiting for an answer* / *No answer recorded*, and when our node info was last sent to it. A priming send logs `Reliable PKI: sent NodeInfo to !xxxxxxxx …` at debug. No notification.

## What I found (and where the issue was wrong)

Read from the firmware (`meshtastic/firmware` `develop`, checked back to v2.5.20 / v2.6.11 / v2.7.15) and the protobufs.

1. **Which sends are PKI.** The radio PKI-encrypts any unicast it originates to a node whose key it holds (`Router.cpp` `wouldEncryptWithPKC`), *except* `TRACEROUTE_APP`, `NODEINFO_APP`, `ROUTING_APP` and `POSITION_APP`. It does not look at the channel index. So the issue's list was partly wrong:
   - **In scope:** DMs (UI, API, auto-ack/auto-responder, automations, message queue), telemetry requests, remote **LocalStats** (it rides the node's channel but is still PKI; the old code comment said otherwise and is corrected), **neighbor info** requests, and **waypoints sent to one node**.
   - **Not PKI, so never primed and never change state:** traceroute, position request, NodeInfo exchange.
   - **Out of scope by decision: remote admin.** `ADMIN_APP` is PKI on the wire, but it has its own admin-key + session-passkey flow, its failures are already shown interactively, and priming inside an admin session would add sends to a user-driven flow. Virtual-node client traffic (`sendRawMessage`) is not ours to hold back.
   - MeshMonitor decides "PKI target" the same way `sendTextMessage` already did: we hold the node's key and no key mismatch is flagged (a mismatch belongs to Auto Key Management, which sends its own exchanges).

2. **The priming packet — reused path, one change that needs your eye.** It is the key-repair / "Exchange Node Info" sender, `sendNodeInfoRequest(node, node.channel)`: `NODEINFO_APP` on the **node's channel** (nev

title: fix(docker): prune dev deps, run every process as node, bump base images (#5692)
body:
Closes #5692

Hardens the Docker images along the three lines the issue proposed, plus the runtime CVEs it named.

## 1. Dev dependencies pruned from the runtime image

- **Alpine (amd64/arm64):** `npm prune --omit=dev` at the end of the **builder** stage, after `build` and `build:server`, so the runtime `COPY` only gets production deps. (A prune after the COPY would leave the full tree in the layer underneath and shrink nothing.) Native modules are built once in the builder as before and kept.
- **armv7:** the emulated `deps` stage now runs `npm install --omit=dev`. Dev deps are no longer installed or compiled under QEMU at all.
- `/app/node_modules`: **763 MB -> 369 MB**; image (amd64): **1.44 GB -> 964 MB**. `vite`, `vitest`, `typescript`, `eslint`, `puppeteer`, `@vue/*`, `seroval`, `@babel/plugin-transform-modules-systemjs` no longer ship (`@babel/runtime` is a real runtime dep and stays).
- **Classification check:** nothing the server loads is a devDependency. `npm run check:imports` (already in CI) now also fails when a package reachable from `dist/server/server.js`, through ESM `import` or `createRequire` `require()`, is not in `dependencies`/`optionalDependencies`. Result today: 852 modules walked, every package is a runtime dependency, so no reclassification was needed.
- **Bug found on the way:** `check:imports` had been a silent no-op since `es-module-lexer` 3.0 renamed the specifier field from `n` to `specifier`. It printed `walked 1 modules ... OK` on every run. Fixed: it reads both fields and fails if the walk finds fewer than 400 modules (the real graph is 852).

## 2. Base images bumped (majors unchanged)

| Image | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| amd64/arm64 | `node:24.15.0-alpine3.22` | `node:24.21.0-alpine3.24` |
| armv7 | `node:22.22.2-bookworm-slim` | `node:22.23.3-bookworm-slim` |

The runtime npm moves from 11.19.0 to **11.21.0** (pinned, same major) because the npm bundled with node 24.21.0 still carries `tar` 7.5.19. npm has to stay: `npm start` launches the server and the user-script dependency installer runs `npm install`. armv7's bundled npm 10.9.9 already carries tar 7.5.22.

## 3. Non-root runtime

Today the **server already ran as `node`** (`su-exec node npm start`), but `supervisord` and **Apprise ran as root**, and the entrypoint ran `chown -R /data /app/dist` on every start.

**Design.** No bare `USER` directive: that would break every existing volume and the serial-device grant. The entrypoint still **starts** as root, does only what needs root, then `exec su-exec node supervisord ...` (`gosu` on armv7). So supervisord, the server and Apprise all run as `node`:

node     {supervisord} /usr/bin/python3 /usr/bin/supervisord -c /etc/supervisord.conf
node     /opt/apprise-venv/bin/python /app/apprise-api.py
node     npm start
node     {MainThread} node dist/server/server.js
```

- **supervisord.conf:** no `user=root`, no `su-exec` in program commands, pidfile `/tmp/supervisord.pid`. One file no

title: feat(mqtt): broker preset chooser with the official Meshtastic broker (#5689)
body:
Closes #5689

Adds a **Broker preset** chooser above the broker address in the three Meshtastic MQTT forms: device MQTT config, remote-admin MQTT config, and the MQTT bridge source's Settings (where #5694 moved it). It offers **Meshtastic Official**, **Meshtastic Official (TLS)** and **Custom…**, plus a helper line with two discovery links and one line on what a public broker means.

## Official broker facts (checked)

| Fact | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Host | `mqtt.meshtastic.org` | [MQTT module docs](https://meshtastic.org/docs/configuration/module/mqtt/), CLI table: "`mqtt.address` · `string` · `mqtt.meshtastic.org`" |
| Login | `meshdev` / `large4cats` | same table: "`mqtt.username` … `meshdev`", "`mqtt.password` … `large4cats`" |
| Empty address | the public server | same page, Server Address: "If not set, the default public server will be used." |
| Root topic | `msh/REGION` | [MQTT integration docs](https://meshtastic.org/docs/software/integrations/mqtt/): "If no specific root topic is configured, the default root topic will be `msh/REGION`." The presets do not touch root topic. |
| Ports | 1883 plain, 8883 TLS | **Not in the docs.** Firmware `src/mqtt/MQTT.cpp`: `defaultPort = 1883`, `defaultPortTls = 8883`; `tls_enabled` switches to 8883, and the default server is accepted on either port. |
| TLS on 8883 | yes | Live check: MQTT CONNECT with meshdev/large4cats got CONNACK 0 on `mqtt://…:1883` and on `mqtts://…:8883` (Let's Encrypt cert, verifies). |
| WebSockets | no | `wss://mqtt.meshtastic.org:443/mqtt` got no CONNACK. No WebSocket preset. |

The repo's existing references agree: `privateBrokerAddress.ts` treats an empty address or `mqtt.meshtastic.org` as public, and the tests and docs use `meshdev / large4cats`. One docs link pointed at a stale anchor (`#default-public-server`); fixed.

## Design

One module, `src/components/MQTT/brokerPresets.ts`, holds the presets and the per-form mapping, so the three forms cannot drift. `BrokerPresetSelector.tsx` is the shared UI.

| Form | Fields a preset sets | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| Device MQTT config | address, username, password, `tlsEnabled` | host only; TLS is the flag |
| Remote-admin MQTT config | same | same |
| MQTT bridge source | URL, username, password | `mqtt://mqtt.meshtastic.org:1883` or `mqtts://mqtt.meshtastic.org:8883` |

A preset never touches root topic, payload encryption, JSON, client proxy, map reporting, channel uplink/downlink, or any bridge mode, topic or filter.

**Which entry shows:** the preset the stored values match. On the device forms an empty address counts as the official broker (that is what firmware does); `host:port` matches only with the right port for the TLS flag. On the bridge, scheme + host + port must match (default port per scheme). Anything else shows **Custom…**. Picking **Custom…** changes no field and stays selected until a preset is picked.

+### Broker Preset

A preset sets the address, TLS and login, and leaves root topic, encryption, JSON, client proxy, map reporting and channel uplink/downlink alone.

title: feat(metrics): export each node's last position time
body:
## Summary
The Prometheus endpoint from #4757 can tell a node is silent (last-heard), but not that a GPS tracker is heard yet has no fix. Firmware stops sending positions while it has no fix but keeps sending telemetry and NodeInfo, so a tracker that lost its fix (or never got one) looks perfectly healthy on last-heard alone. This adds `meshmonitor_node_last_position_timestamp_seconds` so "heard but no fix" becomes alertable.

## Changes
- New per-node gauge `meshmonitor_node_last_position_timestamp_seconds` on `/api/v1/metrics`, read from the `positionTimestamp` the nodes table already stores (ms → seconds, matching last-heard so the two compare directly in a query).
- The series is **omitted** for a node that has never sent a position rather than exported as 0, so `unless on (source, node_id)` catches a never-had-a-fix node as well as a stale one.
- Same labels, active window, ignored-node and channel-visibility rules as the other per-node gauges (~9 series/node, up from ~8).
- Read-only; no packets sent.

## Issues Resolved
None

## Documentation Updates
- `docs/api/REST_API.md`: the new metric in the metrics table, plus an example "heard but no GPS fix" alert query.
- `src/server/routes/v1/openapi.yaml`: metrics endpoint description mentions last position time.

## Testing
- [x] Unit tests pass (29048 tests, rebased on 4.17.0-rc7)
- [x] TypeScript compiles cleanly (`tsc -p tsconfig.server.json`)
- [x] `metrics.test.ts`: the gauge is exported in seconds for a node with a position, and absent for a node that has never sent one
- [x] Running in production since 2026-10-08 (a local build of this branch on our bench and prod instances), scraped by Prometheus and feeding a Grafana "tracker heard but no GPS fix" alert of the shape documented in REST_API.md
- [ ] Reviewer: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" /api/v1/metrics | grep last_position` on an instance with GPS nodes

title: fix(site-planner): fold the panel after predict so the ring shows on phones (#5687)
body:
Closes #5687

## Problem

On a phone the Site Planner form covers the map, so the ring a prediction just drew cannot be seen without closing the panel.

## Change

The panel can now fold to a thin bar. One file pair changed: `SitePlannerPanel.tsx` and `SitePlannerPanel.module.css` (plus strings and tests).

- **Folded bar:** title, a one-line summary ("Reaches up to 15.0 km of 15 km searched. 100% of directions hit the search edge." and "Terrain data missing in places." when that applies), **Edit inputs** and **Clear**, plus the header expand toggle.
- **Auto-fold after a successful predict on the mobile layout.** "Mobile layout" is the app's shared definition, `MOBILE_LAYOUT_MEDIA_QUERY` = `(max-width: 768px), (max-height: 500px) and (orientation: landscape)`, read through `useIsMobileLayoutViewport()`. The CSS uses the same query, so JS and CSS agree on a landscape phone (#5060).
- **Height cap on phones:** the expanded panel gets `max-height: 55%` of the map with internal scrolling, so part of the map always shows below it. Width becomes `min(340px, 100% - 1.5rem)` of the map instead of `100vw`. Top/right offsets stay as on desktop because they clear the map-controls button in the map's top-right corner (moving the panel up hid its close button under that button).
- **Manual toggle on every viewport:** a header button with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and an "Expand/Collapse site planner" label.
- **Desktop does not auto-fold.** The panel is 340px on a wide map, so the ring is already visible beside it, and the shape notices (radius-limited, data gaps, pockets) are the point of #4727 and should stay on screen unless the user folds them.
- **Pending:** stays expanded; Run shows "Predicting…" and is disabled. If the user folds it while pending, the bar shows "Predicting…".
- **Error:** the panel unfolds (even if folded by hand while pending) and shows the error.
- **State:** folding hides the form (`hidden`), it does not unmount it, so inputs keep their exact values, including a half-typed draft. The drawn ring is untouched. Closing works as before; reopening shows the form expanded.
- **Focus:** after an auto-fold, focus moves to the expand toggle, but only if focus started in the panel and the user has not moved it while waiting. The check runs before Run disables, because a disabled button drops focus to `<body>`. **Edit inputs** focuses the first field (frequency).

No change to the `/api/rf/coverage` request or to what is drawn.

**No bottom sheet.** The codebase has no reusable bottom-sheet component. `TilesetSelector` has its own one-off sheet styled by global classes (#4380), and nothing else can be reused, so I followed the issue's Option 1 + 3.

## Where the issue was wrong

- The class is `.sitePlanner`, not `.panel`.
- The rule said "no max-height", but it had `max-height: calc(100% - 5rem); overflow-y: auto`. That cap is relative to the map, so on a phone it still let the panel cover almost the whole map.
- Width: the summary sa

title: feat(auto-ack): wait 5-30 s and stay quiet when enough nodes have already answered
body:
## What this does

No issue: the maintainer asked for this directly.

> Add a randomized time delay of 5-10s. During that time, monitor if other replies have already come in to the triggering message. Allow the user to specify a configurable "Maximum number of responses", that if those have already come in by the time you respond then abort the response. This is to avoid flooding the mesh with numerous tapbacks that stop accumulating value after a bit. This feature should default to 2.
>
> Extend this to include "replies" in addition to tapbacks, using the same logic we use on the frontend to render replies.
>
> Extend the window from 5-10 to 5-30, to account for large or slow meshes.

When Meshtastic Auto-Acknowledge decides to answer a **channel** message it now:

1. waits a uniformly random 5–30 s (`AUTO_ACK_RESPONSE_WAIT_MIN_MS` = 5 000, `AUTO_ACK_RESPONSE_WAIT_MAX_MS` = 30 000; not configurable);
2. runs the whole decision again against the settings as they are now, and checks the trigger still exists;
3. counts the other nodes that have replied to, or tapbacked, that message on this source;
4. sends nothing if the count has reached **Maximum number of responses** (`autoAckMaxResponses`, per source, 0–10, default 2, `0` = no cap).

## Screenshot

![Auto Acknowledge settings with Maximum number of responses](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/blob/101dacc049f6559656e58b516cc2ace7ee00c83c/docs/public/images/features/auto-ack-max-responses.png?raw=true)

## Behaviour change on upgrade

**On for every Meshtastic source, default 2.** A channel ack now arrives **5–30 s after the message, 17.5 s on average**, instead of at once, and is skipped when two other nodes have already answered. Someone testing with "ping" on a channel will see nothing for up to half a minute; the help text and the docs say so. `0` restores "always answer" (still after the wait). Direct messages are untouched and still answered at once.

## One rule for "is this a reply / a tapback"

The rule the channel and DM views used inline now lives in `src/utils/messageReplies.ts` (`isTapbackMessage`, `isTapbackOf`, `isReplyTo`, `isResponseTo`, `countDistinctResponders`). `ChannelsTab` and `MessagesTab` call it, and so does the server counter, so the two cannot drift.

- The refactor keeps rendering as it was. `messageReplies.test.ts` runs a table of cases through both the new functions and the old inline expressions (copied verbatim) and requires equal answers.
- The server query (`MessagesRepository.getReplyCandidates`: source + channel + `replyId`) only selects candidates; each row then goes through the shared predicate. `messages.replyCandidates.perSource.test.ts` proves query + predicate equals the predicate alone over a table of rows.

Quirks of the view rule, kept as they were and now written down in the module header:

- The parent is matched on the last `_` segment of its row id. The `_dbchan` / `_radio` copies of a server-decrypted message end in a suffix, so nothing eve

+- **`autoAckMaxResponses`** — Auto-Acknowledge waits 5 to 30 seconds before it answers a channel
+  message and stays quiet once that many other nodes have replied or sent a tapback (see [Maximum
+  Number of Responses](/features/automation#auto-ack-max-responses)). The engine has no "wait, then
+  check for other responses" step, so a converted channel automation answers every matching
