--- docs/features/automation.md (+38/-0)
@@ -132,6 +132,44 @@ When enabled, auto-ack responses are sent as direct messages (DMs) to the sender
 
 **When to use it**: Give a repeater time to finish transmitting the triggering message before your reply goes out, instead of racing it. For anything more elaborate than a single fixed delay — e.g. a delay followed by other actions — use the Automation Engine's [Pause action](/features/automation-engine#pause) instead.
 
+On a Meshtastic **channel** message the delay works with the wait described under [Maximum Number of Responses](#auto-ack-max-responses): a delay of 5 seconds or less changes nothing (the wait is already 5 to 30 seconds), and a longer delay becomes the start of the wait, so a delay of 20 gives a wait of 20 to 45 seconds. Direct messages use the delay exactly as set.
+
+### Maximum Number of Responses {#auto-ack-max-responses}
+
+When several nodes on a channel run Auto Acknowledge, one "ping" can draw a reply or tapback from every one of them. After the first couple, the rest tell the sender nothing and only use airtime.
+
+So before it answers a **channel** message, MeshMonitor waits a random **5 to 30 seconds**. When the wait ends it counts the other nodes that have already replied to that message or sent a tapback on it. If the count has reached **Maximum number of responses**, MeshMonitor stays quiet: it sends neither its tapback nor its reply.
+
+**Default**: `2` — **Range**: `0` to `10` — set per source.
+
+::: tip Testing with "ping"? Wait for it
+A channel acknowledgement now arrives **5 to 30 seconds** after the message, about 17 seconds on average, and not at all when enough other nodes answered first. Nothing is broken if your "ping" gets no instant reply. To see an answer every time, set the value to `0` and wait up to 30 seconds, or send the ping as a direct message, which is answered at once.
+:::
+
+- `0` means no limit: MeshMonitor still waits 5 to 30 seconds, then always answers.
+- A node that sends both a reply and a tapback counts **once**.
+- Replies and tapbacks are recognised the same way the message view shows them under a message: a message that points at the original (its "reply to") is a reply, and one flagged as a reaction, or whose whole text is an emoji, is a tapback.
+- Your own node's sends never count. Neither does a follow-up from the person who sent the original message.
+- Only answers heard on **this source**, on the same channel, count. If two of your sources hear the same message, each decides by what it heard itself.
+- **Direct messages are not affected.** Nobody else can answer a DM sent to you, so it is answered straight away, as before.
+- Meshtastic sources only. MeshCore messages carry no "reply to" reference, so MeshMonitor cannot tell which message another node's reply answers; the MeshCore Auto Acknowledge is unchanged.
+
+**Why 5 to 30 seconds.** The 5-second floor gives other nodes' answers time to reach you before you decide; without it you would answer before anyone could have been heard. The spread up to 30 seconds is for large or slow meshes, where an answer needs many seconds to cross several hops: the wider the spread, the fewer nodes finish waiting before they have heard each other.
+
+**The wait follows your current settings.** When the wait ends, MeshMonitor decides again from scratch. If in the meantime you turned Auto Acknowledge off, changed the pattern so the message no longer matches, removed the channel, added the sender to the ignore list, lowered the maximum, or the message was deleted, no answer is sent. The answer is also dropped, not kept for later, if the source is disconnected, has TX disabled, or is over the airtime cutoff. Answers still waiting are dropped when the source disconnects or MeshMonitor restarts.
+
+**Cooldown.** The per-node cooldown is checked when the message arrives and starts again when the answer is sent, and a node with an answer still waiting cannot start a second one. Two answers to one node are never closer together than the cooldown, even when the cooldown is shorter than the wait.
+
+**Bursts.** At most 10 answers wait at a time on one source; a burst beyond that is dropped.
+
+The wait can only remove a send or delay it. It never adds one.
+
+The limit is a target, not a guarantee. A node cannot count an answer it has not heard yet, so nodes whose waits end close together can all answer. On a LongFast mesh a few hops across, expect about one answer more than the number set here with 5 nodes answering and about two more with 10. On a slow preset such as LongSlow, where one answer can take 10 to 20 seconds to arrive, expect roughly half of the nodes to answer whatever the limit.
+
+::: warning Upgrade note
+This is on for every Meshtastic source after you upgrade, with the default of `2`. Channel acknowledgements now arrive 5 to 30 seconds after the message (about 17 seconds on average) instead of at once, and are skipped when two other nodes have already answered. To answer every matching message as before (still after the wait), set **Maximum number of responses** to `0`. Direct messages are answered at once, as before.
+:::
+
 ### Long Replies on MeshCore {#meshcore-long-replies}
 
 A MeshCore text message is small. MeshMonitor caps one message at **150 bytes** for a DM, **130 bytes** for a channel, and **120 bytes** for a channel reply that carries a region scope. These are UTF-8 bytes, not characters: an emoji takes 4 bytes and a CJK character takes 3. A template that looks short can go over the cap once `{NODE_NAME}`, `{ROUTE}` and the other tokens are filled in.

title: fix(settings): put each per-source control on the page its name promises (#5683)
body:
Refs #5683

## What was wrong

PR #5684 gave the two per-source pages one icon and one name each: the satellite is **Device Configuration**, the gear is **Settings**. The content did not match the names. Controls that write to the radio sat under Settings, a MeshMonitor-only switch sat under Device Configuration, an install-wide setting sat on a per-source page, and the MQTT bridge used the satellite for a page that configures no device. #5684 listed these and left them for a decision. This PR applies the maintainer's decisions.

## The rule

| Page | Holds |
|---|---|
| Device Configuration (satellite, per source) | what is written to, or done on, the radio |
| Settings (gear, per source) | what MeshMonitor stores and does for that one source |
| Global Settings (`/settings`) | what applies to the whole install |

## Placement, before and after

Every row was checked against the component and the route it calls, not taken from #5684's list.

| Source | Control | Route (grant) | Sent to the device? | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MQTT bridge | Bridge setup: parent broker, upstream URL, username, password, mode, upstream identity, uplink switches, subscribe topics, topic block, geo box, geo status, publish filter, topic rewrites | `GET`/`PUT /api/sources/:id` (`sources:read` / `sources:write`) | No. Stored in the source row | own page, satellite "Configuration" entry | **Settings**, first section, headed "MQTT Bridge Configuration". No satellite entry |
| MeshCore | Default path hash size | `…/config/default-path-hash-size` (`configuration`) | Yes, `CMD_SET_PATH_HASH_MODE` | Settings | **Device Configuration** |
| MeshCore | Default region / scope | `…/config/default-scope` (`configuration`) | Yes, as the device flood scope on send | Settings | **Device Configuration** |
| MeshCore | Discover regions from repeaters | `POST …/regions/discover` (`nodes:write`, TX) | Transmits | Settings, in the scope section | **Device Configuration**, with the scope section |
| MeshCore | Radio contact list: auto-add switch, Push to radio | `…/config/auto-add-contacts` (`configuration:write`), `…/contacts/push-to-device` (`nodes:write`) | Yes | Settings | **Device Configuration** |
| MeshCore | Refresh contacts | `POST …/contacts/refresh` (`nodes:write`) | Reads the device | Settings | **Device Configuration → Device actions** |
| MeshCore | Advert, zero-hop and flood | `POST …/advert` (`connection:write`, TX) | Transmits | Settings and status bar | **Device Configuration → Device actions**; status bar unchanged |
| MeshCore | Discover Nearby / Repeaters / Sensors | `POST …/discover` (`nodes:write`, TX) | Transmits | Settings and Nodes view menu | **Device Configuration → Device actions**; Nodes menu unchanged |
| Meshtastic | Firmware update | `/api/firmware/*` (admin) | Yes | Settings | **Device Configuration**, last section |
| Meshtastic | PKI DM decryption | `…/pki-dm/status`, `POST …/pki-dm` (`configuration`) | No. MeshMonitor reads and stores

title: fix(meshcore): mark unrelayed channel sends "Sent to radio" (#5682)
body:
Refs #5682 (left open: both artefacts quoted in the issue are Meshtastic screens; waiting on the reporter to confirm the source type)

## What changes

A MeshCore channel send that no repeater was heard relaying showed no delivery mark at all. It now reads **Sent to radio**. When a repeater's echo is heard, the mark gives way to the heard-by badge that was already there.

![Dark, desktop](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/blob/0ceab416f/docs/public/images/features/5682-sent-to-radio-dark-desktop.png?raw=true)
![Light, desktop](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/blob/0ceab416f/docs/public/images/features/5682-sent-to-radio-light-desktop.png?raw=true)
![Light, phone width](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/blob/0ceab416f/docs/public/images/features/5682-sent-to-radio-light-phone.png?raw=true)
![Delivery Details for a Sent to radio message](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/blob/0ceab416f/docs/public/images/features/5682-sent-to-radio-dark-modal.png?raw=true)

Screenshots come from a local fixture harness (the real component, real CSS, real `en.json`). No message went out on a radio.

## Read this first: the radio sends no transmit record

The issue, and the decision to add a "Sent" mark, both rest on "the companion pushed the TX record back to MM". **It does not. No such record exists.** The mark can only claim that the radio *accepted* the message, so it says **"Sent to radio"**, not "Sent" or "Transmitted".

Evidence:

- `LogRxData` (push `0x88`) fires from one place in the firmware, `Dispatcher::checkRecv()`, right after `_radio->recvRaw()`. It is a receive feed.
- The firmware has transmit hooks, `Dispatcher::logTx()` and `logTxFail()`, called when a send ends or fails. Both are empty virtuals in `Dispatcher.h`, and the companion (`examples/companion_radio/MyMesh.cpp`) overrides only `logRxRaw`. No `PUSH_CODE_*` reports a transmission. (MeshCore `a366955cb2`, 2026-09-30.)
- For `CMD_SEND_CHANNEL_TXT_MSG` the companion answers `Ok` when the channel slot exists and `sendGroupMessage()` built a packet and queued it, else `Err`. The radio sends later, from the dispatcher loop, after channel-activity and duty-cycle checks. If that send fails or times out, the host hears nothing.
- MeshMonitor writes no TX row for MeshCore either. `meshcore_packet_log` holds only what `LogRxData` delivers.

So the order of proof is: `Ok` (radio took it) < relay echo heard (it went out, a repeater carried it). There is no step between them that the radio reports.

## Where the issue was wrong

1. **The "TX | Via INT | ... | TEXT_MESSAGE_APP | Hops 0/ | Last Hop Direct" row is a Meshtastic row.** Only `meshtasticManager.logOutgoingPacket()` writes `direction: 'tx'` with `TransportMechanism.INTERNAL`, into `packet_log`, and MeshMonitor writes it itself when it hands a packet to the node. The MeshCore Packet Monitor has no direction or "via" column and names the payload `GRP_TXT`.
2. **The `(X/Y hops)` badge is Meshtastic too.** `HopCountDisplay` renders i

title: fix(map): raster fallback when a vector tileset meets a browser with no WebGL2
body:
## The fault

With a vector map tileset selected (`cartoPositron`, the rig's default) in a browser with no WebGL2, the whole app went blank: `#root` ended with zero children. There is no issue for this; the maintainer asked for a direct fix.

Reproduced on unmodified `main` (headless Chrome, `getContext('webgl2')` is `null`):

1. Page load logs `Failed to create MapLibre GL layer: GPUInitializationError: WebGL2 is required…`. The page still renders, with a dead map.
2. A resize or pan throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'jumpTo')`.
3. Leaving the map view throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'remove')` and `#root` goes from 3 children to 0.

### Root cause

`@maplibre/maplibre-gl-leaflet` builds the GL map inside the layer's `onAdd`. Leaflet's `_layerAdd` registers the layer and binds its `move` / `zoom` / `resize` handlers **before** it calls `onAdd`. So when `new maplibregl.Map()` throws, the layer stays on the map with live handlers and no `_glMap`.

`VectorTileLayer` caught the throw, logged it, and returned with no cleanup (`src/components/VectorTileLayer.tsx:361-364` on `main`). After that:

- every Leaflet move called the adapter's `_update` → `gl.jumpTo` on `undefined`;
- `map.remove()` (react-leaflet's unmount of `MapContainer`) called the adapter's `onRemove` → `this._glMap.remove()` on `undefined`.

The second one is what blanked the app. React reports an error thrown by an effect cleanup during an unmount to the nearest boundary **above the subtree being removed**. Leaving a source page removes the whole route, per-tab `ErrorBoundary` included, so nothing caught it and React emptied the root. (When only a tab changes, the tab boundary sits above the removed map and can catch it; that fits the "Configuration failed to load" one agent saw, though I did not reproduce that exact panel.) `ErrorBoundary.test.tsx` now pins this React behaviour.

## The fix

In the order asked:

**a. Detect.** `src/components/map/vectorSupport.ts` probes for a `webgl2` context once (throwaway canvas, context released, answer cached). WebGL1 does not count: MapLibre GL 6 needs WebGL2. A creation failure at runtime, after a passing probe, sets a page-wide flag so no other map tries.

**b. Fall back, for the render only.** `BaseMap` draws `getRasterTileset(tileset)` through its existing raster branch. That is the rule the 3D view and the traceroute mini-map already use (#5448):

| Selected | Drawn without WebGL2 |
|---|---|
| CARTO Positron | CARTO `light_all` raster |
| CARTO Dark Matter, CARTO Voyager Dark | CARTO `dark_all` raster |
| CARTO Voyager | CARTO `rastertiles/voyager` |
| custom `.pbf`/`.mvt` tileset | default `osm` raster |

The CARTO key still rides on the raster URL through `withCartoKey`. `tilesetId`, `onTilesetChange` and the saved `mapTileset` setting are not touched, so the same account gets vector tiles in a capable browser.

**c. Tell the user once.** A small note in the map's bottom-left corner (`VectorFall

title: fix(nav): one icon and one label for Device Configuration and Settings on every source type (#5683)
body:
Closes #5683

## What was wrong

Each source type builds its own nav and spelled the same two entries itself. They drifted: the entry that opens the radio's own config read **Device** on Meshtastic and **Configuration** on MeshCore and Reticulum, under one icon.

Maintainer decisions applied: the label is **Device Configuration**, and each of the two per-source pages (Device Configuration, Settings) must be reached by one icon and one label on every source type.

## Where the issue text was wrong

- The reporter says that on Meshtastic "the gear icon is 'Configuration'". It is not: the gear is **Settings** there too. It sits under a sidebar section header that reads **CONFIGURATION**, which is the likely source of that reading. The header is unchanged.
- The **icons were never swapped**. On every source type the satellite (`configuration`) already opened the radio's config and the gear (`settings`) already opened Settings. Only the satellite's label drifted. No icon moves in this PR.
- The issue lists the MQTT bridge as a third "Configuration" that should join the others. Its page is a different kind of page (see below), so it is left alone and flagged.
- `nav.configuration` held "Device", not "Configuration", so the settings search called the page "Device" and the Users tab named the `configuration` permission "Device".

## Function map (what each entry opens, and where its settings live)

| Source type | Icon | Label before | Label after | Page | What the page holds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Meshtastic | satellite `configuration` | Device | **Device Configuration** | `ConfigurationTab` | On the device: node identity, device, LoRa, position, power, display, telemetry, MQTT, neighbor info, network, every module, security, channels, reboot, purge NodeDB, import/export. MeshMonitor-side: PKI DM decryption, Backup list |
| Meshtastic | gear `settings` | Settings | Settings | `SettingsTab mode="source"` | MeshMonitor-side, this source: node display, telemetry, notifications, packet monitor, solar, reset UI, settings management, danger zone (purge MeshMonitor data). Device action: firmware update |
| MeshCore | satellite `configuration` | Configuration | **Device Configuration** | `MeshCoreConfigurationView` | On the device: name, location, radio parameters, TX power, telemetry modes, reboot, private key export/import, device console |
| MeshCore | gear `settings` | Settings | Settings | `MeshCoreSettingsView` | MeshMonitor-side: connect/disconnect, receive-only (software), saved regions, purge messages. On the device: path hash size, default scope, contact list sync. Device actions: refresh contacts, send advert, discover nodes |
| Reticulum (`own` mode) | satellite `configuration` | Configuration | **Device Configuration** | `ReticulumConfigurationView` | On the device: RNode frequency, bandwidth, SF, CR, TX power, airtime locks; read-only device info |
| Reticulum (other modes) | none | none | none | none | No radio is owned, so there is no dev

title: feat(traffic-management): read-only replay for position dedup and rate limit, and corrected docs (#5670)
body:
Refs #5670

## What this builds

The maintainer's chosen scope for #5670, in one PR:

1. **Docs.** `docs/features/traffic-management.md` corrected against the firmware source, with new sections on what MeshMonitor can and cannot know, on estimating impact by hand in Packet Monitor, and on the new panel.
2. **A read-only "Estimate impact" panel** beside the Traffic Management form (local Device Configuration only). It replays the local node's packet log against the form's **Position Deduplication** and **Rate Limiting** values and shows how many logged packets those values would have dropped.

![Estimate impact panel](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/blob/307a6c657/docs/public/images/features/traffic-management-estimate.png?raw=true)

## What this does not build

- Drop Unknown Packets and NodeInfo Direct Response are **not** simulated (the docs give a by-hand method and say why NodeInfo cannot be judged from history).
- **No observed-drop statistics.** The firmware never sends them (see below).
- No remote nodes, no MQTT sources, no upstream firmware request.
- The existing `TrafficManagementStats` ingest code and telemetry graphs are **unchanged**. Only the docs claim about them is corrected.

Whether this closes the issue is the maintainer's call.

## Firmware source checked

`meshtastic/firmware`, `src/modules/TrafficManagementModule.cpp`, read at `v2.8.0.47db0e3`, `v2.8.0.7239fe8`, `v2.8.1.8e6a88d` and `develop@015d5b1` (2026-10-08). `handleReceived`, `shouldDropPosition`, `isRateLimited`, `runOnce` and `findOrCreateEntry` are **byte-identical in all four**. The file does differ between versions, but elsewhere (2.8.0 → 2.8.1: three lines in the NodeInfo reply throttle; 2.8.1 → develop: `alterReceived`, the relayed-position precision clamp, is removed). The module is absent from `master`.

The mirror's version is one constant, `TMM_MIRROR_FIRMWARE_VERSION = 'v2.8.1.8e6a88d'`, shown in the UI and pinned by a test.

### Where the source differed from the earlier investigation

| Investigation said | Source says |
|---|---|
| Role caps are about "the node's role" | They key on the **sender's** advertised role (`resolveSenderRole(p->from)`), cached at first sight and refreshed on NodeInfo. The replay takes a role per sender. TAK_TRACKER is capped like TRACKER. |
| Precision is "the local node's channel precision, else 19 bits" | Per **arrival channel**, and capped at **15 bits** on a well-known channel, because every well-known channel uses a public key (`getPositionPrecisionForChannel`). An unset channel falls back to 19, which is finer than the cap. |
| "Any window under 10 minutes is one tick" | True for the comparison, but `runOnce` sweeps the cache every 60 s with a TTL of `2 × window / 5 min` ticks. For a window **under 150 s** that TTL is 0, so the sweep zeroes the counter every minute: the real window is at most 60 s. Same for dedup under **90 s** (`4 × interval / 6 min`). The replay models the sweep and samples its phase too. |

title: feat(firmware): explain hardware that cannot be updated in place of the update UI (#5677)
body:
Closes #5677

## What this does

When the selected source's node has hardware MeshMonitor cannot update, **Settings → Firmware Updates** shows a short card in place of the update controls. The card says why and where to update the node instead. The Settings nav entry stays.

The verdict comes from one list, `EXCLUDED_MODELS` in `src/utils/firmwareHardwareMap.ts`, which the server's OTA preflight also reads. The server keeps its refusal and now returns it as `400` with a machine code.

This PR is UI plus one shared module. It never starts, schedules or triggers an update, and it changes nothing about how a supported board is flashed.

## Where the issue was wrong

1. **The docs link is dead.** `https://meshtastic.org/docs/software/meshtasticd/` returns 404. The live page is `https://meshtastic.org/docs/meshtasticd/installation/` (200, checked 2026-10-08).
2. **The suggested commands are not safe to print.** The official page lists ten install routes (Debian, Raspbian, Ubuntu PPA, Fedora COPR, EPEL, Docker, Flatpak, OpenWrt, NixOS, Homebrew). `apt upgrade meshtasticd` is wrong for most of them, so the card names no command: "Update the meshtasticd package with your system package manager, or pull a newer container image", plus the link.
3. **"The backend already refuses the request" was half true.** It refused with a bare `Error`, which the route turned into a **500** with no code. Now `400` + code.
4. **"Changing the server-side error: not in scope."** The text is kept where it was right (`Unknown hardware model N…`, `…is not OTA capable`), but a 500 for a known, permanent condition was a bug, so the status and code changed.
5. **Three excluded models are not the whole dead end.** 14 named models have no firmware build mapped (e.g. `PRIVATE_HW`, `T_ECHO_CARD`, `CROWPANEL_P4`) and 43 are nRF52840 / RP2040 / STM32 boards with no Wi-Fi OTA. A non-bridged one (a RAK4631 with an Ethernet module, say) got the full update UI and then a 500. They get a card too.
6. **"UNSET → node identity not yet reported, reconnect"** describes a transient state, and showing a card for it would flash on every first connect. See "UNSET" below.
7. **`firmwareHardwareMap.ts` cannot simply be "exported to the UI"** from `src/server/`. It had no node-only imports, so it moved whole to `src/utils/` and the server path re-exports it (same pattern as `packetSignaturePolicy`).

## Condition table

Every case where the server cannot or will not update a node:

| Condition | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `PORTDUINO` (37, meshtasticd) | Full update UI. Install → toast `Unknown hardware model 37: cannot determine board name` (HTTP 500) | Card: updated on its Linux host; package manager or container image; link to the meshtasticd guide. Server: 400 `OTA_HARDWARE_LINUX_NATIVE` |
| `ANDROID_SIM` (38) | Full UI, same 500 | Card: a simulator, nothing to flash. 400 `OTA_HARDWARE_SIMULATOR` |
| `UNSET` (0), node has finished reporting | Full UI, same 500 | Card: reports no hardware mode

title: feat(automations): trigger.ageMinutes on MeshCore nodeDiscovered / nodeUpdated (#5675)
body:
Closes #5675

## What

A MeshCore discovery notification printed `Last heard: 1791366294000 m`: the only last-heard token on the MeshCore node triggers was `{{ trigger.lastHeard }}` (epoch ms, #5595). The Meshtastic one prints `Last heard: 0 m` through `{{ node.ageMinutes }}`, which cannot hydrate on MeshCore (no node number).

This adds `{{ trigger.ageMinutes }}` to the MeshCore `trigger.nodeDiscovered` and `trigger.nodeUpdated` contexts. `{{ trigger.lastHeard }}` is unchanged.

## Design

- **One formula.** `node.ageMinutes` computed `Math.max(0, Math.round((now - lastMs) / 60000))` inline in `engineContext.ts`. That line is now `ageMinutesSince(lastHeardMs, nowMs)` in `triggerContext.ts`, used by both the Meshtastic path and `buildMeshCoreNodeContext`. Meshtastic output is unchanged. A parity test feeds the same instants through both paths (0 s to 30 days, and stamps in the future) and asserts equal results.
- **Unit.** Every producer of `MeshCoreNodeEventFacts.lastHeard` goes through `meshCoreNodeTriggerPayload`, which sends `contact.lastSeen`: epoch **ms**. It is `Date.now()` in the advert, path-update and discovery-reply handlers, and the companion's `last_mod` (seconds, scaled to ms, checked for plausibility and clamped to `Date.now()`) after a contact re-read. `ageMinutes` is worked out from the same normalised value `trigger.lastHeard` shows (`epochMsOrUndefined`, which scales a seconds value up), so the two tokens cannot disagree.
- **Clock.** The age is measured to the event `timestamp` (the engine's `now()` at dispatch), which is the same value `ctx.now` holds for `node.ageMinutes`.
- **First-heard node.** The advert handler stamps `lastSeen = Date.now()` before it raises the event, so a discovery renders `0`, the same as Meshtastic. Unknown last-heard (no `lastSeen`) renders empty, as `node.ageMinutes` does for a node row with no `lastHeard`.
- **Builder.** Listed in the Substitutions drawer / token checker for both node triggers, and offered as a number-condition field (as `node.ageMinutes` is on Meshtastic). The Test panel works it out from its existing "Last heard (epoch ms)" input through the same builder; no new input.
- **Templates.** No shipped template or default text used `{{ trigger.lastHeard }} m`; the reported text came from a user-written automation. Nothing is migrated: saved automations keep whatever token they have, and `{{ trigger.lastHeard }}` still renders epoch ms. Users change their template to `{{ trigger.ageMinutes }}`.

## Other raw-value tokens found (not changed)

- `{{ trigger.lastHeard }}` on **Node silent** is also raw epoch ms, but that trigger already has `ageMinutes`.
- `{{ node.lastHeard }}` on Meshtastic is raw epoch **seconds** (a pass-through of the node row); `node.ageMinutes` is the readable one.
- **Node silent** `trigger.ageMinutes` uses `Math.floor`; `node.ageMinutes` (and now the MeshCore token) use `Math.round`. They can differ by one minute. Left alone: changing it would alter existing outp

Closes #5671
Closes #5672

Adds three one-click presets to the MeshCore Analyzer Observer broker list:

| Preset | Broker URL | Token audience | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshcore.ca Primary | `wss://mqtt1.meshcore.ca:443` | `mqtt1.meshcore.ca` | Signed token |
| meshcore.ca Backup | `wss://mqtt2.meshcore.ca:443` | `mqtt2.meshcore.ca` | Signed token |
| RF Lab | `wss://mqtt.rflab.io:443` | `mqtt.rflab.io` | Signed token |

![Preset row, desktop, after clicking the three new presets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5671-meshcore-ca-observer-preset/docs/public/images/features/5671-observer-presets.png)

Phone width (390 px):

![Preset row at phone width](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5671-meshcore-ca-observer-preset/docs/public/images/features/5671-observer-presets-phone.png)

## Design

Both issues say this is "purely new entries in the preset table". I checked that against the code, and it holds:

- **One definition.** `OBSERVER_BROKER_PRESETS` in `src/pages/DashboardPage.observerConfig.ts` is the only preset list. The chooser in `DashboardPage.tsx` maps over it. The server keeps no list of known brokers.
- **Nothing is keyed on host or preset identity.** No non-test server file mentions a preset host. The publisher treats every token-mode broker alike: TLS verify on by default, keepalive 60, client id prefix `meshmonitor-observer`, 24 h token minted per audience, topics `meshcore/{IATA}/{PUBKEY}/packets` and `/status`. A preset row saves and publishes exactly as a hand-typed row with the same values; a test asserts that for every named preset.
- **Model fit.** A preset carries URL, audience and label; auth is always signed token. Both operators need only those. Region (IATA) is one block-level field shared by all brokers, as before.

Changes:

- Three entries in the table, ordered after LetsMesh, with `Custom…` last.
- `ObserverBrokerPreset.id` is now `string` instead of a closed union, so the next analyzer is one table entry, one `en.json` string and one docs row.
- `en.json`: three label keys (brand names, not translated).
- Docs: three rows in the presets table of `docs/features/meshcore-analyzer-observer.md`, with links to each operator's reference. The page names no analyzer backend, so it does not mention Beacon or CoreScope.

**meshcore.ca** — fetched https://meshcore.ca/analyzer/broker-reference/ and the machine-readable https://meshcore.ca/analyzer/observer-config.json (version 2026.09) it links:

- Primary `mqtt1.meshcore.ca`, Backup `mqtt2.meshcore.ca`; port 443; transport WebSockets; TLS required, verify certificates; auth "MeshCore JWT token"; audience equals the host. Matches the issue.
- Topics `meshcore/{IATA}/{PUBLIC_KEY}/packets` and `/status`, IATA is a three-letter code; the pyMC row says `format: letsmesh`. This is what MeshMonitor already publishes.

title: fix(meshcore): per-section /snapshot grants, anonymous neighbour reads, and tabs that follow their grant (#5666, #5667, #5668)
body:
Closes #5666
Closes #5667
Closes #5668

Three MeshCore permission faults, fixed on the rules the #5655–#5665 series set. No new helper or rule: the routes now agree with the MeshCore rows of `socketEventGates.ts`.

## #5667: `/snapshot` gave out nodes and contacts on `connection:read`

`GET /api/sources/:id/meshcore/snapshot` keeps `connection:read` as its route gate (the page needs it to load). Each section is now returned only to a caller who could read it through its own route, on that source. A section the caller may not read is empty, not a 403: `useMeshCore` reads all five keys on first load, and a viewer holding only some grants still needs the shell.

| Section | Grant on the source | Same as route | Before |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status`, `status.localNode`, `deviceTypeName` | `connection:read` | `GET /status` | same |
| `contacts` | `nodes:read` | `GET /contacts` | **`connection:read`** |
| `nodes` | `nodes:read` | `GET /nodes` | **`connection:read`** |
| position fields on both | `nodes:viewOnMap` | same routes | same |
| `messages` | `messages:read`: all. Else `channel_N:read`: that channel's messages only (no DM, no room post) | `GET /messages`, `GET /messages/channel/:idx` | `messages:read` only |
| keyed (repeater-decrypted) messages | read access to the key too (#5551) | same | same |
| `seqCursor` | newest returned message | | same |

Contacts and nodes are not read from the manager at all without `nodes:read`.

One section got wider, on purpose: a viewer with `channel_0:read` and no `messages:read` now gets channel 0's recent messages in the snapshot. The socket (`meshcore:message`) and `GET /messages/channel/:idx` already gave them those; the snapshot was the odd one out.

## #5668: `/neighbors` refused the anonymous account

`GET /neighbors` had `requireAuth()` before `requirePermission('nodes', 'read')`, so `anonymous` got 401 whatever it held. It is a read of stored rows and now uses `optionalAuth()`.

`POST /neighbors/request` transmits. It keeps `requireAuth()`, with a comment saying why.

### Audit of every MeshCore route (122 routes, 9 routers)

Two faults looked for: a read behind `requireAuth()` that blocks a granted anonymous viewer, and a read with no per-source grant check. Every permission gate on these routers already names the source (`sourceIdFrom: 'params.id'`).

Routes changed:

| Route | Method | Gate before | Verdict | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/snapshot` | GET | `connection:read` for every section | read with no grant check on nodes, contacts | per-section gates (above) |
| `/neighbors` | GET | `requireAuth` + `nodes:read` | blocks granted anonymous | `optionalAuth` + `nodes:read` |
| `/nodes/:publicKey/position-history` | GET | `nodes:read` | returns positions without `nodes:viewOnMap` | empty trail without `nodes:viewOnMap` |
| `/config/discoverable` | GET | `requireAuth` + `configuration:read` | blocks granted anonymous; reads a stored setting | `optionalAuth` |
| `/config/default-scope` | GET | same

title: ci: bound the ClamAV install step and add job timeouts
body:
## What hung

On PR #5665 the **ClamAV Scan** job (run 37674527179, attempt 1) sat in "Install & update ClamAV" from 19:28 to 23:01 UTC, 3.5 hours, until a force-cancel. No step or job in `ci.yml` had a timeout, so only GitHub's 6-hour limit bounded it.

The job log shows the stall was in **`apt-get update`**, not `freshclam`: the runner's Azure Ubuntu mirror stopped answering (`Ign: http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com ...`), apt fell back to `archive.ubuntu.com`, printed its last line at 19:29:01 and then never returned. The slowest healthy run on record (323s) was the same mirror serving packages at 54 kB/s. `freshclam` has never been the slow part, but it has the same exposure, so all three network calls are now bounded.

## ClamAV job, measured (55 successful runs)

| | min | median | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| Whole job | 5.4 min | 9.9 min | 13.2 min |
| Install & update ClamAV | 15 s | 19 s | 323 s |
| Scan source tree | 270 s | 527 s | 588 s |

## ClamAV change

- `apt-get update` (120s), the package download (`apt-get install --download-only`, 300s) and `freshclam` (300s) each run under `timeout`, 3 attempts, 15s apart. A stall prints a warning per attempt and then an error that says the download stalled and is not a scan result.
- The download is split from the install so a kill can never land inside `dpkg`; apt keeps partial files, so a retry resumes.
- Step `timeout-minutes: 20` (3.7x the 323s worst case). Job `timeout-minutes: 45` (3.4x the 13.2 min worst case).
- **No database cache.** The job runs only on `pull_request`, and a cache saved on a PR branch is not visible to other PRs, so a cache would only help re-runs of the same PR. The download takes about 10 seconds when healthy, and the stall that prompted this was apt, which a database cache does not touch.

## Job timeouts added

Durations are successful runs from the last 40-80 runs of each workflow.

| Workflow | Job | Measured max (min) | Timeout (min) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ci | Test Suite (22/24/25) | 26.2 | 90 |
| ci | Build Check | 2.2 | 15 |
| ci | Documentation Build | 1.1 | 15 |
| ci | Docker Build | 5.9 | 30 |
| ci | Security Scan | 1.8 | 15 |
| ci | ClamAV Scan | 13.2 | 45 |
| ci | PR Comment | 1.2 | 10 |
| claude-code-review | claude-review | 4.9 | 30 |
| codeql | Analyze | 4.6 | 30 |
| deploy-docs | build / deploy | 1.6 / 1.2 | 15 / 15 |
| desktop-ci | build-windows | 24.6 | 90 |
| desktop-ci | build-macos / build-macos-x64 | 15.0 / 13.0 | 60 / 60 |
| desktop-ci | lint-rust | 31.7 (median 1.2) | 90 |
| desktop-release | build-windows / build-macos / build-macos-x64 | 22.3 / 22.6 / 18.2 | 120 each |
| docker-publish | create-manifest | 0.3 | 15 |
| dockerfile-image-check | Verify Base Images Exist | 0.8 | 10 |
| lxc-template-build | build-lxc-template | 5.7 | 30 |
| release | Validate / Update Release / Notify | 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.1 | 10 each |
| release | Full Test Suite | 47.8 | 150 |
| release | Build Artifacts | 2.1 | 20 |
| reticulum-bridge | Bridge Tests | 1.0 | 15 |

title: fix(permissions): gate every WebSocket event on the recipient's grants, per source
body:
## The fault

The WebSocket pushes the same data the REST routes serve, with none of their permission checks. Verified on main (255e59545):

- `webSocketService.ts` forwarded every `dataEventEmitter` event to every connected socket. The only per-event check was the #5551 key check on repeater-decrypted MeshCore messages.
- A socket that had joined no source room received events from every source (`if (sourceRooms.length > 0 && event.sourceId)`). Any signed-in user could stay in that state, and a user refused `join-source` was left in it.
- `join-source` checked `messages:read` on the source and nothing else. Once joined, the socket got every channel's messages, node updates, traceroutes, the raw channel row with its PSK (`channel:updated`) and the rest, whatever the user's channel, `nodes_private` or `traceroute` grants.
- `firmware:status` carried no source and reached every socket. The firmware routes are admin only.
- `meshbeacon:received` (an automation-engine event) carried the offered channel PSK to every socket.
- The socket read `isAdmin` from the session at connect, so a demoted admin kept admin delivery; a deactivated or deleted user's socket stayed open.

Two REST routes that serve the same rows as `GET /api/poll` had the gaps #5661 listed:

- `GET /api/traceroutes/recent` had no check and read every source.
- `GET /api/config` returned `localNodeInfo` and the firmware version of any named source to every caller, signed in or not, and the source's own TCP port.

There is no issue for this work; it finishes the series #5655–#5658, #5660, #5661, #5664.

## The change

### Every event type has a declared gate

`src/server/services/socketEventGates.ts` holds `SOCKET_EVENT_GATES`, one entry per event type, mirroring `POLL_SECTION_GATES`. It is typed `Record<DataEventType, SocketEventGate>`, so a new event type does not compile without a gate (checked: adding a member to the union fails `tsc` with TS2741). `firmware:status` was raised with a string outside the union; it is now a member. At run time an event whose type has no entry is sent to no one, admins included, and a test reads the server sources for any type raised outside the union.

Each gate is checked on the event's own source. Admins get every event with the payload they got before.

| Event | Scope | REST route serving the same data | Gate for a viewer who is not an admin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message:new` | source | `GET /api/poll` (`messages`) | Channel message: `channel_0:read` and `channel_N:read` on the source. DM: `messages:read` on the source. Virtual channel: the per-entry `canRead` grant. |
| `node:updated` | source | `GET /api/poll` (`nodes`) | `channel_N:viewOnMap` on the source, N = the channel the node was last heard on (read from the node row, once per event). A private position override is removed without `nodes_private:read` on the source. |
| `channel:updated` | source | `GET /api/poll` (`channels`) | `channel_N:read` on the source; sent through `transformChanne

title: fix(permissions): scope embeds and the v1 API per source; MeshCore telemetry ids; restart is admin only
body:
Continues the per-source permission series (#5655–#5658, #5660) on the public and token-facing surfaces: anonymous embeds, the v1 API, MeshCore ids on the telemetry routes, and `POST /api/system/restart`. There is no issue for this work; the faults are described below.

## The faults

**Embeds** (`/api/embed/:profileId/…`, anonymous):
- A node with a **private position override** was drawn at its private coordinates. Nothing checked `positionOverrideIsPrivate`.
- `neighborinfo` did not skip nodes hidden from the map; `nodes` and `traceroutes` did. The three routes each carried their own copy of the filter.
- `neighborinfo` answered when the profile had "Show Neighbor Info" off (`traceroutes` already 404s when its option is off).
- A reported position was shown whatever channel it arrived on, and a traceroute was drawn whatever channel it was heard on.
- A profile with no channel selected showed nodes on Channel Database (server-decrypted) channels, which a profile cannot name.

**v1 API** (`/api/v1/sources/{id}/…`, API tokens):
- `GET …/nodes` and `…/nodes/{id}` returned `latitudeOverride` / `longitudeOverride` / `altitudeOverride` for private overrides with no `nodes_private` check.
- `GET …/network/topology` returned the effective position (private override included) for every node on the source, with no channel check, and every traceroute as `edges` with no `traceroute:read`.
- `GET …/network/direct-neighbors` returned every source's statistics whichever source the path named (the old TODO).
- `GET …/telemetry?type=…` and `GET …/telemetry/count` read every source.
- `GET …/nodes/{id}/position-history` looked up the node with no source, so the privacy flag of another source's row decided.
- `GET …/nodes/{id}` read uptime with no source.
- `GET …/nodes/{num}/copy-candidates` listed sources the user cannot read.
- `GET …/status` for an MQTT or MeshCore source answered with the primary source's node and link, and gave the node identity to any token with the install-wide `info:read`.
- `GET /api/v1/metrics` exported per-node series for nodes on channels the user cannot view.
- Position telemetry of a private node was returned without `nodes_private:read`.

The report said `/api/v1/nodes` "merges channel grants across sources when no source is named". Checked: the root paths 404 since 4.14 and every per-source router is mounted behind `attachSource`, so that branch (`sourceId ?? ALL_SOURCES`, `getUserPermissionSetAsync(userId)`) is not reachable over HTTP today. It is removed anyway: a handler now takes its source from `requireScopedSourceId()` and answers 400 `MISSING_SOURCE_ID` if mounted without `attachSource`. The `default` alias resolves to one source and is then checked like any other.

**MeshCore ids on telemetry routes**: `checkNodeChannelAccess` passed any signed-in user for a 64-hex public key, on any source.

**`POST /api/system/restart`** passed on `settings:write` for any source.

## Design

- **Embeds: the profile is the whole rule.**

+An API token carries the permissions of the user who made it, and each request

With no channel selected, nodes on every device channel (0-7) appear. Nodes last heard on a Channel Database (server-decrypted) channel never appear on an embed.

+The viewer of an embed is anonymous, so the profile alone decides what is sent:

 ### No Session Required
 
 Embed endpoints operate outside the authenticated API. They bypass CSRF protection and rate limiting since the profile ID itself controls access. The embed CSP middleware validates the profile exists and is enabled before serving any data.

 **`GET /api/poll` follows the same rules, section by section.** `POLL_SECTION_GATES` in `pollRoutes.ts` lists every top-level key of the reply with its gate; the reply object is typed from it, and `pollRoutes.scope.test.ts` fails on a key that is not listed. The handler loads the caller's grants once (`loadNodeViewAccess`, no query for an admin) and answers every check from them for the source the data is from: the named source, or with no `sourceId` each row's own source. A caller who names a source they hold nothing on gets `200` with empty sections, not a 403, because every page polls this route. `traceroutes`, `deviceNodeNums` and `config.localNodeInfo` / `deviceMetadata` had no per-source gate before. With no `sourceId` there is no `messages` section for any caller.
 
+**The v1 API is checked on the source in the path, and a handler has no "no source" branch.** Every per-source v1 router is mounted under `/api/v1/sources/:sourceId/…` behind `attachSource(resource, action)`. A handler reads its source from `requireScopedSourceId(req, res)` (`routes/v1/sourceParam.ts`), which takes it from `req.source` and answers 400 `MISSING_SOURCE_ID` if the router was mounted without `attachSource`. The handlers used to carry `sourceId ?? ALL_SOURCES` and a merged-grants branch left over from the root paths removed in 4.14; unreachable today, but one stray mount away from reading every source. Row-level decisions (channel, private position) come from `loadV1Access(req)`: one `loadNodeViewAccess` per request, and `scopeNodeRowsForViewer(rows, access, sourceId)` for raw node rows. A token is its creator (`resolveBearerUser`), so these are the user's per-source grants. Reads that had named no source at all: `telemetry?type=`, `telemetry/count`, `network/direct-neighbors`, the single-node uptime, and the node row behind the position-history privacy check. `publicSurfaces.scope.test.ts` classifies every v1 route and fails on `ALL_SOURCES` in a per-source v1 router.
+
+**An embed has no viewer to check, so the profile is the whole rule.** `visibleEmbedNodes(profile)` (`embedPublicRoutes.ts`) is the one place that decides which nodes a profile shows and where: the profile's source, its channels (never a channel-database channel, which a profile cannot name), not hidden from the map, and never a node with a private position override, since nothing an anonymous viewer holds can satisfy `nodes_private:read` and a profile has no setting for it. A new embed route that carries node data must draw from the same function; the guard in `publicSurfaces.scope.test.ts` fails on a second node read in that file.
+
+**An action on the whole install is admin only.** `POST /api/system/restart` passed on `settings:write` for any source. Like the run-now jobs, it uses `requireAdmin()` (`FORBIDDEN_ADMIN`).
+
 **A job that works on every source is admin only**, not `settings:write`: a grant on one source is not a grant over the others (`POST /api/settings/auto-enrichment/run-now`, `/position-estimation/run-now`). The scope guards detect `requireAdmin()` through `isAdminGate()`.

title: docs(mqtt): explain missing MQTT traffic; warn on the source card when client proxy has no link
body:
Refs #5013. The issue stays open until the reporter answers; this PR ships the docs the maintainer promised there, and makes the most likely cause visible.

## The fault this addresses

A node with MQTT **Proxy to Client** on opens no broker connection of its own. It hands each publish to its client and waits for the client to hand broker traffic back. MeshMonitor does that only through the source's `mqttLink`. With no link, the node hears MQTT traffic only when another node repeats it over LoRa, which is what #5013 describes. Until now the only sign was a banner on Device → MQTT, and the log said nothing.

Each point of the diagnosis was checked in code before it went into the docs:

- Firmware (`src/mqtt/MQTT.cpp` `onReceiveProto` / `shouldDropMqttDownlink`, `Router.cpp`): a broker packet is dropped when the channel (matched by name) lacks `downlink_enabled`, and when `lora.ignore_mqtt` is on. A packet that passes goes to the router like any other.
- MeshMonitor has no filter that drops MQTT-origin packets on a node source.
- One correction to the wording in the issue thread: with no link, MeshMonitor does not always drop the node's proxy frames. `processIncomingData` hands each one to the newest Virtual Node client (`broadcastToProxyDelegate`, #4037) and drops it only when no client is connected. The docs say so.

## What changed

### 1. Docs

New section **Why don't I see MQTT traffic?** in `docs/features/mqtt-broker.md` (anchor `#why-no-mqtt-traffic`):

- How a node gets MQTT traffic (own WiFi; client proxy through a linked source; the MQTT Proxy sidecar)
- The node drops the packet (Downlink Enabled, channel/key, Ignore MQTT; airtime warning for downlink)
- Proxy to Client is on, but nothing is linked (the three places MeshMonitor says so; fix in six steps with the real UI labels; the sidecar case)
- I want to log everything on the broker (add an MQTT Bridge source)
- Tell the cases apart (which Packet Monitor shows the packet; the debug log line)

Linked from `docs/add-ons/mqtt-proxy.md`, `docs/features/device.md` (whose tip told users to turn Proxy to Client on and deploy the sidecar, with no word on linked sources) and a new FAQ entry.

### 2. Warning on the source card

![MQTT not linked badge on a source card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/docs/5013-mqtt-downlink-visibility/docs/public/images/features/5013-mqtt-not-linked-card.png)

- **One rule:** `isMqttProxyLinkMisconfigured` in `src/utils/mqttProxyLink.ts`. Device → MQTT applies it to its form values; `GET /api/sources/:id/status` applies it to the device's cached module config. They cannot disagree.
- **No new requests.** The dashboard did not have `proxy_to_client_enabled`. The flag rides the status poll each card already makes, as `mqttProxyUnlinked: true`, present only when the rule holds.
- **Permission.** The flag is device configuration, so it needs what `GET /api/config/current` needs: `configuration` read on that source. Admins get it; a user with ot

-When using MeshMonitor, enable this option and deploy the [MQTT Client Proxy sidecar](/add-ons/mqtt-proxy). The proxy container handles all MQTT forwarding automatically.
+With this option on, the node opens no broker connection of its own, so something must carry MQTT for it. Pick one:

title: fix(config): send a stored 0 interval as 0, one channel read-back, drop dead desktop Virtual Node checkboxes
body:
Three follow-ups to #5652 / #5659. No issue was filed for this work; the faults are described below.

## 1. A stored 0 interval was raised to a floor on Save

A node reports 0 for a broadcast interval left at the firmware default. Both save paths raised that 0 to MeshMonitor's floor before sending:

| Field | Stored 0 means | Save used to send | Save now sends |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position broadcast interval | 1 h (12 h for router roles) on 2.7 and 2.8; 15 min on older firmware | 32 | 0 |
| Node-info broadcast interval | 3 h | 3600 | 0 |

So saving any field in the Position section of a default node set a 32-second position broadcast.

**Change.** `src/utils/broadcastIntervalFloor.ts` holds the two floors and one rule: 0 stays 0, any other value under the floor is raised (frontend) or refused (server). Used by:

- `ConfigurationTab.tsx` `handleSaveDeviceConfig` / `handleSavePositionConfig` (local)
- `AdminCommandsTab.tsx` `handleSetDeviceConfig` / `handleSetPositionConfig` (remote)
- `configRoutes.ts` `POST /device`, `POST /position`
- `adminRoutes.ts` `/commands` `setDeviceConfig`, `setPositionConfig`

No floor is loosened. A typed 5 is still blocked by `NumberInput` and still raised by the save handler.

**New: the server now refuses a non-zero value under the floor** (400 `POSITION_INTERVAL_BELOW_FLOOR` / `NODE_INFO_INTERVAL_BELOW_FLOOR`). Before this PR the floors lived only in the browser; the four routes passed any number to the encoder. The numbers are the UI's existing 32 and 3600, not new ones. Device-backup restore (`deviceRestoreService`) calls the manager directly and stays verbatim, as designed in #4926; a test pins that it passes 0 as 0.

**Firmware check** (tags `v2.7.26.54e0d8d` and `v2.8.1.8e6a88d`; same on both unless noted):

- `Default::getConfiguredOrDefaultMs` (`src/mesh/Default.cpp`): `configuredInterval > 0 ? configuredInterval : defaultInterval`. 0 is the "use the default" sentinel for both fields.
- Position: `PositionModule::runOnce` uses `default_broadcast_interval_secs` = `IF_ROUTER(ONE_DAY / 2, 60 * 60)` (`Default.h`). `AdminModule::handleSetConfig` does `config.position = c.payload_variant.position;` with no rewrite, so a 0 (left off the wire by proto3) is stored as 0. **A stored 0 keeps the default.**
- Node-info: `NodeInfoModule::runOnce` uses `default_node_info_broadcast_secs` = 3 h. But `handleSetConfig` runs `if (config.device.node_info_broadcast_secs < min_node_info_broadcast_secs) ... = min_node_info_broadcast_secs;` right after `config.device = c.payload_variant.device;`, with no exemption for 0. **A sent 0 is stored as 3600.** The node cannot hold 0 after any save of the Device section, whatever the client sends.
- Whole-struct replace: both cases assign the whole sub-struct, and `PositionConfig` / `DeviceConfig` have no `has_` flags. Every field the sender leaves out becomes 0/false. The new route tests decode the encoded packet and assert the other fields of each section are on the wire next to the omitt

title: fix(permissions): gate every section of GET /api/poll on the source its data comes from
body:
Continues the per-source permission series (#5655, #5656, #5657, #5658). There is no issue for this; the fault is described here.

## The fault

`GET /api/poll` takes an optional `sourceId` and builds ten sections from several tables and several permissions.

- **No `sourceId`:** the handler loaded the caller's grants merged across every source (`getUserPermissionSetAsync(userId)`, `filterNodesByChannelPermission(rows, user)`) and applied them to rows read from every source. `channel_0:viewOnMap` on source A returned source B's channel-0 nodes, `channel_0:read` on A returned B's channel list and unread counts, and so on.
- **Named `sourceId`:** nodes, messages, channels and unread counts were already checked on that source. Three sections had no per-source gate, and one was checked without a source:
  - `traceroutes`: no gate at all. Every caller, signed in or not, got the source's last 24 h of traceroutes with their `routePositions`.
  - `deviceNodeNums`: no gate.
  - `config.localNodeInfo` / `config.deviceMetadata`: any signed-in user got the named source's local node id, names, firmware version and reboot count.
  - `deviceConfig`: `hasPermission(user, 'configuration', 'read')` with no source, so `configuration:read` on A returned B's device config by naming B.

## What changed

The handler loads the caller's grants once (`loadNodeViewAccess`, from #5658) and answers every check in memory for the source the data is from: the named source, or with no `sourceId` each row's own source. With no `sourceId` a caller who is not an admin is served from the sources they hold the section's grant on; the source list goes into the query (`withSourceScope` list form) and each row is still checked on its own source.

`POLL_SECTION_GATES` in `pollRoutes.ts` declares the gate for every top-level key. The reply object is typed from it, so a new key does not compile until it is declared, and a test fails on any undeclared key in a reply.

### Sections

"Admin" is unchanged in every row. "Before" is for a caller who is not an admin.

| Key | Data | Gate before | Gate now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `connection` | manager status of the named source, else the primary | Flags: everyone. `nodeIp`: signed in + `sources:read` (#5619) | Same. No `connection:read` requirement added. |
| `nodes` | `nodes` rows; estimated positions and asset flags (both global by design) attached per visible node | Named: `channel_N:viewOnMap` on the source; private override on `nodes_private:read` on the source. None named: both merged across sources | `channel_N:viewOnMap` and `nodes_private:read` on the row's own source. None named: rows dropped and private overrides removed before the per-node merge, as `GET /api/nodes` does. A named source the caller holds no node grant on is not read. |
| `messages` | newest 100 `messages` rows of the named source | Named: `channel_0:read` + `channel_N:read`; DMs `messages:read`; virtual channels per-entry `canRead`. None named: section absent (the read t

title: fix(permissions): check private positions per source; scope telemetry reads and /api/status; one rule for a source's address
body:
Continues the per-source permission series (#5655, #5656, #5657, #5658). No issue: the maintainer asked for these four items directly.

## The faults

1. **Position gate.** `buildPositionFilter()` checked `nodes_private:read` with no source. That check passes on a grant for any source, so a user allowed to see private positions on source A saw the private positions held on source B.
2. **Telemetry reads.** `info` and `dashboard` are install-wide grants. The telemetry routes are gated on them and then read per-source rows, in three places from every source.
3. **`GET /api/status`.** It gave any caller, logged in or not, the primary node's number, id and names, and node/message/channel counts across every source.
4. **A source's address.** #5658 made the connection routes need `sources:read` AND `connection:read` for `nodeIp` / `defaultIp`, while `/api/poll`, `/api/config` and the source list show the address on `sources:read` alone (#5619). Two rules for one fact.

A note on item 3: the request named `GET /api/system/status`. That route is gated on `dashboard:read` and returns version, platform, memory and database type; it holds no node identity and no counts. The route that matches the description is `GET /api/status`, so that is the one reduced here. `/api/system/status` is unchanged.

## What changed

### 1. Position gate: each row is checked on its own source

`buildPositionFilter()` and `buildMeshCorePositionFilter()` now load the caller's grants once (`loadSourcePermissions`, one query) and answer per row: `channel_N:viewOnMap` on the row's source, and `nodes_private:read` on the row's source for a private position. The call signature is unchanged apart from a new optional last argument (grants already loaded), so no caller had to change how it calls the predicate. Every caller already passed the row's own `sourceId`.

| Caller | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/analysis/positions` | private fixes shown with `nodes_private:read` on any source | shown only with it on the fix's source |
| `GET /api/analysis/coverage-grid` | same, as grid density | same rule |
| `GET /api/analysis/coverage/receivers` | private receiver position kept | nulled unless granted on the receiver's source |
| `GET /api/analysis/coverage/senders` | private sender listed | left out unless granted on that source |
| `GET /api/analysis/coverage/receptions` | private sender's rows returned; private receiver position kept | rows dropped / position nulled, per source |
| `GET /api/analysis/coverage/surveys` | survey of a private sender listed | listed only if the sender is visible on a source the caller holds the grant on |
| `GET /api/analysis/cross-source-links` | edge to a private endpoint drawn | each endpoint checked on the source whose table holds its row; the two-source rule is unchanged |
| `GET /api/analysis/cross-source-links/traceroute-confirmed` | link to a private node drawn | checked on the link's own source |
| `GET /api/aircraft/trails` | private ai

title: fix(admin): explain a stored 0, one request per Owner/Channels Load, drop dead Virtual Node env vars
body:
Three small follow-ups. No issue: the maintainer asked for each directly.

## 1. A stored 0 now says what it means

#5652 let five fields accept 0, because a node reports 0 for "not set, use the firmware default". The field took the 0 but gave no clue what it meant, and three of the save handlers quietly turn it into something else.

`NumberInput` gains a `zeroHint` prop. While the field's value is 0 (typed or loaded) the text shows under the field, linked with `aria-describedby`; it goes away at any other value. It is `aria-hidden` for the same reason as the visible error reason: a sibling span would otherwise join a wrapping label's name. All eight `alsoValid={[0]}` sites pass one, and a test fails if a new one does not.

![hint under the position interval](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/fix/default-hint-load-retries/docs/public/images/features/zero-hint-position-interval.png)

| Field | Forms | Firmware default | A saved 0 becomes (unchanged) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position broadcast interval | Device Config, Admin Commands | 15 min up to 2.7.x, 1 h on firmware master; 12 h for ROUTER / ROUTER_LATE (`default_broadcast_interval_secs`, `Default.h`) | MeshMonitor sends **32** |
| Node-info broadcast interval | Device Config, Admin Commands | 3 h (`default_node_info_broadcast_secs`) | MeshMonitor sends **3600** (firmware would raise it to 3600 itself) |
| Hop limit | Device Config, Admin Commands | factory value 3 (`HOP_RELIABLE`, set in `NodeDB::installDefaultConfig`) | MeshMonitor sends **1** |
| Neighbor-info interval | Admin Commands | 6 h (`default_neighbor_info_broadcast_secs`) | MeshMonitor sends **0**; firmware `AdminModule` stores 21600 |
| MQTT map-report precision | Device Config | 14 bits (`default_map_position_precision`, `MQTT.h`) | MeshMonitor sends **0**; firmware uses 14 |

Defaults were read from meshtastic/firmware at `6d41e279` and tags v2.5.20, v2.6.11, v2.7.15. The pinned protobufs comment for `node_info_broadcast_secs` says 900 s; the firmware has used 3 h since at least 2.5, so the hint follows the firmware.

No floor and no value sent to a radio changed. The hints are worded to match: "Save sends 32 seconds, not 0."

Two things worth a look, both left alone:

- **A loaded 0 plus Save changes the node.** A node on the default position interval reports 0; pressing Save sends 32 s, about the fastest setting allowed. Same shape for hop limit (0 becomes 1) and node-info (0 becomes 1 h, not 3 h). The hint now says so, but the floor could send the 0 through instead.
- **Hop limit 0 may not mean "default".** `Router::allocForSending` uses `config.lora.hop_limit` as is (`getConfiguredOrDefaultHopLimit` only clamps values of 7 and above), so a stored 0 looks like zero hops, not 3. The hint says "not set on the node (the factory value is 3)" and makes no claim that 0 behaves as 3.

## 2. One request per click for Owner and Channels Load

title: fix(permissions): scope optional-sourceId reads to the caller's sources; make install-wide jobs admin only
body:
Follow-up to #5655, #5656 and #5657. Those PRs left four items. There is no issue for this work; the faults are described below.

## The faults

1. **Two install-wide jobs were open to `settings:write` on any one source.** `POST /api/settings/auto-enrichment/run-now` and `POST /api/settings/position-estimation/run-now` work on every source.
2. **Connection reads checked no per-source permission.** `GET /api/virtual-node/status` gave any signed-in user every source's virtual-node settings and client list (with client IP addresses). `GET /api/connection/info` gave any signed-in user the TCP port and override flag of any source. `GET /api/connection` gave the node address of any source to a holder of `sources:read`.
3. **Reads with no `sourceId` merged the caller's grants across sources.** `GET /api/nodes`, `/api/nodes/active`, `/api/messages/unread-counts` and `/api/messages/first-unread` read rows from every source and filtered them with "holds this channel on some source". `channel_0` on source A showed source B's channel-0 nodes and counted B's unread messages. `nodes_private:read` on one source unmasked private position overrides on all of them.
4. **Position history ignored the source.** `GET /api/nodes/:id/position-history` and `/api/nodes/:id/positions` checked channel access on the named source, then read the node's fixes from every source. `/positions` had no private-position check.

## What changed

| Route | Rule now |
|---|---|
| `POST /settings/auto-enrichment/run-now`, `/position-estimation/run-now` | `requireAdmin()`. Non-admin: 403 `FORBIDDEN_ADMIN`. Maintainer decision. |
| `GET /nodes`, `/nodes/active` | Each row is checked on its own source: `viewOnMap` on the row's channel there, and `nodes_private:read` there for a private override. No `sourceId`, non-admin: only sources where the caller holds a channel grant are queried. Rows are dropped and masked before the cross-source merge. Naming a source the caller holds nothing on returns `[]`, as before. |
| `GET /messages/unread-counts`, `/first-unread` | No `sourceId`, non-admin: the sum (or the oldest) over the sources the caller may read, each computed under that source's grants and its own local node. Naming a source the caller holds nothing on: 403, as before. |
| `GET /nodes/:id/position-history`, `/positions` | The telemetry query is scoped to the permitted sources. Named source: that source only. No `sourceId`, non-admin: the sources where the caller passes the channel rule, minus those where the position is private and they lack `nodes_private:read`. 403 when no source passes the channel rule. |
| `GET /connection` | Every caller: the four link flags. `connection:read` on the source: the full status. Plus `sources:read`: `nodeIp`. |
| `GET /connection/info` | Signed-in callers. Same three levels; ports and the override flag need `connection:read`. |

title: fix(permissions): check mesh-request, announce, connection and channel permissions against the target source
body:
Follow-up to #5655, for the next group of routes its audit listed. No issue was filed for this work.

## The fault

`requirePermission(resource, action)` without `sourceIdFrom` is not tied to a source. For a per-source resource it passes when the user holds the permission on any source. The routes below then acted on the `sourceId` in the request, so a user allowed to send a traceroute, announce, or disconnect on source A could do it on source B by naming B.

The per-channel checks inside the `channelRoutes.ts` handlers had the same fault in another form: `hasPermission(user, 'channel_N', action)` with no source argument.

## The fix

Each route now uses `requireDeviceSourcePermission(resource, action, 'query' | 'body')` from #5655. It resolves the target once (the named source, else the primary Meshtastic source), checks the permission on that source, and hands the handler the same manager through `getDeviceSourceTarget(req)`. Handlers no longer call `resolveSourceManager()` or re-read `sourceId`.

title: fix(permissions): check nodes, settings and message routes against the target source
body:
Follow-up to #5655. No issue; the maintainer asked for this directly.

## The fault

`requirePermission(resource, action)` with no `sourceIdFrom` is not tied to a source. For a per-source resource it passes when the user holds the permission on ANY source. Many routes in `nodesRoutes`, `ignoredNodeRoutes`, `settingsRoutes` and `messageRoutes` were gated that way and then acted on the `sourceId` in the request, or on every source when none was sent. A user with a grant on source A could read or change source B by naming it, and could read every source's rows by naming none.

#5655 fixed this for the `configuration` device routes. This PR applies the same rule to the routes its audit listed, and to the other routes in those four files with the same gap.

## The fix

`src/server/utils/sourceScopedAccess.ts` (new; `deviceSourcePermission.ts` and `authMiddleware.ts` are not changed):

- `requireSourcePermission(resource, action, { whenOmitted, device? })` resolves the source once, checks the permission on it, and hands the handler the same value through `getSourceTarget(req)`.
- `sourceId` is read from the query or the body. Different values in the two: 400 `SOURCE_ID_CONFLICT`. Not a string: 400.
- A named source that does not exist: 404 `SOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, after the permission check (a caller without the grant gets 403 and learns nothing).
- `device: 'meshtastic'` routes refuse a source with no radio of its own (400 `SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` / 409 `SOURCE_NOT_CONNECTED`), as #5655 does. Other routes serve every source type.
- `whenOmitted` is the route's rule for a request with no `sourceId`:
  - `primary`: the primary Meshtastic source; the check is on it.
  - `permitted`: admins keep every source; anyone else reaches only the sources they hold the permission on. Never refused outright if they hold it somewhere; never shown or allowed to change a source they lack it on.
  - `first-permitted`: the caller's first enabled source with the permission (what `resolveRequestSourceId` did).
  - `required`: 400 `MISSING_SOURCE_ID`.
- `requireSourcePairPermission()` for copy-nodeinfo: read on the source copied from AND write on the source copied to.

## Routes

| Route | Resource | No `sourceId` | Before |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST `/nodes/:nodeId/send-key-warning` | messages:write | primary (device) | union check; sent on the named source |
| POST `/nodes/:nodeNum/scan-remote-admin` | settings:write | primary (device) | same |
| POST `/auto-ping/stop/:nodeNum` | settings:write | primary (device) | same |
| POST `/nodes/refresh` | nodes:write | primary (device); counts are that source's | union check; counts were all sources' |
| POST `/nodes/scan-duplicate-keys` | nodes:write | permitted; takes an optional `sourceId` now | rewrote flags on every source |
| GET `/nodes/:nodeNum/copy-candidates` | nodes:read | required; candidates limited to sources the caller can read | listed every source's row |
| GET `/auto-favorite/status` | nodes:read | primary | union chec

title: fix(config): check device-config permissions against the target source
body:
## The fault

Permissions are per source. `requirePermission(resource, action)` only checks a specific source when it is given `sourceIdFrom`. Without it, the check for a per-source resource such as `configuration` passes if the user holds the permission on **any** source (`checkPermissionAsync` with no `sourceId` takes the union).

Most routes in `configRoutes.ts` called `requirePermission('configuration', 'read' | 'write')` with no `sourceIdFrom`, then acted on the `sourceId` in the request. A user allowed to configure source A could read and write source B's device config by naming B. #5639 fixed one route (`POST /api/config/module/:moduleType`). This PR fixes the rest of that file and the other `configuration`-gated device routes with the same fault.

There is no issue for this; the maintainer asked for the fix directly.

## Design

New `requireDeviceSourcePermission(resource, action, 'query' | 'body')` in `src/server/utils/deviceSourcePermission.ts`. One middleware, in this order:

1. Read `sourceId` from the one place the route declares. A non-string value is a 400. A different `sourceId` in the other place (query vs body) is a 400 `SOURCE_ID_CONFLICT`, so a request cannot name one source where the check looks and another elsewhere.
2. Resolve the manager once: the named source, or the primary Meshtastic source when `sourceId` is omitted.
3. Check the permission on that source (the named id, or the primary's id).
4. After the permission check, refuse a named source with no Meshtastic device (existing 400 `SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` / 409 `SOURCE_NOT_CONNECTED`). An unauthorised caller still gets 403 and learns nothing about the source's type.
5. Refuse a named source that resolved to another source's manager with 404 `SOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. `resolveSourceManager()` hands back the primary for an id it does not know; the handler must not act on a source the check did not cover.

Handlers take the manager and source id from `getDeviceSourceTarget(req)`. They no longer call `resolveSourceManager()` or re-read `sourceId`, so the check and the action use the same value.

`requirePermission` gains a function form of `sourceIdFrom` (used by the step above) and records what it gates, so a test can find an unscoped gate on a registered route.

## Routes changed

| Route | Permission | `sourceId` from |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/config/current` | configuration:read | query |
| `POST /api/config/device`, `/network`, `/lora`, `/position`, `/mqtt`, `/neighborinfo`, `/power`, `/display` | configuration:write | body |
| `POST /api/config/module/telemetry`, `/module/request`, `/module/:moduleType` | configuration:write | body |
| `POST /api/config/owner`, `/request` | configuration:write | body |
| `GET /api/device-config`, `GET /api/device/backup` | configuration:read | query |
| `POST /api/device/reboot`, `POST /api/device/purge-nodedb` | configuration:write | body |
| `POST /api/channels/encode-url` | configuration:read | body (required) |

title: docs(add-ons): describe Virtual Node sidecars and REST API clients separately
body:
## The fault

`docs/add-ons/index.md` → "How Add-ons Work" said **all** add-ons connect through the Virtual Node and require `ENABLE_VIRTUAL_NODE=true`. Two things are wrong with that:

1. The page lists three REST API clients (CardMesh, Mesh Screensaver, Mesh Widget) that never open the Virtual Node. They read the v1 REST API with a Bearer token.
2. MeshMonitor 4.0 removed `ENABLE_VIRTUAL_NODE` / `VIRTUAL_NODE_PORT`. Virtual Node is a per-source setting in the Dashboard (`docs/configuration/virtual-node.md`; no reader of either variable is left in `src/`).

There is no issue for this; the maintainer asked for a direct fix.

## What changed

**`docs/add-ons/index.md`**, "How Add-ons Work" only. The add-on entries are untouched.
- Intro line now says an add-on reaches MeshMonitor in one of two ways.
- Diagram keeps its box style and shows both paths: sidecars ↔ Virtual Node, and REST clients → `/api/v1` over HTTP(S) with a token.
- **Virtual Node sidecars**: needs a Meshtastic TCP source with Virtual Node on (Dashboard → Edit Source → Virtual Node), the port set there, and a network path to it. Says the old variables do nothing. Notes the configurator covers the MQTT Proxy only.
- **REST API clients**: web address, API token (user menu → API Token; one per user, a new one revokes the old), a read-only user to own it, source-scoped `/api/v1/sources/{sourceId}/…` paths with the `default` alias, and `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` for browser-hosted clients.

**`docs/add-ons/ai-responder.md`, `docs/add-ons/mqtt-proxy.md`**: the same stale claim. Removed `ENABLE_VIRTUAL_NODE=true` / `VIRTUAL_NODE_PORT=4404` from the prerequisites and compose samples, and pointed to the per-source setting. The MQTT Proxy page also said the configurator turns the Virtual Node on; it only publishes the port.

**`docs/development/api-reference.md`**: one line. It sent readers to "Settings → API Tokens", which does not exist; the token dialog opens from the user menu (`UserMenu.tsx`).

Both add-on categories on the page fit one of the two descriptions. The MQTT Proxy is a Virtual Node sidecar (it does not use MeshMonitor's MQTT sources), so no third kind was needed.

## Claims checked against code

| Claim | Source |
|---|---|
| Virtual Node env vars removed, per-source setting | `docs/configuration/virtual-node.md`, `DockerComposeConfigurator.vue`; no reader in `src/` |
| Token from user menu, one per user, new revokes old | `UserMenu.tsx`, `apiTokenRoutes.ts` (`/generate` "revokes existing token") |
| Token carries its user's permissions | `resolveBearerUser` in `authMiddleware.ts` |
| `default` source alias; root v1 paths gone in 4.14 | `routes/v1/sourceParam.ts`, `docs/development/api-reference.md` |
| No `Origin` header ⇒ allowed; unknown origin ⇒ blocked | `cors()` setup in `server.ts` |
| Swagger at `/api/v1/docs` | `routes/v1/index.ts` |

## Mesh impact checklist

Docs only. No packets, notifications, or timers.

## Tests

`npm run docs:build` exits 0 with no dead links. Checked

+                         └────────────────────────┘
 ```
 
-### Prerequisites
+### Virtual Node sidecars
 
-All add-ons require:
-1. **Virtual Node enabled** in MeshMonitor (`ENABLE_VIRTUAL_NODE=true`)
-2. **Virtual Node port exposed** (default: 4404)
-3. **Docker networking** so sidecar containers can reach MeshMonitor
+MQTT Proxy and AI Responder open a TCP connection to the [Virtual Node](/configuration/virtual-node) and speak the Meshtastic protocol, as a phone app does. They need:
 
-### Deploying Add-ons
+1. **A Meshtastic TCP source with Virtual Node on.** Virtual Node is off by default and you set it per source: **Dashboard → Edit Source → Virtual Node**. See [Enabling Virtual Node on a Source](/configuration/virtual-node#enabling-virtual-node-on-a-source). MeshMonitor 4.0 removed the `ENABLE_VIRTUAL_NODE` and `VIRTUAL_NODE_PORT` environment variables; they now do nothing.
+2. **The port you set there.** Most setups use 4404. Point the add-on at the same port.
+3. **A network path to that port.** A sidecar in the same Docker Compose file reaches it as `meshmonitor:<port>`. Publish the port on the host only if the add-on runs somewhere else.
 
-The easiest way to deploy add-ons is with the [Docker Compose Configurator](/configurator), which can generate the appropriate configuration. You can also add them manually to your existing `docker-compose.yml`.
+The [Docker Compose Configurator](/configurator) can add the MQTT Proxy to your compose file. Add the AI Responder by hand; its page has the block to paste.
+
+### REST API clients
+
+CardMesh, Mesh Screensaver, and Mesh Widget call the [v1 REST API](/development/api-reference) over HTTP(S). They never open the Virtual Node, so you can leave it off. They need:
+
+1. **MeshMonitor's web address**: the one you open in a browser, with your [`BASE_URL`](/configuration/#optional-variables) path if you set one.
+2. **An API token.** Sign in, open the user menu, choose **API Token**, and generate one. The client sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Each user holds one token; a new one revokes the old.
+3. **A read-only user to own the token.** A token can do whatever its creator can do. Create a user that can only read the sources the add-on needs, sign in as that user, and generate the token there.
+4. **Source-scoped paths.** Mesh data lives under `/api/v1/sources/{sourceId}/…`, and `default` names the primary source. MeshMonitor 4.14 removed the old root paths such as `/api/v1/nodes`; they return `404`.
+5. **An [`ALLOWED_ORIGINS`](/configuration/#security-reverse-proxy-variables) entry, for clients that run in a browser.** A web page or a widget host sends an `Origin` header, and MeshMonitor rejects origins that are not on the list. Native apps send no `Origin` header and need no entry.
+
+Each project's README covers install steps. The [API reference](/development/api-reference) lists every endpoint, and your own server shows the same docs at `/api/v1/docs`.
