title: feat(meshcore): auto return path for Trace Path (#5485)
body:
Closes #5485

## Problem
Trace Path sent only the contact's saved out-path (the repeaters), never the target, and nothing brought the packet back. So the trace stopped at the last repeater: it never reached a repeater target, and on multi-hop paths the initiator often couldn't hear the end. MeshCore One avoids this with **Auto Return Path**, which sends `outbound + mirroredReturn`.

## Fix
An **Auto return path** checkbox next to Trace Path, on by default and remembered per browser. The hop list depends on the target type:

| Target | `outPath = [5e]`, target `f6` | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Repeater / room server | `[5e, f6, 5e]` | Repeaters forward direct TRACE packets. Firmware puts `path_len` in a TRACE packet's hash ("TRACE packets can revisit same node on return path", `Packet.cpp`), so a revisit isn't dropped as a duplicate. |
| Companion / sensor | turn at the last repeater: `[a, b]` → `[a, b, a]` | A companion only forwards a trace when repeat is on (`MyMesh::allowPacketForward` → `isRepeatEn()`), and it's off by default. Looping through one would time out. |

Other behavior:
- Falls back to one-way if the round trip would exceed the firmware's trace limit (63 hops, `MAX_PATH_SIZE`).
- The results table labels each row with the hop actually traced (the server now returns `path`), so a return leg reads `5e, f6, 5e` rather than the out-path indices.
- **Automations keep the one-way trace**: the manager's `autoReturn` option defaults to off, and only the UI route turns it on. Only a literal `true` in the request body enables it.

## Mesh impact
Trace is a single direct packet the user starts, with no timer. The return leg raises it from N to 2N−1 hops (3 instead of 1 for a 1-hop repeater). The toggle's tooltip says it uses about twice the airtime. Scheduled automation traces are unchanged.

## Tests
- `buildTracePathHops`: one-way, repeater loop, companion turnaround, 2-byte width, 63-hop fallback, empty path.
- Manager: the bytes sent to the bridge for each case, plus the default-off path.
- Route (`createRouteTestApp`): forwards `autoReturn: true`; no body, `false` or non-boolean values stay one-way.
- Panel: the toggle is on by default, is remembered, sends the flag, and rows use the traced path.
- Full suite: 23,280 passed, 0 failed. `tsc` (server and frontend) and `lint:ci` clean.

## Also fixed: Trace Path resent itself every 30 s
Found while validating. The trace waits up to 60 s for the radio (`sendBridgeCommand(..., 60000)`), but `server.setTimeout(30000)` (`server.ts`) closes the socket at 30 s with no reply. The browser then silently resends the POST, and each resend starts **another RF trace**: one click produced a trace every 30 s (9 in ~4 min) until the page was closed. This is already on `main`, independent of the return leg. The trace-path route now sets a 75 s socket timeout. Verified live after the fix: one click sends one trace, times out once and shows the error, with no resends.

Other routes that wait on the radio longer t

title: feat(delivery): show Meshtastic ack proof "Proven receipt" (#5279)
body:
Closes #5279. Implements `docs/internal/dev-notes/ACK_PROOF_PLAN.md`.

## Summary
Firmware 2.8.1 (on `develop`: #11877, #11932, #11965) reports `MeshPacket.ack_proof_status` on the ack that settles a unicast our own radio sent. It is an 8-byte HMAC check against the recipient's key. MeshMonitor now records that verdict and shows it. We never compute or check the proof ourselves.

- **Migration 184:** nullable `ackProofStatus` on `messages` (SQLite INTEGER, PG/MySQL SMALLINT), idempotent. `NULL` means no status reported.
- **Capture** in `processRoutingErrorMessage`: on the target-node confirmed ack and on the target-node DM nak (naks carry proofs too). Relay acks and channel messages store nothing. Always stored as the enum **number**, never the name.
- **ABSENT handling:** `ack_proof_status` is a plain proto3 enum, so ABSENT (0) is never on the wire and reads the same as older firmware. The radio that sets it is our own, so `resolveAckProofStatus()` checks that radio's firmware:
  - 2.8.1+: a missing value is stored as ABSENT ("Receipt not proven").
  - Older or unknown firmware: `NULL`, and the row stays hidden.
- **Delivery Details** row, after XEdDSA:
  - **VALID**: green "Proven receipt: the recipient's key signed this ack".
  - **INVALID**: warning "Ack proof failed: this ack may be forged". UI only, no notification (decided).
  - **ABSENT / NO_KEY**: muted "Receipt not proven", with a tooltip explaining multi-hop relay echoes and missing keys. Never styled as a failure.
- **Packet Monitor:** the detail view of a ROUTING_APP packet shows e.g. `ACK_PROOF_VALID (1)`, read from the packet's own decode. There is no `packet_log` column (decided).
- 8 locale keys.

## Screenshot
Dev container, a sent DM seeded with `ackProofStatus = 1`; the seed was reverted afterwards:

![Ack proof in Delivery Details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/ack-proof-5279/docs/public/images/features/5279-ack-proof-delivery-details.png)

## Testing
- Capture: 9 cases in `meshtasticManager.deliveryEvents.test.ts`, covering confirmed and nak, relay acks ignored, names mapped to numbers, and ABSENT stored for a 2.8.1 radio.
- `ackProof.test.ts` covers the reader and the firmware-gated resolver (`2.8.1.x` → ABSENT, `2.8.0.x`/unknown → none).
- Delivery Details and `MessageDetailsModal` rendering is tested per value.
- Migration 184 has a SQLite test plus a pgmysql test run against live PG 16 / MySQL 8.4 (35 passed, 0 skipped).
- Full Vitest suite: `success: true`, 24,523 passed, 0 failed (PG/MySQL up, 109 skipped). Both `tsc` configs clean; `npm run lint:ci` passes.
- Deployed to the dev container: migration 184 applied, and the row renders as in the screenshot.
- Not tested yet: live hardware, which needs a 2.8.1 radio. Plan step 8: expect VALID on 1 hop and often ABSENT on multi-hop.

## Notes
- A `2.8.1` build from before firmware #11965 (Sep 25) would show "Receipt not proven" for every ack. That is muted and technically true.
- **AEAD Phase 1

title: fix(meshtastic): send data requests at the node's configured hop limit
body:
Follow-up to #5484, which moved waypoint sends to the node's configured hop limit. Four request builders still hardcoded theirs:

| Request | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Position exchange | 3 | node's configured hop limit |
| NodeInfo exchange | 3 | node's configured hop limit |
| NeighborInfo request | **7** | node's configured hop limit |
| Telemetry request | default 3 | node's configured hop limit |

The builders now take a `hopLimit` argument (default `DEFAULT_HOP_LIMIT`, passed through `resolveHopLimit`), and `meshtasticManager` passes `getConfiguredHopLimit()`.

Unchanged on purpose:
- `requestRemoteLocalStats` keeps its caller-sized hop limit.
- The local-node LocalStats request goes to our own node.
- The `FromRadio` packet built for virtual-node clients is never transmitted over the radio.

## Mesh impact
These are on-demand, unicast requests; nothing new is scheduled.
- NeighborInfo requests stop flooding to 7 hops when the node is set lower, which reduces airtime.
- On a node configured above 3, position, NodeInfo and telemetry requests can now reach as far as the node's own setting. That matches what the node does for its own traffic.

## Tests
- New `meshtasticProtobufService.requestHopLimit.test.ts`: each request carries the passed hop limit, falls back to the firmware default, and clamps at 7.
- Server suite: 11,982 passed, 0 failed. `tsc` and `lint:ci` clean.

title: chore(protobufs): bump to master 2542e06, and plan AEAD channels (#5248) and ack proof (#5279)
body:
Refs #5248, #5279.

## Summary
Bumps the `protobufs` submodule from `970fb19` (v2.8.0-15) to master **`2542e06`** (115 commits, untagged; the maintainer approved tracking untagged master). It also fixes a startup break the bump would otherwise cause, and adds implementation plans for both issues.

### What the bump brings
- `ChannelSettings.use_aead = 8`: AEAD channels (#5248).
- `Routing.ack_proof = 4`, `MeshPacket.ack_proof_status = 23` + `AckProofStatus`: ack proof (#5279).
- `MeshPacket.slot_parity`, `NodeInfo.heard_on_current_lora`, `StoreAndForward.original_id`, MeshBeacon frequency slots, 3 hardware models, 2 UI languages, 2 codec2 bauds.
- `field_metadata.proto` annotations on config fields.

### Compatibility check (field-by-field diff of every .proto)
- 51 added, **0 renumbered or retyped**.
- 16 removed:
  - `EnvironmentMetrics` 42–56 (soil/water chemistry) moved to the new `SoilWaterMetrics` (`Telemetry.soil_water_metrics = 11`), and the old tags are `reserved`. No release shipped them: v2.8.0 never had them, only our post-2.8.0 pin did. MeshMonitor never read them.
  - `AS3935Config.tuning_cap_pf` moved to `AS3935State`. Unused here.

### Startup fix
`field_metadata.proto` imports `google/protobuf/descriptor.proto`. Both proto loaders (`protobufLoader.ts`, `protobufService.ts`) resolved that relative to the importing file, so the server would fail at startup with `ENOTDIR`. A shared `resolveProtoImport()` now maps `google/protobuf/*` to the copies `protobufjs` ships, and both loaders use it.

### Plans
- `docs/internal/dev-notes/ACK_PROOF_PLAN.md` (#5279): ready to build.
- `docs/internal/dev-notes/AEAD_CHANNELS_PLAN.md` (#5248): Phase 1 ready (store and preserve the flag; today a MeshMonitor channel edit would silently clear AEAD). Phase 2 waits for a 2.8.1 build.
- Both are grounded in firmware `develop` (version 2.8.1; all 8 upstream PRs merged, none reverted, none tagged yet).

## Testing
- New `protobufLoader.postV280.test.ts` loads the real submodule and covers:
  - the descriptor.proto resolution
  - `field_metadata` option parsing
  - round-trips of `use_aead`, `ack_proof` and `ack_proof_status`
  - the `SoilWaterMetrics` move with reserved tags
- Without the loader fix, the existing `protobufLoader.tmmSchema` suite fails with `ENOTDIR`.
- Full Vitest suite: `success: true`, 23,171 passed, 0 failed. `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` clean; `npm run lint:ci` passes.
- Dev container built from this branch:
  - `field_metadata.proto` and protobufjs's `descriptor.proto` are present in the runtime image.
  - Every loader logs success, with no `ENOTDIR` or protobuf errors.
  - 448 live packets decoded in 3 min.
  - `/api/health` returns 200.
- `system-test` label added: this changes the on-wire schema used against real radios.

## Mesh impact
None. No packets, notifications or timers change.

+# Ack Proof ("Proven receipt") — Implementation Plan (#5279)
+
+Status: **plan**, 2026-09-30. Protobufs submodule bumped to master `2542e06` in the PR that adds this file.
+
+## Upstream status (verified 2026-09-30)
+
+| Piece | Where | State |
+|---|---|---|
+| `Routing.ack_proof = 4` (8-byte HMAC) | protobufs #1094 `072c607`; firmware #11877 `6f3f0bd` | Merged (`master` / `develop`), 09-16 / 09-17. |
+| Verify against the node we addressed | firmware #11932 `57bdedf` | Merged to `develop` 09-24. |
+| `MeshPacket.ack_proof_status = 23`, enum `AckProofStatus` | protobufs #1109 `8f97d66`; firmware #11965 `2028484` | Merged 09-21 / 09-25. |
+| Doc note: multi-hop acks often read ABSENT | protobufs #1114 `ad0bf31` | Merged; comments only. |
+| First firmware to ship it | `develop` = **2.8.1** | No 2.8.1 tag yet. Newest build `v2.8.0.47db0e3` (09-01) predates all of it. |
+| Upstream testing | #11877 "native suite only"; #11932/#11965 device-regression boxes unchecked | Hardware-unverified upstream. |
+
+None of these PRs has been reverted. Firmware `develop` pins protobufs at `8f97d66` (includes #1109).
+
+## What the firmware does (`develop`)
+
+- **Proof:** `HMAC-SHA256(SHA256(X25519(priv, peerPub)), "ack" ‖ LE32(ackFrom) ‖ LE32(ackTo) ‖ LE32(request_id) ‖ Routing-without-field-4)[0..8)` (`CryptoEngine.cpp:360-392`).
+- **Which acks carry it:** any unicast ROUTING_APP ack or nak with a `request_id`, when the acking node holds an authoritative key for the requester. This covers **channel-encrypted DMs too, not only PKI DMs**. Implicit acks and relay echoes carry none.
+- **`ack_proof_status`:** set **only** on the phone-bound (FromRadio) copy of the ack that settles a unicast *this node* sent. Cleared on every inbound packet (LoRa, MQTT, UDP) and on client sends. Never on MQTT uplink.
+  - `VALID`: proof checks out against the addressed node's key.
+  - `INVALID`: a proof was carried and failed.
+  - `NO_KEY`: a proof was carried but the node has no key to check it.
+  - `ABSENT`: everything else, including naks from relays and acks that arrive after the relay echo already settled the packet. **On multi-hop paths a genuine receipt often reads ABSENT** (#1114).
+- **Advisory only:** `ACK_PROOF_ENFORCE = false`. INVALID logs a warning; the ack still stops retransmission.
+
+Consequences for MeshMonitor:
+- We never compute or verify anything; we record what the radio tells us.
+- The status is meaningful **only** on packets from our own TCP radio. MQTT-ingested acks never carry it, and MeshMonitor cannot verify `ack_proof` itself (it would need the node's private key).
+- ABSENT and NO_KEY mean "not proven", never "failed".
+
+## Implementation (build now; the field decodes after this bump)
+
+1. **Migration (next free number):** `ackProofStatus` smallint, nullable, on `messages`. All three backends. `NULL` = no status reported (older firmware, MQTT, channel broadcast). Pattern: `xeddsaSigned` (migrations 125, 140; `src/db/schema/messages.ts:31/80/123`).
+2. **Capture:** in `processRoutingErrorMessage` (`meshtasticManager.ts:9195`), in the target-node confirmed branch (`~:9272`), pass `meshPacket.ackProofStatus` into the `updateMessageDeliveryState(..., 'confirmed', ..., {...})` metadata. Also record it on a target-node nak (failed branch, `~:9455`), since naks carry proofs too. Only for DMs; ignore the field on anything that isn't the settling ack.
+3. **Types and API:** `DbMessage`, `transformDbMessage.ts`, `src/types/message.ts` gain `ackProofStatus`. Map the enum by number, not by name (protobufjs `toJSON` emits names; see the enum-names gotcha).
+4. **Delivery Details** (`src/utils/deliveryDiagnostics/meshtasticDelivery.ts:~195`, next to the XEdDSA row):
+   - `VALID` → "Proven receipt: the recipient's key signed this ack."
+   - `INVALID` → warning styling: "Ack proof failed: this ack may be forged." UI only, no notification (decided).
+   - `ABSENT` / `NO_KEY` → muted: "Receipt not proven" with a tooltip explaining multi-hop echoes and missing keys. Never shown as a failure.
+   - `NULL` → row hidden.
+5. **Packet Monitor:** show the decoded `ackProofStatus` on the ROUTING_APP row from the packet's own decode. No `packet_log` column (decided).
+6. **Locale keys** for all of the above in `public/locales/en.json`.
+7. **Tests:** capture on confirmed and nak branches; not stored for non-target acks or channel messages; Delivery Details rendering per value; migration tests incl. PG/MySQL containers.
+8. **Hardware validation (after 2.8.1 ships):** DM a 1-hop and a 3-hop node from a 2.8.1 radio; expect VALID on the 1-hop and often ABSENT on the 3-hop.
+
+Mesh impact: none. Display only; no packets, notifications or timers.
+
+## Decisions (maintainer, 2026-09-30)
+
+- Bump protobufs to untagged master: **yes** (done in this PR).
+- INVALID: UI warning only, no notification: **yes**.
+- Store on `messages` only, no `packet_log` column: **yes**.

+# AEAD (AES-CCM) PSK Channels — Implementation Plan (#5248)
+
+Status: **plan**, 2026-09-30. Protobufs submodule bumped to master `2542e06` in the PR that adds this file.
+
+## Upstream status (verified 2026-09-30)
+
+| Piece | Where | State |
+|---|---|---|
+| `ChannelSettings.use_aead = 8` | protobufs #868, `e4fbafb` | Merged to `master` 09-09. No tag (latest `v2.8.0`). In our submodule after this bump. |
+| AES-CCM PSK channels | firmware #9749, `d05fbec` | Merged to `develop` (the integration branch) 09-14. Not reverted. |
+| First firmware to ship it | `develop` `version.properties` = **2.8.1** | No 2.8.1 tag or prerelease yet. Newest build is `v2.8.0.47db0e3` (09-01), which predates it. |
+| Upstream testing | #9749 checklist | "End-to-end AEAD path test" and "Hardware test on ESP32/nRF52" **unchecked**. |
+| Open upstream PRs touching the path | firmware #9951 (big-endian nonce order), #9600 (constant-time compare), #11979 (key cache) | Watch #9951: it could change nonce bytes on big-endian hosts. |
+
+## Wire format (firmware `develop`, `src/mesh/CryptoEngine.cpp`, `aes-ccm.cpp`, `Channels.cpp`)
+
+- **Cipher:** RFC 3610 AES-CCM, M=12 (tag), L=2. Key = the expanded channel PSK (`AQ==` expands to the default key). 16 bytes → AES-128, 32 → AES-256.
+- **Nonce (13 bytes):** `LE32(packet.id) ‖ 0x00000000 ‖ LE32(from) ‖ 0x00`. This is the CTR nonce truncated to 13 bytes.
+- **AAD (8 bytes):** `LE32(from) ‖ LE32(to)`. Hop fields are excluded.
+- **Payload:** `ciphertext ‖ 12-byte tag`. Every packet grows by 12 bytes; firmware rejects sends where payload + 16 + 12 > 255 (`TOO_LARGE`).
+- **Channel hash:** `xorHash(name) ^ xorHash(expandedPsk) ^ 0xAE` when `use_aead` is set. The XOR is applied to the finished hash.
+- **Mode choice:** hash match first, then the receiver's *own* channel flag picks CCM or CTR. Nothing else on the wire marks AEAD. **No CTR fallback**: AEAD and legacy nodes on the same name and PSK cannot talk.
+- **Empty PSK:** firmware silently clears `use_aead` (`Channels.cpp:83-86`).
+- **`set_channel` replaces the whole channel** (`Channels::setChannel`). A client that omits `use_aead` turns AEAD off.
+- **MQTT:** no AEAD branch in `MQTT::onSend`. With MQTT encryption on, the envelope carries the on-air ciphertext and tag unchanged, `packet.channel` = the AEAD hash. With it off, the envelope carries plaintext as before.
+- **Unchanged:** PKI DMs. `setDefaultPresetCryptoForHash` does not apply `0xAE`, so an AEAD LongFast is not auto-matched by the default-preset path.
+
+## The risk to fix first
+
+`createSetChannelMessage` (`src/server/protobufService.ts:1340`) builds `ChannelSettings` from the fields it knows. The `channels` table (`src/db/schema/channels.ts`) and the save in `meshtasticManager.ts:~6210` don't store `use_aead`. Once a node runs 2.8.1 with AEAD on, **any channel edit from MeshMonitor turns AEAD off**, and channel URL export (`channelUrlService.ts:122,200`) drops it too. Phase 1 closes this.
+
+## Phase 1 — store and keep the flag (build now)
+
+No firmware needed to build or test; a synthetic `ChannelSettings` with `useAead: true` exercises every path.
+
+1. **Migration (next free number, 183 at time of writing):** `useAead` boolean, not null, default false, on `channels` (per-source). All three backends via `addColumnIfMissing*`. Update the schema's three table definitions and `DbChannel`.
+2. **Read from the device:** `meshtasticManager.ts:~6133` and `~6210` store `channel.settings.useAead ?? false`.
+3. **Write to the device (read-modify-write):** `createSetChannelMessage` accepts `useAead`. Every caller fills it from the stored channel row when the request omits it:
+   - `adminRoutes.ts:1334` (bulk channel save / import)
+   - `adminRoutes.ts:1779` (single channel edit)
+   - `deviceAdminService.ts:142` (remote admin). For remote nodes MeshMonitor may have no stored row; read the channel from the node first (existing get-channel flow) rather than defaulting to `false`.
+4. **Channel URLs:** `channelUrlService.ts` decodes and encodes `useAead` in the `ChannelSet`.
+5. **Config export/import and device backup/restore** (`ExportConfigModal`, `ImportConfigModal`, the #4926 device-config restore): carry the field.
+6. **UI, read-only:** an "AEAD" badge on the channel in `ChannelsConfigSection.tsx` and `ChannelsTab.tsx`, with a tooltip: "This channel uses AES-CCM authenticated encryption. Only nodes with the same setting can read it."
+7. **Tests:** round-trip `useAead` through save → edit → `createSetChannelMessage` bytes (the edit must keep `true`); URL encode/decode; migration tests on SQLite + PG/MySQL containers.
+
+Mesh impact: none new. One admin packet per edit, as today.
+
+## Phase 2 — decrypt and edit (after a 2.8.1 build ships AEAD)
+
+1. **Migration:** `useAead` on `channel_database` (global table, per CLAUDE.md exception). Backfill nothing; default false.
+2. **Hash:** `computeChannelHash(name, psk, useAead)` in `channelDecryptionService.ts:73` applies `^ 0xAE`. Extend the hash lookup at `:156-167`, and add AEAD hashes to the stored-hash backfill (migration 104 pattern).
+3. **Decrypt:** a CCM branch in `tryDecryptWithKey` (`:252`) using Node's `aes-128-ccm` / `aes-256-ccm`, `authTagLength: 12`, the 13-byte nonce and 8-byte AAD above. Pattern: `pkiDecryptionService.ts:123`. The tag check confirms the key, so no plausibility heuristics are needed; a tag failure is a clean miss.
+4. **MQTT hint:** debug-level log only, when an encrypted packet's hash equals a known non-AEAD row's hash `^ 0xAE` ("channel X looks AEAD-enabled upstream; enable AEAD on it to decrypt"). Nothing at warn level: an AEAD packet is otherwise indistinguishable from a wrong key.
+5. **Editable checkbox** in `ChannelsConfigSection.tsx` and `ChannelDatabaseSection.tsx`, labelled **Experimental**, gated on firmware ≥ 2.8.1 for the device channel, disabled when the PSK is empty. Confirm dialog on enable. Proposed warning (for maintainer sign-off):
+   > **AEAD cuts this channel off from nodes that don't use it.** Nodes on older firmware, or with AEAD off, can no longer read or send on this channel, even with the same name and key. Turn it on for every node on the channel at the same time.
+6. **Compose limit:** reduce the per-message byte limit by 12 on AEAD channels (confirm the exact figure against firmware `TOO_LARGE` at implementation).
+7. **Tests:** known-answer vectors generated from the firmware's own test suite (or a 2.8.1 node capture), hash `^0xAE`, tag failure = miss, MQTT hint.
+8. **Hardware validation:** two 2.8.1 nodes on an AEAD channel, MeshMonitor on TCP + MQTT ingest, before release.
+
+## Decisions (maintainer, 2026-09-30)
+
+- Bump protobufs to untagged master: **yes** (done in this PR).
+- Phase 1 read-only now; Phase 2 editable, marked Experimental: **yes**.
+- MQTT hint at debug level only: **yes**.
+- Warning text above: **pending sign-off**.

title: feat(automation): broadcast waypoints with a hop limit (#5482)
body:
Closes #5482

Adds an Automation Engine action that broadcasts a Meshtastic waypoint, and a hop limit on every waypoint send. Spec with the maintainer's decisions: `docs/internal/dev-notes/WAYPOINT_AUTOMATION_SPEC.md`.

## What changes
**Hop limit on every waypoint send**
- `createWaypointMessage` no longer hardcodes `hopLimit: 3`.
- `broadcastWaypoint` defaults to the node's configured LoRa hop limit and caps any requested value at it (`clampHopLimitOverride`), so a setting can only shorten reach.
- Every path goes through that one resolver: the UI editor, REST POST/PATCH, the delete tombstone, the rebroadcast scheduler and the automation.
- `want_ack` stays off for waypoints.
- ⚠️ **Behaviour change:** existing waypoint sends move from a fixed 3 hops to the node's configured hop limit (the maintainer's choice). Nodes set above 3 will send waypoints further.

**Storage and API**
- Migration 183 (all three backends) adds `waypoints.hop_limit` (NULL = inherit), `automation_key` and `broadcast_fingerprint`.
- REST POST/PATCH accept `hop_limit`/`hopLimit` (0–7 or `null`); anything else returns `400 INVALID_HOP_LIMIT`. GET returns `hopLimit`.
- The waypoint editor has a hop-limit field with an airtime warning.

**New action `action.broadcastWaypoint`**
- Fields: source, waypoint key, lat/lon, name, description, icon, expiry, channel, hop limit, and "only send when changed". Text fields accept `{{ }}` templates, so a `runScript` step can feed live values.
- Each run updates the same waypoint (stable id per automation + key), so clients don't pile up copies.

## Mesh impact
- **Cost:** a waypoint is about 110 bytes, roughly 1 s at LongFast. It floods, so at hop 3 on a ~30-node local mesh one send is about 30 transmissions (~30 s of channel time). Hop 0 is one transmission.
- **30-minute floor per automation waypoint**, read from the persisted `lastBroadcastAt`. Saving the automation or restarting can't re-arm it, and only a successful send stamps it. At the floor, a hop-3 waypoint is about 1.7% channel use.
- **Runs are serialized per waypoint**, so overlapping trigger events can't both pass the floor (review finding, fixed with a regression test).
- **Waypoint key and source accept `{{ var.* }}` only.** Text from mesh messages can't create new waypoints, each with its own fresh floor.
- **"Only send when changed"** (per action, off by default) compares a fingerprint of what was last sent, so a change that arrived while the floor held a send back still goes out.
- The trigger-level rate limit and cooldown still apply on top. TX-disabled sources are recorded as a skip.

## Other decisions
- A bad channel slot fails the step instead of silently using Primary.
- Names are cut at 29 bytes and descriptions at 99 (the firmware limits), on character boundaries. The editor labels say so.
- Automation waypoints have no separate periodic rebroadcast; they send only when the automation runs.

## Tests
- Full Vitest with the PG and MySQL containers up: 24,458 pass
author: Yeraze

@@ -536,6 +536,43 @@ Loop safety: turning an automation on or off raises no event, so no trigger can
 Rule A that toggles rule B can't set off rule B, and two rules can't toggle each other in a loop
 through this action alone. The trigger's own cooldown and rate limit still apply.
 
+### Broadcast a waypoint
+
+In JSON mode, this action has the type `action.broadcastWaypoint`.
+
+Creates a Meshtastic waypoint, keeps it up to date, and broadcasts it with the hop limit you
+choose. Use it to publish a value that changes, such as a border wait time from a script, to a
+bounded area of the mesh. Meshtastic only.
+
+- **Send via source** — the Meshtastic radio that owns and sends the waypoint.
+- **Waypoint key** — names the waypoint within this automation. Each run updates the same
+  waypoint instead of making a new one, across runs and restarts. Use one key per waypoint. It
+  takes `{{ var.* }}` templates only, so a mesh message can't create waypoints.
+- **Latitude**, **Longitude**, **Name**, **Description**, **Expires after (hours)** — take
+  `{{ }}` templates, so a [Run a script](#run-a-script) step with a result variable can fill
+  them, for example `{{ var.wait.lat }}`. The name is cut to 29 bytes and the description to 99,
+  the firmware limits.
+- **Icon** — an emoji. **Channel #** — the device slot, 0-7.
+- **Hop limit** — blank or **Inherit** uses the node's configured hop limit. A value is capped at

+- **Only send when changed** — skip the send when the name, description, position, icon, expiry,
+  channel and hop limit match what was last sent. Off by default: every allowed run sends.
+
+What happens when it runs:
+
+- The waypoint row is always updated, so the map shows the new values at once.
+- **A waypoint goes out at most once per 30 minutes.** A run inside that window updates the
+  waypoint and records a skip (`MIN_INTERVAL`) in the run log. The time of the last send is
+  stored with the waypoint, so saving the automation or restarting MeshMonitor does not reset it.
+- A change held back by the 30-minute limit still goes out on the next allowed run, even with

+- A TX-disabled source records a skip, as **Send a message** does.

Leave it alone and the waypoint goes out on Primary (slot 0), the channel every waypoint used before this option existed. The picker is disabled for virtual waypoints, which are never transmitted.
 5. Click **Save**. MeshMonitor allocates a waypoint id (Python-style id allocation), persists the row, and broadcasts a WAYPOINT_APP packet to the mesh.
 
@@ -84,6 +85,8 @@ All mutations require the standard `X-CSRF-Token` header. Mutations on a waypoin
 
 `POST` and `PATCH` accept an optional `channel` field — an integer device channel slot `0`-`7`. Anything else returns `400`. Omit it and the waypoint stays on slot 0.
 
+`POST` and `PATCH` also accept `hop_limit` (or `hopLimit`): an integer `0`-`7`, or `null` to use the node's configured hop limit. Anything else returns `400` with code `INVALID_HOP_LIMIT`. The stored value is what you asked for; at send time it is capped at the node's own hop limit. `GET` returns it as `hopLimit`.
+
 ## Database
 
 Waypoints live in a per-source `waypoints` table introduced in migration **053**, with composite primary key `(sourceId, waypointId)`, a foreign key to `sources` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, and indexes on `(sourceId, expireAt)` and `(sourceId, ownerNodeNum)`.
@@ -92,6 +95,10 @@ Migrations **054** / **055** seed the new `waypoints:read` / `waypoints:write` p
 
 Migration **130** adds the `channel` column that records which slot a waypoint is broadcast on. Rows created before it read back as `NULL`, which every send site treats as slot 0 — the same channel they always used.
 
+Migration **183** adds `hop_limit` (`NULL` = the node's configured hop limit, which every earlier row gets), plus `automation_key` and `broadcast_fingerprint`, used by the Automation Engine's [Broadcast a waypoint](/features/automation-engine#broadcast-a-waypoint) action.
+
+Waypoints used to go out at a fixed hop limit of 3. They now use the node's configured LoRa hop limit unless the waypoint sets its own.
+
 The daily database maintenance tick sweeps expired waypoints (with a grace window) and emits `waypoint:expired` events for each removed row.
 
 ## Arrival notifications
--- docs/internal/dev-notes/WAYPOINT_AUTOMATION_SPEC.md (+103/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+# Waypoint broadcast automation + hop limit (#5482) — spec
+
+Requested by a user who broadcasts border-wait-time waypoints for two ports of
+entry and needs them to reach a bounded radius, not the whole mesh.
+
+## Decisions (maintainer, 2026-09-30)
+
+| Question | Decision |
+|---|---|
+| Default hop limit when none is given | The node's **configured** LoRa hop limit (`getConfiguredHopLimit()`), for every waypoint send — UI, REST, rebroadcast scheduler, automation. Replaces today's hardcoded `3`. |
+| Maximum hop limit | The node's configured hop limit. A setting can only **lower** reach (`clampHopLimitOverride`, `src/utils/hopLimitOverride.ts`). |
+| Minimum interval between automation broadcasts of the same waypoint | **30 minutes**, enforced from the persisted `waypoints.lastBroadcastAt`, never an in-memory field. Saving the automation or restarting MeshMonitor must not re-arm it or count as a send. |
+| Re-send when unchanged? | **Configurable per action**: `onlyWhenChanged` (default `false` = send every allowed run). |
+
+## Airtime (for the PR body)
+
+~110-byte packet ≈ 1 s at LongFast. A flood is rebroadcast once by every node
+within the hop limit: ~30 transmissions (~30 s) per send on a ~30-node local
+mesh at hop 3. At the 30-minute floor that is ≈1.7 % channel use per waypoint;
+hop 0 is a single transmission.
+
+## 1. Hop limit on the send path
+
+- `meshtasticProtobufService.createWaypointMessage` takes an optional
+  `hopLimit`; drop the hardcoded `3`.
+- `meshtasticManager.broadcastWaypoint(waypoint, { ..., hopLimit })` resolves the
+  effective value: `clampHopLimitOverride(hopLimit ?? inherit, getConfiguredHopLimit())`.
+- `want_ack` stays off for broadcasts. For a DM waypoint with an effective hop
+  limit of 0, force `want_ack` off too (firmware rewrites hop 0 on want_ack
+  packets to the node default — #5121).
+- `broadcastWaypointDelete` uses the waypoint's stored hop limit.
+
+## 2. Persistence (migration 183, all three backends)
+
+- `waypoints.hopLimit` integer, nullable. `NULL` = inherit the node's
+  configured value. Idempotent helpers; update hand-written PG/MySQL test DDL
+  where a suite uses it.
+- The rebroadcast scheduler (`waypointService.rebroadcastTick`) passes the
+  stored hop limit.
+
+## 3. REST API (`src/server/routes/waypoints.ts`)
+
+- POST and PATCH accept `hop_limit` (alias `hopLimit`): integer 0–7, or
+  `null` to inherit. Validate with the existing `parseHopLimitOverride`; reject
+  out-of-range with `fail(res, 400, 'INVALID_HOP_LIMIT', …)`. The stored value
+  is what was asked for; the clamp to the device limit happens at send time.
+- GET returns `hopLimit`.
+
+## 4. Automation action `action.broadcastWaypoint`
+
+Params (all string fields accept `{{ }}` templates, so a preceding
+`action.runScript` with `resultVariable` can supply values):
+
+- `sourceId` (required; a Meshtastic source)
+- `waypointKey` (required, string; identifies this automation's waypoint so
+  each run UPDATES the same waypoint id instead of creating a new one)
+- `latitude`, `longitude` (required, numeric after interpolation, range-checked)
+- `name` (≤ 29 bytes after firmware limits — reuse existing waypoint
+  validation), `description`, `icon` (emoji), `expireHours` (optional)
+- `channel` (0–7), `hopLimit` (optional, same field and clamp as
+  `action.sendMessage`'s hop limit — reuse `HOP_LIMIT_FIELD` / `hopLimitParamError`)
+- `onlyWhenChanged` (bool, default false)
+
+Behaviour on each run:
+1. Resolve the waypoint for `(sourceId, automationId, waypointKey)`. Store the
+   mapping so the id is stable across runs and restarts (a small column on
+   `waypoints` such as `automationKey`, or an automation variable — pick one,
+   persisted).
+2. Upsert the waypoint row (owner = local node, not virtual) with the new
+   fields and `hopLimit`.
+3. **Floor:** if `now - lastBroadcastAt < 30 min`, skip the send and record a
+   skipped result with the reason (the row update still happens, so the
+   periodic rebroadcaster and the UI see fresh content).
+4. If `onlyWhenChanged` and name, description, position, icon, expiry, channel
+   and hop limit are unchanged, skip the send.
+5. Otherwise `broadcastWaypoint(..., { origin: 'automation', hopLimit })` and
+   persist `lastBroadcastAt = now`.
+6. Respect TX-disabled / receive-only states the same way `action.sendMessage`
+   does.
+
+Validation lives in `src/types/automation.ts` alongside the other actions; the
+executor in `src/server/services/automation/actionExecutor.ts`; the real dep in
+`meshActionDeps.ts`. The trigger-level `rateLimit` / cooldown still apply on
+top.
+
+## 5. UI
+
+- `src/components/automations/catalog.ts`: a catalog entry for the new action
+  with the fields above; show a warning next to the hop limit and a note that
+  sends are at most once per 30 minutes per waypoint. Tester preview in
+  `AutomationTester.tsx`.
+- `WaypointEditorModal.tsx`: a hop-limit input (blank = node default), with the
+  same warning text used for the message hop limit.
+- Locale keys in `public/locales/en.json`.
+
+## Tests
+
+Protobuf hop limit + want_ack; clamp to device value; migration (SQLite + PG +
+MySQL containers); REST validation via `createRouteTestApp`; rebroadcast uses
+stored hop limit; action: stable id across runs, 30-minute floor survives a
+simulated restart (floor read from DB), `onlyWhenChanged`, template
+interpolation from a script variable, TX-disabled skip; catalog/editor
+component tests.

title: feat(nav): Pin sidebar on MeshCore sources, shared with Meshtastic (#5481)
body:
Closes #5481.

## Summary
The Meshtastic per-source sidebar has a **Pin sidebar** toggle; the MeshCore nav had none. Checking the live app showed a second difference the issue didn't mention: MeshCore's nav never collapsed after a nav click, and it started collapsed on every load and source switch, while Meshtastic collapses an unpinned nav on click and starts expanded when pinned.

This takes the issue's Option B:
- **`useSidebarPin`** (`src/components/nav/useSidebarPin.ts`): one hook over the existing global `sidebar-pinned` localStorage key, safe when storage is blocked. Pin state stays global, so switching between a Meshtastic and a MeshCore source never flips the nav mode.
- **`SourceNav`**: optional `pinned` / `onTogglePin` props add a pin button to the built-in controls, shown only while expanded, with `aria-pressed` and the same green pinned style as `Sidebar.css`.
- **MeshCore** now matches Meshtastic: it starts expanded when pinned, pinning expands it, and an unpinned nav collapses after a nav click.
- **Meshtastic `Sidebar`**: uses the same hook; its markup and classes are unchanged.

**Behaviour change for MeshCore:** unpinned users now see the nav collapse after a click, as on Meshtastic. Pinning keeps it open.

Mobile is unchanged: the bottom bar hides the controls slot on both source types.

## Screenshot
MeshCore source, pinned (green pin, bottom left) after a nav click:

![MeshCore nav pinned](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/fix/meshcore-nav-pin-5481/docs/public/images/features/5481-meshcore-nav-pin.png)

## Testing
- New `MeshCorePage.navPin.test.tsx` (4 cases: unpinned collapse on click, pin expands + persists + stays open, starts expanded when already pinned, unpin). **All 4 fail without the `MeshCorePage` change.**
- New `useSidebarPin.test.ts` (read default, toggle + persist, storage throwing) and 2 `SourceNav` pin cases (shown only while expanded, labels/aria, absent without `onTogglePin`).
- Full Vitest suite: `success: true`, 23,165 passed, 0 failed. `npm run lint:ci` passes; `tsc` clean.
- Deployed to the dev container and driven in the browser:
  - MeshCore unpinned: a click collapses the nav.
  - Pin: expands and stores `sidebar-pinned=true`; the nav stays open on click.
  - Switching to a Meshtastic source: it loads expanded and pinned from the same key.

## Mesh impact
None — frontend only.

title: Feature: Inline translation of messages
body: ## Description I belong to a mesh that runs across multiple languages where not every user knows or is comfortable communicating using both languages. This feature adds native inline chat message translation to MeshMonitor for mesh channels and direct messages (both inbound incoming messages and outbound composer drafts). ### Screenshots NOTE: When disabled, the UI remains as it was previously. #### Global Settings: Message Translation #### Inbound Chat Messages #### Outbound Chat Messages ### Key Features - **Multiple Translation Providers**: - **LibreTranslate**: Self-hosted local Docker or cloud-hosted instances (Free & Open Source). - **OpenAI-Compatible**: Ollama (Free/Local inference), OpenRouter, OpenAI, vLLM. - **DeepL API**: Free Developer tier (500k chars/mo, no payment details required) & Paid Pro tier (Cloud). - **Google Cloud Translation API**: Cloud translation API. - **Inbound Message Translation**:

--- docs/.vitepress/config.mts (+2/-1) @@ -71,7 +71,8 @@ const featuresSidebar = [ { text: 'Message Search', link: '/features/message-search' }, { text: 'Delivery Details', link: '/features/delivery-diagnostics' }, { text: 'Channel Database', link: '/features/channel-database' }, - { text: 'Store & Forward', link: '/features/store-forward' } + { text: 'Store & Forward', link: '/features/store-forward' }, + { text: 'Message Translation', link: '/features/message-translation' } ] }, { --- docs/features/message-translation.md (+116/-0) @@ -0,0 +1,116 @@ +# Message Translation + +MeshMonitor includes native inline chat message translation for mesh broadcast channels and direct messages. This allows operators and mesh communities across different regions and languages to communicate seamlessly over radio networks. + +--- + +## Overview + +Message translation in MeshMonitor operates on-demand: +- **Inbound Messages**: Hover over any received message in a channel or direct message thread and click the **Translate** icon to view the translated text inline directly below the message. +- **Outbound Composer**: Click the **Translate** icon in the message compose bar to translate your draft into a destination language before transmitting over the mesh network. +- **Language Switcher**: Dynamically change the destination language right on the message card, with choices automatically remembered for future translations. +- **LoRa Packet Awareness**: Real-time UTF-8 byte counting warns you if translated text exceeds typical radio packet limits (~200–220 bytes). + +--- + +## Supported Translation Providers + +MeshMonitor supports four flexible translation backends, catering to cloud APIs, self-hosted open-source software, and completely offline local language models: + +| Provider | Cost / Tier | Hosting | Setup Complexity | Best For | +| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | +| **DeepL API**
*(Recommended)* | **Free** (500k chars/mo) or Paid Pro | Cloud | **Easiest** | **Recommended.** Easiest setup. High translation quality. Free developer account requires no payment details. | +| **LibreTranslate** | **Free & Open Source** | Local (Docker) or Cloud | Low | Offline/air-gapped nodes, self-hosted servers, privacy-focused deployments. | +| **OpenAI-Compatible** | **Free** (Local Ollama) or Pay-per-token (OpenAI, OpenRouter, vLLM) | Local or Cloud | Low–Medium | Flexible LLM-based translations, local Ollama models (`llama3`, `qwen2.5`), or cloud LLMs. | +| **Google Cloud Translation** | Free trial / Pay-as-you-go | Cloud | Medium | Users with existing Google Cloud Console infrastructure. | + +--- + +## Recommended: Setting Up DeepL API (Free) + +For most users, **DeepL API Free** provides the best balance of speed, translation accuracy, and ease of setup: + +1. Sign up for a free DeepL API developer account at [deepl.com/pro-api](https://www.deepl.com/pro-api) (select the **DeepL API Free** plan). +2. Copy your **Authentication Key** from your DeepL account dashboard (Free keys end in `:fx`, such as `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx:fx`). +3. In MeshMonitor, navigate to **Settings** → **Message Translation**. +4. Check **Enable Message Translation**. +5. Select **DeepL API (Free / Pro)** from the **Translation Provider** dropdown. +6. Paste your authentication key into the **DeepL Auth Key** field. +7. Click **Test Connection** to verify connectivity. +8. Click **Save Changes** in the bottom save bar. + +::: tip Automatic Endpoint Detection +MeshMonitor automatically detects whether your DeepL key is Free (`:fx`) or Pro and routes requests to the correct API endpoint (`https://api-free.deepl.com/v2` vs `https://api.deepl.com/v2`). +::: + +--- + +## Local & Offline Options + +If your MeshMonitor node operates in an off-grid, air-gapped, or privacy-conscious environment without internet access, you can run a local translation engine on the same host or local network: + +### 1. LibreTranslate (Self-Hosted Docker) + +LibreTranslate is a free and open-source self-hosted translation engine. + +You can launch a local instance using Docker: + +```bash +docker run -d -p 5000:5000 --restart always libretranslate/libretranslate +``` + +In MeshMonitor: +- Set **Translation Provider** to `LibreTranslate (Local / Self-Hosted / Cloud)`. +- Set **LibreTranslate URL** to `http://localhost:5000` (or `http://libretranslate:5000` if running inside a Docker network). +- Leave the API key blank if authentication is not enabled on your instance. + +### 2. OpenAI-Compatible / Ollama (Local LLM) + +If you run [Ollama](https://ollama.ai/) or another OpenAI-compatible local inference server: + +- Set **Translation Provider** to `OpenAI-Compatible (Ollama, OpenRouter, OpenAI, vLLM)`. +- Set **OpenAI Base URL** to `http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1` (or your local Ollama address). +- Set **Model Name** to your desired model (e.g. `llama3`, `qwen2.5`, or `mistral`). +- Leave the API key blank for local Ollama instances. + +--- + +## How to Use Translation + +### Inbound Message Translation +1. In the **Channels** or **Messages** tab, hover over any message. +2. Click the **Translate** icon on the message toolbar. +3. The message is translated into your primary language (configured in settings or your last chosen language). +4. To switch the target language, select a new language from the inline dropdown on the translated banner. MeshMonitor will re-translate the message and remember your preference in your browser's local storage. +5. Click the close (**✕**) icon to hide the translation banner at any time. + +### Outbound Message Translation +1. Type a message in the chat composer input box. +2. Click the **Translate** icon to the right of the compose box. +3. The **Translate Outgoing Message** modal will appear with your text pre-populated. +4. Select your **Source Language** (or keep *Auto-detect*) and choose the **Target Language**. +5. Use the **⇄** (swap) button if you need to reverse the language direction. +6. Click **Translate**. +7. Review the translation and check the byte counter. +8. Click **Replace in Draft** to insert the translated text directly into the compose box ready for transmission. + +--- + +## Radio Constraints & Byte Limits + +LoRa packet payloads are typically constrained to approximately **200 to 220 UTF-8 bytes** depending on modem presets and packet metadata. + +- The outbound translation modal features a real-time UTF-8 byte counter showing current payload usage (e.g., `45 / 200 bytes`). +- If a translation exceeds the 200-byte threshold, a **LoRa Packet Payload Warning** banner appears in the modal advising you to shorten the text before transmitting over RF. + +--- + +## Security & Privacy + +- **Authentication & Permission Gating**: Translation endpoints (`POST /api/translate` and `POST /api/v1/translate`) require an authenticated user with `messages:read` permission. Unauthenticated visitors or users lacking message permissions cannot access translation endpoints, and translation action buttons are hidden in the UI. +- **Dedicated Rate Limiting**: Translation endpoints are protected by a dedicated user/IP rate limiter (`RATE_LIMIT_TRANSLATE`, defaulting to 30 requests/minute in production and 120 in development) to defend provider API quota against automated loops and excessive usage. +- **Secret Masking**: Sensitive translation API keys and authentication tokens are stored securely server-side and automatically stripped from `GET /api/settings` for non-admin viewers. +- **Admin Gating**: Connection testing (`POST /api/translate/test`) requires administrative privileges (`requireAdmin()`). +- **Telemetry Filtering**: Raw telemetry packets, system status logs, emojis, and standard radio pings (`ack`, `ping`, `test`, `73`) are automatically detected and filtered out to prevent unnecessary API queries and costs. +- **Payload Limits**: Inbound translation requests enforce a maximum character limit of 5,000 characters and include automatic request timeouts. ... 49 more files truncated

+
+MeshMonitor **v4.16.2** is the full release of the 4.16.2 line, after six release candidates. It is larger than the version number suggests: a new Coverage Report, likely-aircraft detection, asset tracking and a long list of MeshCore work.
+
+Highlights below. The full list is in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
+
+## Coverage Report
+
+Firmware 2.8 removed the Range Test module. The [Coverage Report](/features/coverage-report) replaces it, and it sends nothing. Every position fix your radio sources hear is stored with that radio's SNR, RSSI and hop data. Drive a GPS node around, then open **Reports → Coverage** to see where the mesh hears you.
+
+MeshCore receptions and opt-in MQTT gateways count as receivers too. The report shows coverage gaps, a summary, a grid view, export, deep links and saved surveys.
+
+## Likely aircraft
+
+A node flying well above the terrain beneath it is now flagged as a [likely aircraft](/features/maps#likely-aircraft), with a plane badge on the map. Mountaintop repeaters stay fixed. You can also:
+
+- Age out aircraft that go quiet, and bring them back when a live position arrives.
+- Draw [flight trails](/features/maps#flight-trails).
+- Match the node to a real flight through a community ADS-B feed ([flight matching](/features/maps#flight-matching-ads-b), off by default).
+
+MQTT sources now store position history, so trails and Position History work for nodes heard only over MQTT.
+
+## Asset tracking
+
+Flag a node as an [asset](/features/maps#asset-tracking) to keep its telemetry for up to a year, always draw its trail, and exempt it from automated cleanups. A playback bar replays the trip with a moving marker.
+
+## And more
+
+- **Per-transport breakdowns** split nodes, messages, route records and traffic charts into RF, UDP and MQTT.
+- **Sign-flipped position correction** shows a node whose latitude or longitude lost its minus sign at the right place, when the fix is unambiguous. Stored data never changes.
+- **Message [Forwarding](/features/automation#forwarding)**, per source, copies matching messages to a node or channel, with a hard rate cap.

+- **CARTO vector basemaps** and a bundled [Voyager Dark](/features/maps#carto-vector-basemaps) style.
+- **Nodes tab:** a quick age filter, per-source First Heard, Group by Role, and adding a node from a Meshtastic contact URL.
+- **Automation Engine:** `action.setAutomationEnabled`, and a `trigger.packetHash` template variable for MeshCore messages.
+- **Firmware OTA** runs on the selected source with its own TCP port, and the board map now matches Meshtastic's release file names.
+- Telemetry outlier purge, scheduled NodeInfo Enrichment, and many mobile and iOS 27 fixes.
+
+## Upgrade notes
+
+**MeshCore adverts default to zero-hop**, and automated flood adverts are limited to one per hour per source. Saved configs with no mode set keep flooding but fall under the hourly limit. See [Adverts](/features/meshcore#adverts).
+

title: fix(aircraft): let an aged-out aircraft come back on MQTT sources
body:
## Summary
An aircraft aged out on an MQTT source could never come back.

**Cause:** aircraft age-out ignores the node with reason `aircraft`, and only a live position is supposed to lift it (D3). In `mqttIngestion.ts`, the POSITION case drops a still-ignored sender *before* it stores the fix, but the lift hook (`aircraftAgeOutService.handlePositionReception`) only ran *after* the store. So on MQTT the lift was unreachable.

**Seen live:** Ken Mobile 2 (`!cd46b954`) was aged out on Yeraze MQTT Broker and Florida MQTT on Sep 26. Its `lastHeard` kept advancing (heard today), but neither source stored a single position or telemetry row from it in three days; its MQTT position stayed frozen at the Sep 26 fix. The Meshtastic TCP path has no pre-store ignore gate, so lifts worked there.

**Fix:**
- New `AircraftAgeOutService.liftIfLivePosition(sourceId, nodeNum, rxTime, nowMs)`: lift-only, live receptions only, no classification (the existing post-upsert hook still queues that). `onLivePosition` now shares the same private lift helper.
- `mqttIngestion.ts` POSITION case: for an ignored sender with a live, non-bogus fix, call it *before* the ignore gate. The gate then re-checks, so manual and geo ignores still drop the fix, and replayed/retained frames never lift.
- The lat/lng/bogus parsing moved above the gate (pure computation) so the lift only fires on a trustworthy fix.

## Testing
- New `src/server/mqttIngestion.aircraftLift.test.ts`: lifted aircraft ingests and reaches the post-upsert hook; declined lift still drops; bogus fix never attempts a lift; non-ignored sender skips it. **The first two fail without the fix.**
- New `liftIfLivePosition` cases in `aircraftAgeOutService.test.ts` (live lift, stale rxTime, manual/geo, never aged out).
- Full Vitest suite: `success: true`, 23,156 passed, 0 failed (PG/MySQL suites skipped locally; no schema change).
- `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` clean; `npm run lint:ci` passes.

## Mesh impact
None — no packets sent, no notifications, no automation events, no timers. The lift is DB-only.

The Nodes list header on Meshtastic sources had grown to ~310px, with every control on its own line.

**Cause:** the global `.sidebar-header { display: flex }` rule in `Sidebar.css` also matches the Nodes list header, so the title and the controls sat side by side and the controls got a narrow column. Adding Group by Role, Add from URL and the age filter made it much worse.

- Filter, Group by Role and Add from URL become icon buttons (`filter`, `list`, `plus`) with tooltips and `aria-label`s. Group by Role keeps its accent-color pressed state and `aria-pressed`.

- New `src/components/NodesListHeader.module.css`; the frozen `nodes.css` is untouched. Removed the now-unused `toggleActive` class from `NodeRoleGrouping.module.css`.

title: test: give every react-i18next mock a stable t
body:
## The pattern

PR #5473 found `MeshCoreNodeNeighboursConfig.test.tsx` mocking react-i18next like this:

```ts
vi.mock('react-i18next', () => ({
  useTranslation: () => ({ t: (key, fallback) => fallback ?? key }), // new `t` per call
}));
```

Every `useTranslation()` call built a new `t`. Real react-i18next keeps `t` stable, and components list it in `useEffect` / `useCallback` deps. With the mock, each render re-ran those effects: one loaded config 373 times in 300ms, and assertions raced a "Loading…" state that flickered in and out under load. Production is fine; the tests were latent flakes.

The global mock in `src/test/setup.ts` had the same shape, as did 170 per-file mocks. Files override the global mock because it returns the bare key; most tests assert on the English fallback text.

## What changed

**Helper: `src/test/mockI18n.ts`**
- `createReactI18nextMock(t = mockT, extra = {})` builds one `useTranslation()` result per mock and returns it on every call. It also supplies `Trans` (children pass-through) and `initReactI18next`. `extra` adds or overrides exports, such as a custom `Trans`.
- `mockT` is a module-level constant: it returns the fallback (`t(key, 'Text {{n}}', { n })` or `t(key, { defaultValue, n })`), else the key, and fills `{{var}}` from the options object.
- `keyT` returns the key. `setup.ts` now uses it, so the global mock's output is unchanged.

**Sweep: 170 test files plus `setup.ts`** (175 files changed including the helper and guard)
- **122 files** now use the default `mockT`.
- **48 files** keep their own `t`, which the `vi.mock` factory creates once so it stays stable. Their output differs from `mockT`: key+JSON echoes, en.json lookups, hard-coded translation tables, `{{var}}` left unfilled, and so on.
- Deciding which files could share `mockT` was not guesswork. I ran every file once with a probe `t` that called the old function and `mockT` side by side and logged any call where the results differed. A file moved to `mockT` only if no call in its run differed, so each test sees the same strings as before. No assertions changed.
- Eight files already had a stable `t` (hoisted constant), including the files #5473 fixed. I left them alone.

**Guard: `meshmonitor-ui/stable-i18n-mock` ESLint rule**
- `scripts/eslint-rules/stable-i18n-mock.mjs` flags a `vi.mock` / `vi.doMock('react-i18next', …)` factory whose `useTranslation` returns an object with an inline `t` function. It covers test files and `src/test/**`.
- It has a node test (`stable-i18n-mock.node-test.mjs`), which `lint:ci` already runs through its `scripts/eslint-rules/*.node-test.mjs` glob.
- The repo has zero violations now, so the lint ratchet fails any new one.

## Evidence

- **Full Vitest suite** (`--reporter=json`): `success: true`, 1,638 files, 24,426 tests, 23,076 passed, 0 failed, 1,329 pending. The PG/MySQL containers were not running, so those suites skipped. This change only touches frontend test mocks.
- **`src/components` under load** (`--pool=

EmbedSettings dialog: Escape sent before the listener exists **Cause.** "+ New Embed Profile" calls the async `openCreate`, which awaits `/api/nodes/active` before `setEditingId('new')`. So the dialog commits **outside `act()`**: 1. The dialog node lands in the DOM, and `findByRole('dialog')` resolves on that mutation. 2. React runs `useDialogA11y`'s passive effects (focus the dialog, attach the document `keydown` Escape listener) in a **later task**. 3. The test fired Escape between those two steps. No listener was attached, so the Escape was lost and `waitFor` timed out with the dialog still open. The first test's `expect(document.activeElement).toBe(dialog)` raced the same effect. Under load the gap grows, so the race only shows up in busy runs. **Fix.** - New `openDialog()` helper: click the trigger, `findByRole` the dialog, then `waitFor` focus to land in it. React flushes both effects in the same pass, so focus proves the Escape listener is attached. - Awaited `userEvent.setup()` (`user.click`, `user.keyboard('{Escape}')`) in place of `fireEvent`. - Every close is awaited with `waitFor`. The hook removes its listener and restores overflow and focus on unmount, and `src/test/setup.ts` runs RTL `cleanup()` after each test, so no state leaks between tests. ## 2. MeshCore neighbours config: the test's `t` mock made the load loop **Cause.** The `react-i18next` mock built a **new `t` on every render**. The panel's config-load effect lists `t` in its deps, so every render re-ran the load, and every load's `setCfg` caused another render. A probe counted **373 config GETs in 300 ms**. The panel kept flipping between "Loading…" and the loaded controls. The enable checkbox only exists once loaded, while the poll button renders at once. So `await findByText('Poll Neighbours')` followed by a synchronous `getByRole('checkbox')` failed whenever it landed on a loading frame. **Fix.** - The mock returns one hoisted `t`, stable like the real react-i18next `t`. title: fix(frontend): only poll MeshCore neighbors for MeshCore sources
body:
## Cause

`useMeshCoreNeighbors` (`src/hooks/useMapAnalysisData.ts`) fetched `/api/sources/:id/meshcore/neighbors` for every source its caller passed. Three callers pass every source:

- `DashboardPage` in Unified view (`neighborSourceIds = sourceIds`) when "Show Neighbors" is on
- Map Analysis `MeshCoreNeighborLinksLayer` (all sources when none are picked)
- `use3DNeighborLines` (same)

The route sits behind `meshcoreRouteGuard`, which answers 404 for any source without a device-backed MeshCore manager. So each Meshtastic or MQTT source drew a 404 on every refetch. The comment in `DashboardPage` assumed "Non-MeshCore sources simply return no edges", which is not what the server does.

## Fix

- The hook now narrows `sources` to enabled, device-backed MeshCore sources, using the shared `useDashboardSources()` cache. It stays disabled when none remain, and until the source list loads. This fixes all three callers in one place.
- New helper `isDeviceMeshCoreSourceType()` in `src/utils/nodeTypeCategory.ts`, next to `isAnyMeshCoreSourceType()`. It is the client mirror of `isMeshCoreManager()`. `meshcore_mqtt` ingest sources are excluded on purpose, because the device guard refuses them too (see the `source.type` vs manager-predicate note in CLAUDE.md).
- I left the server route alone. A 404 from the guard for a non-MeshCore source is correct. The guard emits a bare `{ success:false, error }` without a `code`, like the rest of the MeshCore barrel; converting it to `fail()` is out of scope.

### Live reproduction (before the fix, dev container on main, v4.16.2-rc5)

With 8 sources (2 `meshcore`, 2 `meshtastic_tcp`, 3 MQTT, 1 `reticulum`) and "Show Neighbors" on:

- **Unified Dashboard** (`/`): each load fired the neighbors request for all 8 sources, twice (the second pass after `maxNodeAgeHours` settles and changes the query key). That gives 12 × 404 (6 non-MeshCore sources × 2) plus 4 × 200 for MC-Sandbox and MC-BLESandbox. Later refetches add more.
- **Sandbox → Automation** (`/source/<id>/automation`): zero neighbors requests over 45–60 s, both on a hard load and after an in-app click from the Unified Dashboard. The global Automation Engine page (`/automations`) also sent none in 40 s. So the Automation page does not cause these requests. The Unified Dashboard is the app's landing page, so a console that keeps its log across in-app navigation shows the dashboard's 404s while you are on Automation. That matches the reported ~13.

No mesh impact: this change only removes HTTP requests. It sends no packets and adds no timers.

## Tests

- `src/hooks/useMapAnalysisData.test.tsx`: new `useMeshCoreNeighbors` suite. No fetch for a Meshtastic source; no fetch for MQTT, `meshcore_mqtt` or disabled MeshCore sources; no fetch before the source list loads; fetches for a MeshCore source; a mixed list requests only the MeshCore id; no fetch when `enabled: false`. title: fix(ui): /settings fits a phone; geofence fields commit on blur
body:
## Summary

Two small UI fixes: the global `/settings` page scrolled sideways on a phone, and the Geofence Lat/Lng/Radius fields moved the circle on every valid keystroke.

## 1. `/settings` at 390px scrolls sideways

**Measured** (live app, 390x844 mobile emulation, read-only `evaluate_script`): `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` was **538** against a 390 viewport. I scanned every element whose right edge passed the viewport and was not inside a clipping ancestor (the section nav chips live in their own scroll strip, and Leaflet tiles are clipped by the map). Two sources remained:

| Culprit | Measurement | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| Channel Database cards (every card) | 462px wide, right edge 511, inside a 292px section | The list is `display: grid` with an implicit `auto` column. An `auto` track never shrinks below its items' min-content, and each card's row (drag handle + info + four buttons, no wrap) had a ~462px min-content. |
| Map overlay (GeoJSON/KML) layer rows | name input right edge 471, Delete button right edge **538** | One-line flex row: Visible, Public, Disable click popup, Color, name input, Delete. The input's automatic minimum is its ~214px intrinsic width. |

**Fix**, as new CSS modules (global sheets untouched), with no viewport media query, following the `AutomationFormLayout.module.css` pattern (#5462/#5463):
- `ChannelDatabaseSection.module.css`: `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)` on the list. The card row wraps, the info column is `flex: 1 1 12rem; min-width: 0`, and the buttons drop below the info when they don't fit. The `h4` name + status also wraps.
- `GeoJsonLayerManager.module.css`: both layer rows wrap. The name input gets `flex: 1 1 7.5rem; min-width: min(100%, 7.5rem)`, so on a phone it takes its own line.
  - Follow-up (5ce80b0c0): the first version used a 9rem floor. At 1280px the section is 497px and the row's other controls take 354.4px, so 9rem needed 498.4px and wrapped Delete to a second line. At 7.5rem the row fits on one line (input 143px, 22px spare). At 390px it still wraps and scrollWidth stays 390. A width-math test pins the 497px case and fails at 9rem.

With the same rules applied in the live page, scrollWidth dropped to **390** with nothing past the right edge. Desktop layout is unchanged: the rows only wrap when too narrow.

## 2. Geofence typed values

GeofenceMapEditor builds on #5467's draft-text state and `lastEmittedRef` guard, and the new constant lives in `geofenceEditorGeometry.ts`.

- **(a) Blur didn't reformat before a circle existed.** The blur handlers returned early when `circle` was null, so a lat typed before the lng stayed raw until a second focus/blur. Blur now commits and then reformats any valid field: from the circle when there is one, otherwise from its own number, formatted the same way. Invalid or empty fields keep their text and error, as before.

title: fix(repo): untrack tiles symlink and make dev tileserver opt-in
body:
## Summary

Git tracked `tiles` as a **symlink** (mode `120000`), not a directory. This PR restores `tiles/` as a real directory, blocks tracked symlinks in `lint:ci`, and makes the dev tileserver opt-in.

## History

- #1254 (579f9dfc0) added `tiles/` as a real directory with `tiles/.gitkeep`, and `.gitignore` ignored `tiles/*.mbtiles` and `tiles/*.pbf`.
- #4950 (1701bf67b) replaced it with a symlink to `../../../tiles`.
- #5162 (1cb0350c0) changed the target to `../../tiles`.

Both came from worktree setups that linked `tiles/` back to the main checkout, and the link was committed by accident.

## Effect

- A fresh clone gets a dangling `tiles` link, since `../../tiles` points outside the repo.
- The dev tileserver bind-mounts `./tiles` to `/data`, so it crash-looped with `EACCES ... open 'zurich_switzerland.mbtiles'`.

## Fix

- Remove the symlink from the index and restore `tiles/.gitkeep`, as #1254 had it.
- `.gitignore`: ignore `tiles/*` except `!tiles/.gitkeep`, so tile files never get committed.
- `.dockerignore`: exclude `tiles/` from the build context. The Dockerfile never copies it.
- **Guard:** `scripts/check-no-tracked-symlinks.mjs` runs in `npm run lint:ci` and fails if `git ls-files -s` shows any mode-`120000` entry. The repo has no other tracked symlinks.
- **Tileserver opt-in:** in `docker-compose.dev.yml` the `tileserver` service now sits behind `profiles: [tiles]`. The normal `COMPOSE_PROFILES=sqlite` deploy no longer starts it, and nothing depends on it. To start it, use `COMPOSE_PROFILES=sqlite,tiles`. No other compose file, Helm chart or devcontainer runs a tileserver.
- **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md`, `/worktree`, `/deploy` and the `docker-dev-deployer` agent now say the tileserver is opt-in, not used for testing, and that nobody should copy tiles or link `tiles/` into a worktree. The user docs on self-hosting offline tiles (`docs/features/maps.md`, `docs/configuration/custom-tile-servers.md`) stay as they are.
- `lxc/sparse-cone.txt` needs no change: `tiles/` is not needed at runtime.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck`: clean
- [x] `npm run lint:ci`: node tests pass, glyph scan passes, tracked-symlink check passes, lint ratchet OK
- [x] `npx vitest run scripts/`: 31/31 pass
- [x] `git check-ignore`: `tiles/foo.mbtiles` is ignored, `tiles/.gitkeep` is not
- [x] `docker compose config --services`: with `sqlite` only `meshmonitor-sqlite` runs; with `sqlite,tiles` it adds `tileserver`
- [x] On the parent commit, `git ls-tree` shows `120000 ... tiles`, the exact form the guard rejects

+#!/usr/bin/env node
+// Fail if git tracks any symlink (mode 120000).
+//
+// Worktree setups sometimes point `tiles` at the main checkout with a
+// symlink. Committing that link (#4950, #5162) gave every fresh clone a
+// dangling `tiles` and crash-looped the dev tileserver, which bind-mounts
+// ./tiles. The repo has no legitimate tracked symlinks, so reject them all.
+import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
+
+let out;
+try {
+  out = execFileSync('git', ['ls-files', '-s'], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 });
+} catch (err) {
+  console.warn(`Tracked-symlink check skipped: git ls-files failed (${String(err.message).split('\n')[0]}).`);
+  process.exit(0);
+}
+
+const links = out
+  .split('\n')
+  .filter(line => line.startsWith('120000 '))
+  .map(line => line.split('\t')[1]);
+
+if (links.length) {
+  console.error('Tracked symlinks found. Keep worktree links local and untracked (git rm --cached <path>):');
+  for (const link of links) console.error(`  ${link}`);
+  process.exit(1);
+}
+

title: feat(meshcore): client-side Ignore/Block for nodes and text patterns (#5408)
body:
Closes #5408

MeshCore firmware has no block or mute, so MeshMonitor now filters in the client. Spec with the maintainer's decisions: `docs/internal/dev-notes/MESHCORE_IGNORE_BLOCK_SPEC.md`.

## What it does
**Two per-source lists (migration 182, all three backends):**
- `meshcore_ignored_nodes`, keyed by `(sourceId, publicKey)`. Independent of `meshcore_nodes`, so pruning a node can't strand an entry (the #1796 deadlock).
- `meshcore_message_filters`: text rules. Match type is exact, wildcard (`*`, `?`, anchored) or regex (RE2; refused patterns and anything over 256 chars get a 400 at save). Each rule picks sender name, body, or both, and can be case-sensitive.

**Modes (block wins when both match):**
- **Ignore:** stored, but no notification, automation, auto-ack, auto-responder, forwarding or Virtual Node relay, and not counted as unread. Runs of ignored messages collapse into an expandable `N ignored messages` row. The flag is computed at read time, so removing an entry shows them normally again.
- **Block:** dropped on receipt. Only the entry's hit counter moves.
- Nodes on either list are hidden from the node list, Node Details and the map.

**Matching:**
- DMs and room posts match by public key (full key or 6-byte prefix; room posts by author).
- Channel messages match the sender name against the node's advert name, case-insensitive. Names can be spoofed; the Settings UI says so.
- Lists and compiled rules are cached per source and reloaded on every write. They load before a source connects.
- Hit counts batch-flush every 30 s and on shutdown.

**UI:**
- Ignore / Block / Remove controls under the contact detail panel.
- Two new sections in the MeshCore source's Settings: nodes and text rules, each showing hits and last hit.

## Decisions beyond the spec (conservative)
1. **Permissions:** node entries use `nodes` read/write and rules use `messages` (there is no MeshCore resource).
2. **Room posts:** a blocked post still advances the room's last-post time, so the next sync doesn't pull it again.
3. **MQTT adverts** don't refresh an entry's name snapshot, because they can be forged.
4. **MQTT ingest page:** drops ignored messages rather than collapsing them. It has no Settings screen of its own.
5. **Fail-open:** if loading a source's lists fails, messages pass until the retry (logged, retried at most every 30 s).

## Mesh impact
Sends no packets. It reduces airtime: ignored and blocked messages no longer trigger auto-ack or auto-responder replies. The only timer is the hit-count flush, and it touches only the database.

## Tests
- Classifier, repository (incl. `*.perSource.test.ts`), route permissions via `createRouteTestApp`, ingest (block not persisted; ignore stored but no auto-ack/automation/VN relay), read-time annotation, the collapsed-row component, and the Settings sections.
- Full Vitest with the PG and MySQL containers up: 24,155 passed, 0 failed, 0 failed suites. The migration-182 and repository PG/MySQL suites ran rather than ski

--- docs/internal/dev-notes/MESHCORE_IGNORE_BLOCK_SPEC.md (+112/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+# MeshCore Ignore / Block (#5408) — spec
+
+MeshCore firmware has no block or mute, so the whole policy lives in
+MeshMonitor. Two kinds of entry, both **per-source**, both with two modes.
+
+## Decisions (from the maintainer, 2026-09-28)
+
+| Question | Decision |
+|---|---|
+| Does a node entry filter channel messages? | **Yes**, by matching the channel sender name to the node's advert name (case-insensitive). Spoofable and collision-prone; the UI says so. |
+| Scope | **Per-source** for both node entries and text rules. |
+| Blocked-message visibility | **Hit counter + last-hit time** per entry. No content kept. |
+| Rule fields | **Selectable per rule**: sender name, body, or both (default both). |
+
+## Modes
+
+- **Ignore** — the message is stored. It fires no notification, automation,
+  auto-ack or auto-responder, and does not count as unread. The channel/DM view
+  collapses a run of consecutive ignored messages into one
+  `N ignored messages` row; clicking it expands them. Removing the entry makes
+  them render normally again, so the ignored state is **computed at read time
+  from the current lists, never stored on the message row**.
+- **Block** — the message is discarded on receipt: not stored, not emitted, no
+  automation, no auto-ack/auto-responder. Only the entry's hit counter moves.
+- **Both** — an ignored or blocked node is hidden from the MeshCore node list,
+  the Node Details view and the map. Adverts still update its `meshcore_nodes`
+  row (so un-ignoring shows current data); only display is suppressed.
+
+Block wins over ignore when a message matches entries of both modes.
+
+## Data (migration 182, all three backends)
+
+`meshcore_ignored_nodes` — PK `(sourceId, publicKey)`
+- `sourceId`, `publicKey` (64-hex), `name` (advert-name snapshot at ignore
+  time, refreshed when a newer name is seen; used for channel matching and so
+  the Settings list stays readable after the node row is pruned — the #1796
+  lesson: this table is the authority, independent of `meshcore_nodes`)
+- `mode` `'ignore' | 'block'`, `createdAt` (ms), `createdBy` (user id, nullable)
+- `hitCount` (int, default 0), `lastHitAt` (ms, nullable)
+
+`meshcore_message_filters` — PK `id`
+- `id`, `sourceId`, `mode` `'ignore' | 'block'`
+- `matchType` `'exact' | 'wildcard' | 'regex'`, `pattern`, `caseSensitive`
+  (bool, default false), `fields` `'name' | 'body' | 'both'` (default `'both'`)
+- `enabled` (bool, default true), `createdAt`, `createdBy`,
+  `hitCount`, `lastHitAt`
+
+Every query scopes by `sourceId`. Add a `*.perSource.test.ts`.
+
+## Matching (server; one shared module)
+
+`src/server/services/meshcoreMessageFilter.ts` exposes
+`classifyMeshCoreMessage(sourceId, { fromPublicKey, fromName, text, kind })`
+→ `{ action: 'allow' | 'ignore' | 'block', entryKind, entryId }`.
+
+- **Node entry, DM / room post:** match by public key. DMs carry a 6-byte
+  prefix; resolve to the full key the same way ingest already does, and also
+  accept a prefix match against the stored key.
+- **Node entry, channel message:** match `fromName` (parsed from `"Name: body"`)
+  to the entry's `name` or the contact's current advert name,
+  case-insensitive, trimmed.
+- **Text rule:** `exact` = whole-field equality; `wildcard` = `*` any run,
+  `?` one char, everything else literal, anchored at both ends; `regex` =
+  compiled with `compileUserRegex` (RE2, `src/utils/safeRegex.ts`) — reject
+  patterns RE2 refuses **at save time** with a 400. Cap pattern length (256).
+  Checked against the chosen field(s).
+- Rules and node entries are cached in memory per source (like
+  `ignoredNodes.isIgnoredCached`) and the cache is invalidated on every write.
+  Compile each rule once, not per message.
+- Hit counts: increment in memory and flush to the DB in a batch at most every
+  30 s and on shutdown. Losing a few counts on a crash is acceptable.
+
+## Where it plugs in
+
+- Ingest: `meshcoreManager.handleBridgeEvent` — `contact_message`,
+  `channel_message`, `room_message`, before `addMessage` — and the MeshCore MQTT
+  manager's message path (`meshcoreMqttManager.ts`). Block → return early.
+  Ignore → store, but skip `emitMeshCoreMessage`-driven notifications,
+  automation events, auto-ack and auto-responder. The socket event still goes
+  out, flagged `filtered: 'ignore'`, so an open view can collapse it.
+- Read: message list endpoints annotate each message with
+  `filtered: 'ignore'` when it currently matches an ignore entry. Unread counts
+  exclude ignored messages.
+- Node list / map / Node Details: exclude nodes with an entry (server-side where
+  the list is built, or client-side from the entry list — pick one place and
+  cover all three views).
+
+## API (under the existing MeshCore routes, per-source)
+
+- `GET/POST/DELETE /api/sources/:id/meshcore/ignored-nodes[/:publicKey]`
+- `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/sources/:id/meshcore/message-filters[/:id]`
+- Read needs MeshCore read permission on the source; writes need MeshCore
+  write. Use `ok()` / `fail()`. Route tests use `createRouteTestApp()`.
+
+## UI
+
+- Node Details (`MeshCoreContactDetailPanel`): **Ignore** and **Block**
+  buttons (confirm for Block), or **Remove from ignore/block list** when the
+  node already has an entry.
+- Settings, MeshCore source: two sections — the node list (name, key prefix,
+  mode, hits, last hit, delete) and the text rules (add/edit/delete, enable
+  toggle, match type, fields, case, mode, hits, last hit). Show the RE2 error
+  inline on save. Note beside channel matching that names can be spoofed.
+- Channel and DM streams (`MeshCoreMessageStream`): collapse consecutive
+  `filtered: 'ignore'` messages into an `N ignored messages` row that expands on
+  click. Icons via `UiIcon`; styles in a CSS module.
+
+## Mesh impact
+
+Sends no packets. It *reduces* traffic: ignored/blocked messages no longer
+trigger auto-ack or auto-responder replies. No timer re-arms on save; the only
+timer is the hit-count flush, which touches only the DB.

title: fix(ui): /settings nav offset, embed modal a11y, en-US locale 404, heap telemetry 401
body:
Fixes three older UI and console issues. There is no linked issue.

## 1. /settings: content scrolls above the sticky section nav

**Cause.** `.section-nav` is `position: sticky; top: var(--app-header-height)`. Inside the app shell, `useAppHeaderHeightVar` writes the measured header height to that variable. The standalone `/settings` page mounts outside the shell, so it has no header and the hook never runs. The variable fell back to the `:root` default (60px), and page content scrolled through the empty 60px band above the nav. Confirmed on the live app: no `.app-header`, nav `top` computed to `60px`.

**Fix.** A new `GlobalSettingsPage.module.css` `.page` wrapper sets `--app-header-height: 0px` for the page's own subtree. It replaces the inline wrapper style. Pages inside the app shell never render this wrapper, so their offset is unchanged. SectionNav's click-scroll offset from #5455 reads the nav's computed `top`, so it now sees 0 here and still keeps the `WINDOW_SCROLL_OFFSET` floor. SectionNav itself is untouched.

## 2. Create Embed Profile modal: Escape ignored, unlabelled ×

**Cause.** Both Embed settings modals (create/edit profile and embed code) were plain divs. They had no key handling, no dialog role, and a bare `×` close button. Confirmed on the live app: Escape left the modal open, `role` was null, the close button had no `aria-label`, and focus stayed on `<body>`.

**Fix.** A small `EmbedDialogContent` wraps the modal box with the existing `useDialogA11y` hook. It gives `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal` and `aria-labelledby` (the `<h2>`), Escape-to-close, focus in on open and back to the trigger on close, and a Tab trap. The close button now uses `aria-label={t('common.close')}` (an existing en.json key) and `<UiIcon name="close">` in place of the `×` glyph. `closeModal`/`closeCodeModal` are `useCallback`s, so the hook's Escape listener does not re-bind on each render. The JSX body keeps its indentation, which keeps the merge with #5467's `embed-map-picker` hunk clean.

## 3a. `GET /locales/en-US.json` 404

**Cause.** i18next used `load: 'currentOnly'` with no `supportedLngs`. A browser that reports `en-US` made it request `/locales/en-US.json`, which does not exist, before it fell back to `en`. Confirmed on the live app: `en-US.json [404]`, then `en.json`.

**Fix.** Two init options in `src/config/i18n.ts`:

- `supportedLngs: AVAILABLE_LANGUAGES.map(l => l.code)`. i18next now maps a regional code to its base language (`en-US` → `en`, `de-AT` → `de`), and a language we don't ship falls back to `en` with no 404.
- `detection.convertDetectedLanguage`, backed by a new `src/config/languageTag.ts`. Our locale files use underscore codes (`zh_Hans`) while browsers report hyphenated tags, and i18next alone turned `zh-CN` into `zh`, matched nothing, and served English. The converter maps:
  - `zh-CN`, `zh-SG`, `zh-Hans`, `zh-Hans-CN`, bare `zh` → `zh_Hans`
  - `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, `zh-MO`, `zh-Hant`, `zh-Hant-TW` → `zh_Hant`
  - any hyphenated t
